# dilla-web-1 — browser core, client core and the first usable web slice Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship the first usable slice of the dilla web client: in one browser tab a person signs up with an invite (browser-rooted identity), or comes back and re-establishes the session from the device key stored in that browser, sees their communities and channels, and reads and sends text in an end-to-end encrypted channel against a real dillad that serves the built client from its own origin. To get there this plan: carries the MLS-authenticated sender out of `dilla-core` (C22); makes the browser store own one connection shared by MLS and typed app tables (C2) and puts the per-group ordered processing with atomic persistence in Rust (C1); exposes it through a wasm-bindgen `CoreHandle` built with a size profile (C16); adds to dillad the discovery reads the slice needs (C11, F13), the gateway registry reseed (C12) and same-origin SPA serving from `embed.FS` with CSP, cache headers and a content manifest (C9); creates `@dilla/client-core` (deterministic CBOR codec C20, HTTP client with the error and retry vocabulary, account and session lifecycle with the KEK ruling C7, gateway client without resume C19, the TypeScript half of sync, a single-tab leader worker C5) and `@dilla/web` (the shell and the minimum screens on new `@dilla/ui` components); and proves it with a browser e2e against the test host and a native testkit counterparty in a new CI job (C18).

**Architecture:** One dedicated worker per tab owns everything secret and everything stateful: the device KEK (random, wrapped by a non-extractable WebCrypto key in IndexedDB), the encrypted OPFS database, the Rust core (`CoreHandle`), the session token and the single gateway connection. Inside the worker the split is strict: **Rust decides and persists, TypeScript transports.** Rust takes delivery-service rows exactly as they came off the wire, applies handshakes and messages of a group in sequence order, and writes the MLS state change, the message row and the group cursor in one SQLite transaction; it returns ready-to-send request bodies for everything that must go back out. TypeScript fetches, paces, retries, keeps timers and the WebSocket, and never parses an MLS object. The page is a renderer: it receives immutable state slices from the worker, calls a small command surface, and holds no key, no token and no ciphertext. dillad stays a single binary that now also serves the built client from its own origin, so the browser needs no CORS and the gateway's same-host Origin rule already admits it. The tab that holds the Web Lock is the only tab that runs a core; a second tab says so and waits (followers arrive in web-2).

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.98.1, `dilla-core` on OpenMLS 0.9.0 with `rusqlite` 0.40.2 (native SQLCipher; wasm `sqlite-wasm-rs` 0.5.5 with `sqlite3mc`, `sqlite-wasm-vfs` 0.2.0 `opfs-sahpool`), `aes-gcm` 0.10.3, `hkdf` 0.13, compiled to `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with wasm-bindgen 0.2.128 / wasm-pack 0.15.0 under a new `wasm-release` profile (`opt-level = "z"`, `strip = true`); Go 1.27.0 (`github.com/jonasthim/dilla`), stdlib `http.ServeMux`, `embed`, sqlc v1.31.1; TypeScript 5.9.3, React 19.3.0, Vite 7.3.6 with `@vitejs/plugin-react` 4.7.0, vitest 3.2.7, Storybook 9.1.20, ESLint 9 with `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` and `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`; Playwright 1.63.0 (Chromium 153.0.8010.12, Firefox 155.0, WebKit 26.6); the Rust `dilla-testkit` as the native counterparty in every browser test.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-dilla-design.md` — the design section (L166–330: tokens, components, surfaces, accessibility), Clients (L420–445, L510–524), Identity (L468–490), Error handling and failure modes (L600–637), Testing and verification strategy (L637–653), the roadmap (L655–670) and sub-project 5 (L709) — with `docs/design/brief.md` as the visual authority and `protocol/02-delivery-service.md`, `protocol/03-identity.md`, `protocol/06-backup-archive.md`, `protocol/09-http-api.md` and `protocol/07-versioning.md` amended by the tasks named in "Protocol and spec edits in this plan". The rulings of the wave are `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-05-dilla-web/facts/rulings.md` (C1–C24 adopted; F1–F18 provisional on the recommended options). Where a verified fact (`facts/interfaces.md`, `facts/deviations.md`, `facts/critic.md`, `facts/gap-G1…G8.md`, the eight `facts-*.md`) disagrees with the spec, **the fact wins**; where a facts file and the code disagree, **the code wins** and the task says so.

- `@dilla/client-core` and `@dilla/web`: `"license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later"`, `"private": true`, `"type": "module"` in `package.json`; no LICENSE file in the package (the root `LICENSE` covers them, as for `@dilla/ui` and `@dilla/media`).

**Copy rules (F10) and the lint that enforces them**
- Encryption vocabulary — the words `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs` forbids (`kanal(s)`, `team(s)`, `PMs`, `E2E(E)`, `end-to-end`, `encrypted`, `encryption`, `SRTP`, `X3DH`, `Signal Protocol`, `SQLCipher`, `AES-NNN`, `MLS`) — appears in no string literal and no JSX text of `packages/ui/src`, `packages/web/src` or `packages/client-core/src`. Task 12 extends the lint to the two new roots (L-CI-03); `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx` and `*.stories.tsx` files are scanned too, so test names and story titles are written without those words.
- The only exemption is the allow-listed module `packages/web/src/strings/privacy.ts` (Settings → Privacy, channel-mode settings, the report dialog). **web-1 has none of those surfaces, so the file does not exist in this plan**; the lint's allow-list names the path so web-2 can add it without touching the lint.
- Every user-visible string of `@dilla/web` lives in `packages/web/src/strings/en.ts` (L-TS-11) and is passed to `@dilla/ui` components as props; `@dilla/ui` components added by this plan hard-code no English except `aria-label` defaults that the caller can override (the existing `Dialog` gains `closeLabel`, L-UI). Copy is the tool's tone: lower-case labels in the chrome — the shell's rail, channel list, log, composer, status bar and row actions — and sentence case on the ceremony, splash and dialog surfaces (onboarding, boot splashes, the join and reset dialogs), which is what the Mesh onboarding reference does (`docs/design/reference/mesh-handoff/onboarding.jsx:149, 235, 298, 508`); no exclamation marks, no "secure", "safe", "protected" or a lock glyph anywhere (the private-channel lock of `ChannelRow` is the one existing exception and is not reused).
- No string promises what web-1 cannot do. In particular no string says or implies that the recovery key restores an account today (L-COPY-01 carries the exact sentences).
- A client never switches on a server `detail` text (protocol/02 "a client MUST NOT parse it"): every mapping from a refusal to a string is by `code` and HTTP `status` (L-TS-09). A unit test in `packages/web` greps `packages/web/src` and `packages/client-core/src` for `.detail ===`, `.detail.startsWith(` and `.detail.includes(` and fails on any match outside a `*.test.ts(x)` file.
- Exact strings: the onboarding and recovery-key strings are fixed once, in **L-COPY-01** of the ledger; `docs/design/flows/` (task 19), the stories of task 20, `en.ts` (task 23) and the e2e (task 25) quote that table and none of them changes a key or a text. The `boot.*` strings are fixed by task 22 and the `shell.*`, `join.*` and `dialog.*` strings by task 24; a drafter of a UI task writes every string out.

**Accessibility rules (WCAG 2.2 AA)**
- Tokens only: every colour, size, radius, duration and font comes from `@dilla/design-tokens` CSS variables; no hex colour, no `px` font size, no new z-index or breakpoint constant outside `packages/ui/src/styles/base.css`. All three themes (`mesh`, `light`, `high-contrast`) and reduced motion must render every new component.
- Every new `@dilla/ui` component ships: a story per state; a unit test with `vitest-axe`; passes the Storybook test-runner's axe gate (`critical` and `serious`) and its Tab focus-ring check; an accessible name and role stated in its task; a pointer target of at least 24×24 CSS px (2.5.8; `Button size="sm"` at 22px is not used for new controls).
- Keyboard map of the web-1 shell (fixed here; tasks 21 and 24 implement and test it). Focus order: skip link → community rail → channel list → channel header → message log → composer → status bar. Rail and channel list are single tab stops with roving focus (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`, `Home`/`End`, `Enter`/`Space` activates). `Alt+ArrowUp`/`Alt+ArrowDown` selects the previous/next channel from anywhere. In the composer `Enter` sends, `Shift+Enter` inserts a newline, and neither fires while `event.isComposing` is true (IME). `Escape` in the log or a dialog returns focus to the composer. There are **no single-character shortcuts** (2.1.4). The message log is `role="log"` with an accessible name and `aria-live="polite"`; it never steals focus.
- Forms: every field has a visible label, errors are text bound with `aria-describedby` and announced through `role="alert"`; paste is allowed in every field (3.3.8); the recovery key is selectable text with no copy button (protocol/03, F2). Each onboarding step and each dialog is one `<form noValidate>` whose forward button is `type="submit"`, so `Enter` in a field advances; a submit that leaves a field in error moves focus to the first such field.
- A control that is blocked for a reason the person must be able to hear stays focusable: it carries `aria-disabled="true"` (and `readOnly` for a text control), never the `disabled` attribute, with the reason as its description (the `Composer`, L-UI-13). Tests assert `aria-disabled`; jest-dom's `toBeDisabled()` reads only the native attribute.
- Print (F2 allows printing the recovery key): the print rules use system colours (`CanvasText` on `Canvas`), never a theme token, because browsers do not print backgrounds and the default theme's text is near-white (L-UI-06).
- The Storybook test-runner enables axe's `target-size` rule (off by default in axe-core 4.13) for the stories this plan adds (titles under `Form/`, `Ceremony/`, `Shell/`, `Conversation/`; task 20 edits `packages/ui/.storybook/test-runner.ts`); the existing primitives keep today's rule set, and the composed `Screens/` stories are covered by the e2e's own `target-size` run on the real pages.
- The e2e (task 25) runs axe on every page state it reaches with zero `serious`/`critical` violations and with the `target-size` rule enabled, and drives one full flow with the keyboard only.
- F16 artefacts: tasks 20, 21, 23 and 24 run `packages/ui/scripts/shoot-stories.mjs` (L-UI-15) and leave PNGs of every new story in all three themes under `target/ui-screens/web-1/` (ignored by git); the supervisor attaches them to the task's review and task 26 uploads them from CI as the artifact `ui-screens`.

**Testing**
- TDD in every implementation task: the failing test first, its run and the recorded failure, then the implementation, then the passing run, then the one commit.
- **A test must be able to fail (lesson a).** For each security- or correctness-critical assertion the task names the mutation that turns it red and has one step that applies the mutation, shows the red run, and reverts it. The task index names the mutation for every task that has one.
- The module-wide Go command is pinned and never narrowed in a task's final verification: `/home/thim/.local/go/bin/go -C /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol test -race -shuffle=on -timeout 15m ./...`. A Go test that cannot run under the race detector is listed in `NON_RACE_STEP` of `scripts/check-ci-workflow.mjs` and in the `go` job's non-race step in the same task (no task in this plan is expected to add one).
- Rust final verification mirrors the `rust-native` and `rust-wasm-node` jobs: `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo fmt --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml --all --check`, `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo clippy --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked`; and for every task that touches `core/` also `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml -p dilla-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked --features vectors` and `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml -p dilla-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`. The native clippy never compiles the wasm-only modules of `dilla-core-wasm` (`store.rs`, `probe.rs`, `facade.rs`), so tasks 3 and 7 also run `/home/thim/.cargo/bin/cargo clippy --manifest-path /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/Cargo.toml -p dilla-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib --locked -- -D warnings` and end with it clean (task 3 fixes whatever it reports in the existing `store.rs`, `probe.rs` and `lib.rs`, applying each lint's own suggestion, and lists a file it had to touch in its commit); task 26 adds the same line to the `rust-wasm-node` job.
- TypeScript final verification: `npm --prefix /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol test` (doc, brief, copy and CI checkers, lint from task 12 on, and every workspace's unit tests). Unit tests of `@dilla/client-core` and `@dilla/web` never load the wasm: they run against the `CorePort` interface (L-TS-03) with two in-memory doubles, `FakeCore` for the account half (task 15) and `ModelCore` for the group half (task 16). `ModelCore` is held to the Rust core by the parity fixture of L-CORE-10: the same cases are asserted natively in task 6 and replayed through the model in task 16. The real wasm is exercised only in browsers (tasks 3, 7, 18, 25), where OPFS exists.
- Tests assert behaviour against the real thing: real SQLite for the Rust client engine (native `cargo test`, in-memory SQLCipher connection, two or three `ClientCore`s exchanging the bodies they produce); the real dillad for every route (the `internal/api` and `internal/dillad` test harnesses); real browsers for every claim about a browser; the real test host and a native testkit peer for every claim about the client talking to a server.
- **Browser thresholds (lesson c).** The CI runner has 4 vCPUs and is 3–5× slower than the dev machine. A browser test waits for a state (`expect.poll`, `locator.waitFor`, a worker state slice), never for a duration; every wait has an explicit timeout of at least 30 s locally and 90 s when `process.env.CI === 'true'`; no assertion is an upper bound on elapsed time. `workers: 1`, `retries: 0`, `fullyParallel: false`. So that a bare `expect(locator)…` cannot fall back to Playwright's 5 s default, both new configs set `expect: { timeout: process.env.CI === 'true' ? 90_000 : 30_000 }`, and a new spec on the existing spike config passes the timeout explicitly on every web-first assertion. A job budget is taken from a measurement, not asserted: task 25 records the local wall time of the core-worker suite and of the web suite, and task 26 sets `browser-web`'s `timeout-minutes` from it (CI table below).
- **Audio (lesson d).** web-1 has no audio: no task starts `scripts/ci-audio-server.sh` and no browser project sets media prefs.
- CI is fail-closed: no `|| true`, no `continue-on-error`, no `if: always()` on a gate step; every `upload-artifact` sets `if-no-files-found: error`; a job that downloads an artifact carries `needs:` on the job that uploads it.

**Execution environment**
- The implementer (Codex under a supervisor) works in a sandbox that has network access and can launch Chromium and Firefox. It cannot write the git directory: **the supervisor makes every commit.** The supervisor re-runs every Firefox leg itself before committing.
- `TMPDIR` is `/home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol/.superpowers/tmp`. That path is too long for Chromium's socket files, so browser profile directories are never under it: persistent Playwright contexts use `/tmp/dw/<project>-<worker>` (created and removed by the fixture), and the test host's data directory is `/tmp/dw/host-<port>`.
- Fixed ports, one owner each. Existing: 5178 (spike page; tasks 3 and 7 extend that suite), 6006 (Storybook test-runner), 8443/8444 and 5179 and 7880/7882 (media suite; untouched). New: **8453/8454** test host public/control for the core-worker suite (task 18); **8463/8464** test host public/control for the web suite (task 25); **6016**, **6017**, **6018**, **6019** the screenshot script's static server in tasks 20, 21, 23, 24. Go tests bind port 0. Two ports are opened only by a person or an optional leg, never by a gate: **5432** (task 8's optional local Postgres container) and **5180** (the `dev` script of `@dilla/web`, a Vite server that proxies to a test host for a manual developer loop; untested). The demo of task 25 (`demo:web`) reuses 8463/8464 and therefore never runs beside the web suite. No other task opens a listening port.
- WebKit cannot launch on the dev host (missing `libicu74`), and no container route works for the suites of this plan (the Playwright image has no Go toolchain for the global setup, the host-built testkit binary does not start on its older glibc, and a persistent context cannot be launched against a remote browser). **WebKit is gated in CI only**: the spike matrix in `browser-spike`, the web suite's two WebKit specs in `browser-web`. No task has a local WebKit step.

**Protocol-edit rules**
- Every edit to a `protocol/*.md` document gets its `protocol/07-versioning.md` change-table row in the same task and the same commit, and is listed in "Protocol and spec edits in this plan". No version axis is bumped: every edit is additive to a structure no shipped client reads, or documents existing behaviour (07 precedent: "no client has shipped: no version bump").
- `npm run check:docs` (part of the root `npm test`) must stay green after every protocol edit.

**Commits**
- One commit per task, conventional subject (`feat(core): …`, `feat(wasm): …`, `feat(api): …`, `feat(client-core): …`, `feat(ui): …`, `feat(web): …`, `test(e2e): …`, `ci: …`, `docs(design): …`), made by the supervisor in one command line: `git -C /home/thim/Repositories/dilla/.claude/worktrees/sdd-dilla-protocol commit -s -m "<subject>" -m "<body>" --trailer "Co-Authored-By: Codex <noreply@openai.com>" --trailer "Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XLFud8eoDaqf8uiZq5wjuP"`. The trailer block of every commit is therefore these two lines followed by the `Signed-off-by` that `-s` adds, which is the layout of the commits on main (`1e77667`). A `-m` value never spans two lines, and the two trailers are never passed as `-m` paragraphs (they would not form one trailer block).
- Task 26 is the one task that may end in more than one commit: a red first CI run is fixed by further commits (`fix(ci): …`, or `fix(<scope>): …` for product code) inside the task. The workflow runs on `pull_request` only, so task 26 opens the plan's PR as a draft when it does not exist yet; the green run's id goes into the PR description and `progress.md`, not into another commit.

## File structure

**Package layout and why.** The spec names two deliverables, `dilla-client-core` and `dilla-web`, and says the web client is "bundled unchanged into `dilla-desktop`" (L424). The repository convention (`interfaces.md` A9) is `@dilla/<name>` workspaces under `packages/*`, TypeScript source exports, no build step for libraries. So: `packages/client-core` (`@dilla/client-core`, the library Electron will reuse), `packages/web` (`@dilla/web`, the Vite application whose `dist/` dillad embeds) and `packages/core-wasm` (`@dilla/core-wasm`, a two-file wrapper that gives the wasm-pack output a package name so neither client package reaches into `packages/media/wasm` by relative path). There is no `apps/` directory: the root workspace glob is `packages/*` and a second glob would be the only reason to add one. All presentational components land in `packages/ui` (one Storybook, one axe gate); `packages/web` contains wiring, strings and screens composed from them, and has no stories of its own.

## Interface ledger

The single source of truth for every interface that crosses a task boundary. A task text may add private helpers; it may not change a name, a type, a field order, a constant or an error code written here. If a drafter finds the code makes an entry impossible, the task says so in a "Ledger conflict" note at its top and the reviewer rules; the drafter does not silently adapt.

**Adjudicated 2026-10-05.** The drafters' `ARCH-ISSUE` notes and the four reviews were ruled on in `adjudication.md`; every accepted correction that crosses a task boundary is written into the entries below, which now supersede any task text that still says otherwise. The fix orders were applied and verified on 2026-10-05; no `ARCH-ISSUE:` marker remains in a task file, and a task's "Settled by the plan head" note is history, not an open question.

Conventions used below. `b16`, `b32`, `b64` are CBOR byte strings of exactly that many bytes; `uint` is a CBOR unsigned integer (a Rust `u64` unless a narrower range is stated); `tstr` is UTF-8 text; `x|null` is the value or CBOR `null`. Every structured value that crosses the Rust/TypeScript boundary is one deterministic CBOR item of the dilla subset (`interfaces.md` A1.2), encoded with `dilla_core::cbor::Encoder` on the Rust side and L-TS-01 on the TypeScript side. An identifier ending in `_body` is **the exact HTTP request body** of the named route; an argument documented as "the 200 body of …" is the response bytes exactly as received. Timestamps are unix seconds.

### L-CORE — `dilla-core`

**L-CORE-01 `ReceivedApplication`** (`core/dilla-core/src/mls/group.rs`; C22, G8)

```rust
pub struct ReceivedApplication {             // Debug is implemented by hand, see below
    pub envelope: Envelope,
    pub sender_leaf: u32,
    pub sender: crate::identity::CredentialIdentity,
    pub epoch: u64,
}
pub enum DillaProcessed {
    Application(Box<ReceivedApplication>),   // was Application(Envelope)
    Proposal(Box<QueuedProposal>), ExternalJoinProposal(Box<QueuedProposal>),
    StagedCommit(Box<StagedCommit>), OwnPendingCommit, OwnPrivateMessage,
}
```

`ReceivedApplication` implements `Debug` by hand and prints four fields only: `sender_leaf`, `sender_device` (the credential's device id), `epoch` and `msg_id`. (`Envelope` has its own redacting `Debug`, `envelope/mod.rs:184-198`, which still prints attachment and preview metadata; the hand-written impl keeps the output to routing facts, and a test asserts that no body and no credential material is printed.) In `process_message`'s `ApplicationMessage` arm, in this order: the sender must be `Sender::Member(leaf)` else `MlsError::OpenMls("application message from a non-member")`; the credential must convert to `BasicCredential` and decode as `CredentialIdentity`, any failure is `MlsError::Protocol(ProtocolError::Credential)`; then the existing `Envelope::decode` and `verify_commitment`. `epoch` is the processed message's epoch, read before `into_content()`. Call sites to update: `core/dilla-core/tests/mls_roundtrip.rs:169`, `testkit/src/client.rs:823`. The testkit's `sync` refuses a message whose MLS sender is not the uploader with the error text, exactly, `message seq <n> in group <group hex>: the MLS sender <device hex> is not the uploader <device hex>` (task 17's harness test matches on `is not the uploader`).

**L-CORE-02 `ClientError`** (`src/client/error.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ClientError { pub code: &'static str, pub detail: String }
impl core::fmt::Display for ClientError { /* "<code>" when detail is empty, else "<code>: <detail>" */ }
impl std::error::Error for ClientError {}
```

| code | raised for | detail |
|---|---|---|
| any `ProtocolError::code()` (`E_BINDING`, `E_CREDENTIAL`, `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`, …) | `MlsError::Protocol(e)` or a direct `ProtocolError` | empty |
| `E_CORE_INPUT` | an argument that is not the documented CBOR shape, a wrong length, `limit` out of range, info and tree of different epochs (detail `info_body and tree_body disagree`); since the hardening (L-CORE-07): a GroupInfo of another group id (detail `GroupInfo group id does not match`), a GroupInfo that would rejoin at or below an epoch this device has held (detail `GroupInfo would rejoin at or below an epoch this device has held`), and the same refusal of a Welcome, which reaches the caller as outcome 2 with reason `E_CORE_INPUT` | which argument and why; never the bytes |
| `E_CORE_STATE` | a call that is invalid now: `signup_begin` with an identity or a pending signup; a phase-1-only call (`signup_request`, `signup_complete`, `signup_reset`) in phase 0 (detail `no signup is pending`) or phase 2 (detail `the identity is complete`); `signup_reset` while a `session` record exists (detail `the account is registered`); `send_encrypt` while another row of the group is in flight (detail `a message of this group is in flight`), while the group has a queued proposal (detail `proposals are pending`) or a pending commit (detail `a commit is pending`); `commit_build` with a pending commit; any group call on a group whose state forbids it; `ClientCore::open` on a newer app schema; since the hardening: a join over a row bound to another channel (detail `group is bound to another channel`), a stored MLS group that does not match its row (detail `the stored group does not match its row; resync the group`), `send_confirm` at a seq that holds another row (detail `message seq exists`; the outbox row is failed first, L-CORE-09) | the state found. A caller switches on the code only, never on the detail |
| `E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY` | a call that needs phase 2, or, for `session_sign` and `session_store`, phase ≥ 1. `identity`, `session`, `session_clear`, `sealed_objects` and `unload` answer in every phase | empty |
| `E_CORE_NOT_FOUND` | unknown `group_id` or `msg_id` | empty |
| `E_CORE_MLS` | `MlsError::OpenMls(s)` | `s` (an OpenMLS `Debug` string; it carries no key material) |
| `E_CORE_STORAGE` | `MlsError::Storage`, `MlsError::Tx(s)`, `StorageError`, a `TxError` other than `RolledBack` | the error's `Display`; for `MlsError::Tx(s)` the detail is `s` itself (pre-flight ruling, task 4); never SQL text that carries a parameter |
| `E_CORE_RELOAD` | `MlsError::NeedsReload` that persists after `ClientCore` has dropped and reloaded the group once and retried | empty |

No `ClientError` detail and no `Debug` output ever contains a private key, `k_f`, a session token, the recovery key or a message body. The table is implemented by `From` impls of `ClientError` for `ProtocolError`, `MlsError`, `StorageError` and `TxError<ClientError>` (additive, public). `src/client/mod.rs` has `pub use error::ClientError;`, so both types are reachable as `dilla_core::client::{ClientCore, ClientError}`. `TxError`, `StorageError` and `MlsError` are `#[non_exhaustive]`: a `match` on them in an integration test (a separate crate) needs a wildcard arm.

**L-CORE-03 `DillaStorage::unit`** (`src/mls/tx.rs`)

```rust
pub struct UnitScope<'a> { /* private: &'a DillaStorage */ }
impl UnitScope<'_> {
    /// Runs `f` on the connection inside the open unit. Must not be called from inside a
    /// `transaction()` closure.
    pub fn with_conn<T>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&rusqlite::Connection) -> Result<T, StorageError>)
        -> Result<T, StorageError>;
}
impl DillaStorage {
    pub fn unit<T, E: From<StorageError> + core::fmt::Debug>(
        &self, f: impl FnOnce(&UnitScope<'_>) -> Result<T, E>,
    ) -> Result<T, TxError<E>>;
}
```

Semantics. `unit` takes the same single slot `transaction` takes (`try_enter_tx`; a second `unit` or a `transaction` started outside it while it is open is `TxError::AlreadyOpen`), runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, calls `f`, then `COMMIT` on `Ok` and `ROLLBACK` on `Err` with the same `TxGuard` panic safety and the same `Begin`/`Commit`/`RolledBack`/`RollbackFailed` mapping as `transaction`. **While a unit is open, a `transaction()` call on the same storage does not fail: it runs its closure between `SAVEPOINT dilla_tx` and `RELEASE dilla_tx`, and on error runs `ROLLBACK TO dilla_tx` then `RELEASE dilla_tx` and returns `TxError::RolledBack(cause)`**; the unit stays open and its caller decides. A `transaction()` nested in a `transaction()` is still `AlreadyOpen`. `transaction` outside a unit is byte-for-byte what it is today. Consequence the callers rely on: every `DillaGroup` method called inside a unit is atomic with the app-table writes made through `UnitScope::with_conn` in the same unit. After a unit rolls back, every `DillaGroup` touched inside it is stale: `ClientCore` drops it from its cache.

**L-SQL-10 app schema v1** (`src/client/schema.rs`; C2; created by `pub fn migrate_app(storage: &DillaStorage) -> Result<(), StorageError>`, idempotent, inside one `unit`)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_meta (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_groups (
  group_id     BLOB    PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(group_id) = 16),
  kind         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  community_id BLOB    CHECK (community_id IS NULL OR length(community_id) = 16),
  target_id    BLOB    NOT NULL CHECK (length(target_id) = 16),
  state        INTEGER NOT NULL,            -- 0 registering, 1 joining, 2 active, 3 needs_resync, 4 gone
  next_seq     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  -- every delivery-service seq below it is applied or skipped
  acked_seq    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  acked_epoch  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  resync       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (resync IN (0, 1)),  -- 1 while a state-1 row is joining over a local group that was in state 2 or 3
  was_gone     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (was_gone IN (0, 1)),  -- 1 while a state-1 row is joining over a row that was gone (state 4)
  max_epoch    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0   -- the highest epoch this device has held for the group id; only ever raised
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_groups_by_target ON app_groups (target_id, kind) WHERE state <> 4;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_handshake_tail (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, epoch INTEGER NOT NULL, kind INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sender INTEGER, blob BLOB NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (group_id, seq)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_proposals (
  group_id BLOB NOT NULL, ref BLOB NOT NULL, epoch INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (group_id, ref)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_messages (
  group_id      BLOB    NOT NULL,
  seq           INTEGER NOT NULL,
  epoch         INTEGER NOT NULL,
  recv_ts       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status        INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- 0 ok, 1 cannot_decrypt, 2 deleted
  reason        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  sender_user   BLOB,                       -- NULL unless status = 0, or status 2 for this device's own deleted upload (L-CORE-08 rule 2)
  sender_device BLOB    NOT NULL,           -- status 0: the MLS credential's device; else the DS uploader_device
  sender_leaf   INTEGER,
  sender_kind   INTEGER,
  sender_tier   INTEGER,
  msg_id        BLOB,
  type          INTEGER,
  body          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  envelope      BLOB,                       -- the envelope CBOR (with k_f) of an ok row; NULL otherwise
  franking_tag  BLOB    NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (group_id, seq)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_messages_by_msg ON app_messages (group_id, msg_id);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_outbox (
  msg_id   BLOB    PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(msg_id) = 16),
  group_id BLOB    NOT NULL,
  envelope BLOB    NOT NULL,
  created  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  state    INTEGER NOT NULL,                -- 0 queued, 1 in_flight, 2 failed
  error    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  epoch    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0       -- the epoch send_encrypt framed the message in; read by send_confirm
) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS app_outbox_by_group ON app_outbox (group_id, created, msg_id);
```

`app_meta` keys and values (each value one CBOR item): `schema` = `1`; `signup` = `[1, instance_id b16, device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, umk_pub b32, ssk_pub b32, sig_umk_ssk b64, sig_ssk_dev b64, ssk_priv b32, k_backup b32]`; `identity` = `[1, instance_id b16, user_id b16, device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, umk_pub b32, ssk_pub b32, username tstr, credential bstr, device_list_body bstr, list_published uint 0|1]`; `session` = `[token tstr, expires uint, idle_expires uint]`; `root_sealed` = the stored root object of protocol/06 (exactly 103 bytes); `state_sealed` = the stored state object of protocol/06. `pub const HANDSHAKE_TAIL: usize = 64` (defined once, in `src/client/schema.rs`, re-exported from `dilla_core::client`; task 6 uses it as `HANDSHAKE_TAIL as i64` and defines no constant of its own) is the number of tail rows kept per group (the oldest are deleted in the unit that inserts). The whole schema above is created by task 4, in one file, with both columns `resync` and `epoch` (schema v1 has not shipped, so there is no migration and task 5 does not edit `schema.rs`). `migrate_app` creates every table `IF NOT EXISTS` and seeds `schema = 1` with `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so a newer file keeps its value; `ClientCore::open` reads `schema` right after and refuses a value greater than 1 with `E_CORE_STATE` "app schema <n> is newer than this build" (`StorageError` has no variant for it, so the refusal is made at the `open` boundary, the only caller). `ClientCore::open` runs `PRAGMA secure_delete = ON` on the connection before migrating, so the deleted `signup` record (with `ssk_priv` and `k_backup`) is zero-filled in its page; a file-backed native test asserts that both secrets are in the database file after `signup_begin` and absent after `signup_complete`. Residual, recorded and not addressed: on OPFS sahpool a journal slot may keep an old page until it is reused.

*Amended after the core hardening (2026-10-05; `376ed5f`, `bf7687d`, `cfa1023`).* Schema v1 gained `app_groups.was_gone` and `app_groups.max_epoch` in place (the version stays 1: v1 has not shipped; a store created by an earlier build of this branch lacks both columns and every group call on it fails with `E_CORE_STORAGE`, so persistent test profiles must start fresh). `was_gone` is written 1 only by `group_join_external` over a row in state 4, and cleared by `group_joined` and by `group_discard`; `resync` and `was_gone` are never both 1, and a state-1 row with both 0 was created by its join. `max_epoch` is written only through `MAX(max_epoch, ?)`, and exactly when the device reaches an epoch (as amended by `3f26670`): by `group_apply` for every commit it merges (staged, or this device's own pending commit) with the new epoch; by `commit_confirm` with the epoch after the merge; by `group_joined` with the epoch of the joined group (the external commit the server accepted; the uncommitted epoch of a join is not recorded before); by `welcomes_apply` with the joined epoch (which equals the served label), on the UPDATE or the INSERT. These are every epoch change of a stored group, so no deletion writes it: not the removal of this device (state 4), not `group_join_external` when it deletes a stale group, not `group_discard` — the value they would write was already written when that epoch was reached. A group created by `group_create` starts at epoch 0, the column's default. The floor it feeds is L-CORE-07's.

**L-CORE-05 `ClientCore` lifecycle** (`src/client/mod.rs`)

```rust
pub struct ClientCore { /* provider: DillaProvider, signer: Option<SignatureKeyPair>,
                           groups: BTreeMap<[u8; 16], DillaGroup> — all private */ }
impl ClientCore {
    /// Takes the only handle. Runs `DillaStorage::migrate()` then `migrate_app`, then loads the DSK
    /// with `SignatureKeyPair::read` when `identity` or `signup` exists.
    pub fn open(conn: ConnHandle) -> Result<Self, ClientError>;
    /// Drops every cached `DillaGroup`; each reloads on its next use with `DillaGroup::load`.
    pub fn unload(&mut self);
}
```

Dropping a `ClientCore` drops the provider and with it the last `ConnHandle`; `ClientCore` never clones the handle and never hands it out. Randomness (ids, `k_f`, key seeds, nonces, the recovery key) comes from the provider's `OpenMlsRand`, except the DSK: `SignatureKeyPair::new` draws from `OsRng` itself (`openmls_basic_credential-0.6.0/src/lib.rs:162`); both are the platform CSPRNG. A `DillaGroup` is loaded on first use and cached; any method whose unit rolls back evicts the groups it touched. Every method that changes state does so inside exactly one `unit`.

**L-CORE-06 identity, signup, session, KeyPackages** (`src/client/identity.rs`; methods of `ClientCore`)

```rust

///  device_id b16|null, username tstr ("" unless phase 2), list_published uint 0|1]
pub fn identity(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 0 only. Generates UMK and SSK seeds, the DSK (`SignatureKeyPair::new`, stored in OpenMLS's
/// signature-key table, C6), a random device_id and a random 32-byte recovery key RK. Builds the
/// credential signatures with kind = user, tier = browser, signer_tier = browser. Seals the root
/// object under k_header(RK) and writes `root_sealed`; writes the `signup` record (with ssk_priv and
/// k_backup(RK)). Returns RK as 52 Crockford base32 characters, ungrouped. RK and UMK_priv are
/// zeroised before returning and are stored nowhere.
pub fn signup_begin(&mut self, instance_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<String, ClientError>;

/// Phase 1 only. The POST /v1/accounts body:
/// [invite tstr, username tstr, display tstr, umk_pub b32, ssk_pub b32, sig_umk_ssk b64,
///  password tstr|null, [device_id b16, dsk_pub b32, 1, 1, credential bstr]]
/// where credential is the 10-element CredentialIdentity with user_id = 16 zero bytes.
/// Pure: calling it again with other arguments is how a refused registration is retried.
pub fn signup_request(&self, invite: &str, username: &str, display: &str, password: Option<&str>)
    -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// writes `identity` with list_published = 0, deletes `signup` (zeroising ssk_priv and k_backup).
/// Returns the PUT /v1/users/{user_id}/device-list body [1, blob bstr, ssk_signature b64, prev_hash b32].
pub fn signup_complete(&mut self, user_id: &[u8; 16], username: &str, now: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Phase 1 only, and only while no `session` record exists: a stored session in phase 1 means

/// stored DSK. Phase becomes 0.
pub fn signup_reset(&mut self) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

pub fn device_list_body(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;        // phase 2; the stored PUT body
pub fn device_list_published(&mut self) -> Result<(), ClientError>;    // sets list_published = 1

/// Phase >= 1. The POST /v1/devices/{device_id}/sessions body [nonce b32, purpose uint, sig b64, null, null],
/// sig = Ed25519(DSK, "dilla session v1" || instance_id || device_id || nonce || purpose as one byte).
/// purpose must be 0 or 1, else E_CORE_INPUT. Signs exactly `session_preimage(...)`.
pub fn session_sign(&self, nonce: &[u8; 32], purpose: u8) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// A free function of `dilla_core::client` (public so the vector `protocol/vectors/identity.json`
/// `session_preimage`, which fixes a device id, can be checked): the 81 bytes
/// "dilla session v1" || instance_id || device_id || nonce || purpose. It returns a `Vec<u8>`, not
/// `[u8; 81]`, on purpose: with a fixed array a dropped purpose byte would leave a trailing zero and
/// the purpose-0 vector would stay green.
pub fn session_preimage(instance_id: &[u8; 16], device_id: &[u8; 16], nonce: &[u8; 32], purpose: u8) -> Vec<u8>;

/// Phase >= 1 (Signup.submit stores the token in phase 1, before signup_complete).
pub fn session_store(&mut self, token: &str, expires: u64, idle_expires: u64) -> Result<(), ClientError>;
pub fn session(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;                  // null | [token, expires, idle_expires]
pub fn session_clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// Phase 2. Builds `count` (1..=32) KeyPackages and, when `last_resort`, one last-resort package, each
/// as an MLSMessage. Returns the POST /v1/keypackages body [packages [bstr], last_resort bstr|null].
pub fn key_packages(&mut self, count: u32, last_resort: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// [root_sealed bstr|null, state_sealed bstr|null] — what web-2 uploads to /v1/backups.
pub fn sealed_objects(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

Sealing (protocol/06 "Header"): `stored = CBOR [1, nonce b12, ciphertext]`, `ciphertext = AES-256-GCM(key, nonce, plaintext, aad)`, random nonce; root: key `k_header(RK)`, plaintext `CBOR [1, umk_priv b32, ssk_priv b32]`, aad `"dilla root v1"`, stored length exactly 103; state: key `k_backup(RK)`, plaintext `CBOR [1, device_list bstr, []]`, aad `"dilla state v1"`.

**L-CORE-07 groups** (`src/client/groups.rs`; web-1 handles `kind = 0` text groups of community channels only). `policy_version` in every signature below is **the instance's** policy version (`GET /v1/instance` element 8, `Instance.policyVersion`), which is what protocol/01 puts in `dilla_binding`; it is not the community's `policy_version` of L-HTTP-01. `DillaBinding::matches` (`binding.rs:143-156`) does not compare it, so a joiner whose instance value has moved on still joins.

```rust

///   next_seq uint, proposals_pending uint, pending_commit uint 0|1]] ordered by group_id.
/// epoch is 0 for a group in state 4 (its MLS state is deleted).
pub fn groups(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Creates the MLS group with DillaBinding { v: 1, instance_id, community_id: Some, target_id: channel_id,
/// kind: Text, policy_version, e2ee_version: 1, media_version: GroupKind::Text.media_version() } and the
/// instance's external sender (`external_senders(external_sender_pub, instance_id)`); inserts the row in
/// state 0. Returns the POST /v1/groups body [group_id b16, binding bstr, group_info bstr, ratchet_tree bstr].
/// E_CORE_STATE when a non-gone row exists for (channel_id, 0).
pub fn group_create(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], community_id: &[u8; 16], channel_id: &[u8; 16],
    policy_version: u64, external_sender_pub: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// State 0 -> 2 with the `next_seq` of the 201 body [group_id, next_seq].
pub fn group_registered(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], next_seq: u64) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// States 0 and 1 only (E_CORE_STATE "group state <n>" otherwise): deletes the MLS group and the

/// group_join_external when a local group in state 2 or 3 existed) returns to state 3 with
/// `resync = 0`; a row that was `joining` over a gone row (`was_gone = 1`) returns to state 4 with
/// `was_gone = 0`, keeping every app_messages, app_outbox and app_handshake_tail row, next_seq,
/// acked_* and max_epoch; any other row (one its join or registration created) is deleted with its
/// timeline, outbox and tail.
pub fn group_discard(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// External join, and resync when a local group exists (it is deleted first, in the same unit).
/// `info_body` is the 200 body of GET /v1/groups/{id}/info [epoch, group_info, tree_hash, next_seq];
/// `tree_body` the 200 body of GET /v1/groups/{id}/tree [epoch, ratchet_tree, tree_hash]. Checks, in
/// this order, each refusal writing nothing: their epochs and tree hashes must be equal (E_CORE_INPUT
/// "info_body and tree_body disagree"); the GroupInfo's group id must be `group_id` (E_CORE_INPUT
/// "GroupInfo group id does not match", checked before any row is read or anything joined); an

/// info_body label) must not be below the floor, because the join lands at e + 1 (E_CORE_INPUT
/// "GroupInfo would rejoin at or below an epoch this device has held"). The expected binding is built
/// as in group_create. Row state 1: an existing row is updated (resync = 1 over state 2 or 3,
/// was_gone = 1 over state 4; max_epoch is not written: the deleted stale group's epoch is already

/// community_id and target_id are never rewritten; a missing row is inserted.

/// State 1 -> 2 with next_seq = max(next_seq, seq + 1) (never lowered), from the 200 body

pub fn group_joined(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], seq: u64) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// `welcomes_body`: the 200 body of GET /v1/welcomes

/// next_seq = commit_seq + 1, or max(next_seq, commit_seq + 1) over an existing row: never lowered),

/// joined epoch. Checks, in this order: not expected → 3; a row in state 0, 1 or 2 → 1; an existing

/// E_CORE_STATE (the row is never rebound); a non-gone row of a *different* group for the expected
/// channel → 2 E_CORE_STATE; a blob that is not an MLS Welcome or a ratchet_tree that is not a TLS
/// RatchetTree → 2 E_CORE_INPUT; then, on the staged Welcome before anything is stored
/// (`DillaGroup::join_from_welcome_labelled`, `3f26670`): an OpenMLS staging failure → 2 E_CORE_MLS;
/// the staged binding is not the expected one → 2 E_BINDING; the staged group id is not the item's
/// `group_id` → 2 E_BINDING; the staged GroupContext's epoch is not the item's `epoch` or its tree hash
/// is not the item's `tree_hash` (the delivery service's label: the state right after the commit
/// that added the device) → 2 E_CORE_INPUT (`MlsError::WelcomeLabel`, detail "the Welcome's epoch or
/// tree hash is not the served label"); then, over an existing row, a joined epoch at or below the
/// floor → 2 E_CORE_INPUT. E_CORE_STORAGE and E_CORE_RELOAD are returned as the call's error, never as
/// an outcome.
pub fn welcomes_apply(&mut self, welcomes_body: &[u8], expected: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

*The epoch floor (amended after the core hardening, `bf7687d`, `cfa1023`).* A rejoin over an existing row — a resync by GroupInfo (states 2 and 3), a rejoin of a gone row (state 4), a Welcome over a row in state 3 or 4 — may not land in an epoch this device has already held. The floor is `max(app_groups.max_epoch, the epoch of the MLS group still stored for the id)` (L-SQL-10 says who raises `max_epoch`). A Welcome is refused when its joined epoch is **at or below** the floor (its epoch is known only after OpenMLS staged it, so the refusal rolls the unit back); a GroupInfo at epoch `e` is refused when `e` is **below** the floor (its join lands at `e + 1`; a GroupInfo at exactly the floor is accepted). A first join (no row) has no floor. Both refusals are `E_CORE_INPUT`. A resync that is discarded keeps the floor, so it can be repeated from the same GroupInfo (the uncommitted epoch of an external join is not recorded until `group_joined`). Because a Welcome must carry the epoch the delivery service labelled (`3f26670`), a Welcome can raise the floor only to an epoch the server vouched for. Known limits, recorded for web-2: after `dillad restore` the server's sequence and epoch move back, and this core cannot tell that from a rollback, so rows below its `next_seq` are ignored and a resync below its floor is refused until the group passes it (both values would need keying to the instance `generation`); the floor is a number only, so a GroupInfo at exactly the floor is not compared with the epoch the device held.

*Loaded groups (amended, `fc29402`).* Every method that loads a stored MLS group to use it (`group_apply`, `send_encrypt`, `commit_build`, `commit_confirm`, `commit_abort`) first compares it with its row: MLS group id, `kind = 0` with a text binding, `target_id`, `community_id`. On a mismatch it returns `E_CORE_STATE` "the stored group does not match its row; resync the group" and caches nothing; the repair is `group_join_external` for the row (states 2 and 3), which deletes the stored group unchecked. `send_confirm` treats such a group as "no MLS group stored" (`sender_leaf` NULL). `groups()`, `cursor_body`, `message_deleted` and `group_apply`'s epoch read-back read the stored group's epoch without the check. Only a corrupted store reaches this state; the TypeScript model does not model it.

`groups()`'s `pending_commit` and the pending-commit checks of L-CORE-08/09 read `DillaGroup::has_pending_commit`, which task 5 adds to `core/dilla-core/src/mls/group.rs` after `epoch()` (`group.rs:803-805`): `pub fn has_pending_commit(&self) -> bool { self.group.pending_commit().is_some() }`. Own-leaf removal needs no accessor: `StagedCommit::self_removed()` is public in OpenMLS 0.9.0.

**L-CORE-08 ordered processing, commits, cursor** (`src/client/sync.rs`; C1)

```rust
/// `handshakes`: a CBOR array of rows [seq uint, epoch uint, kind uint, sender uint|null, blob bstr]
/// (the row shape of GET /v1/groups/{id}/handshakes and the payload of gateway op 16).
/// `messages`: a CBOR array of rows
/// [seq uint, epoch uint, uploader_device b16, blob bstr|null, commitment b32|null, franking_tag b32,
///  recv_ts uint, deleted uint 0|1] (the row shape of GET /v1/groups/{id}/messages).
/// Either array may be empty. `through`: the caller asserts that the two arrays together hold every
/// row of the group with next_seq <= seq <= through.
///
/// Group state must be 2. Rows are merged by seq and applied ascending; a row with seq < next_seq or
/// seq > through is ignored; a seq present in both arrays is E_CORE_INPUT. Each row is one unit that
/// also sets next_seq = seq + 1. After the last row next_seq = max(next_seq, through + 1).
/// Returns [state uint, epoch uint, next_seq uint, new_seqs [uint], proposals_pending uint, flags uint]
/// flags: bit 0 the epoch changed, bit 1 an outbox row was adopted (rules 2 and 4: a queued, in-flight
/// or failed row whose upload the server stored; it is deleted from the outbox).
pub fn group_apply(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], handshakes: &[u8], messages: &[u8], through: u64)
    -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// State 2, no pending commit. `proposals_body`: the 200 body of GET /v1/groups/{id}/proposals
/// [[ref bstr, kind uint, target_leaf uint|null, blob bstr, void uint 0|1]]. Queues every non-void
/// proposal of the current epoch that is not yet in app_proposals, then builds a self-update commit
/// (it covers every queued proposal and yields the Welcomes). Returns the POST /v1/groups/{id}/commit
/// body [epoch uint, commit bstr, group_info bstr, welcomes [[device_id b16, blob bstr]], null].
pub fn commit_build(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], proposals_body: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Merges the pending commit (no-op when there is none: the echo was applied first), clears
/// app_proposals of the group and raises max_epoch to the epoch after the merge. Returns the
/// group_apply result shape with new_seqs = [] and bit 0 set.
pub fn commit_confirm(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Clears the pending commit; queued proposals stay queued. No-op without one.
pub fn commit_abort(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// CBOR null when next_seq - 1 <= acked_seq, else the POST /v1/groups/{id}/cursor body
/// [last_seq uint = next_seq - 1, last_epoch uint = the group's epoch].
pub fn cursor_body(&self, group_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
pub fn cursor_acked(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], last_seq: u64, last_epoch: u64) -> Result<(), ClientError>;

/// Gateway op 21 for a row this device already holds: the stored row (group_id, seq) becomes status 2
/// with body '' and envelope NULL, exactly the write of row rule 2. Any group state but 4. A seq
/// that is not stored is a no-op (a row the device has not fetched yet arrives later with deleted = 1).
/// Returns the group_apply result shape with new_seqs = [seq] when a row changed, else [], flags 0.
/// E_CORE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown group.
pub fn message_deleted(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], seq: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

Row rules of `group_apply` (binding; the reference is `testkit/src/client.rs:761-840`, which this must exceed):

1. *Handshake row.* Insert into `app_handshake_tail` (trim to 64; the write is an upsert, so a handshake row is never skipped because its seq is occupied: a commit served where an own message already sits, as after `dillad restore`, must still be processed). Deserialize the blob as an `MLSMessage` protocol message; **a blob that is not an MLS protocol message is an error under the same rules as a processing error below** (it stops the group on a kind-1 or kind-2 row and is skipped on a kind-0 row; pre-flight ruling, task 6). If its framed epoch is lower than the group's epoch: skip (an own commit already merged, or a replay). Otherwise `process_message`: `StagedCommit` → when `StagedCommit::self_removed()` is true, delete the MLS group **without merging** and set state 4 (the merged state of a removed member is never used); else clear this device's own pending commit if it holds one (`DillaGroup::clear_pending_commit`: the device lost a race and has not yet called `commit_abort`), then `merge_staged_commit`, delete the group's `app_proposals`, set bit 0 — all in the row's unit. `Proposal` → if its ref is not in `app_proposals`, `store_pending_proposal` and insert the ref with the current epoch. `OwnPendingCommit` → `merge_pending_commit`, as `commit_confirm`. `ExternalJoinProposal`, `OwnPrivateMessage`, `Application` in the handshake stream → skip. **An error from `process_message` or a merge on a row of kind 1 or 2 (a commit) sets state 3, leaves `next_seq` at this row and stops; the result is returned, not an error.** An error on a kind 0 row (a proposal) skips the row.
*Stored seqs (amended, `f79424a`).* Before rules 3–5, a message row with `deleted = 0` whose `(group, seq)` already holds an `app_messages` row (an own row confirmed ahead of `next_seq`, or a row the server serves twice) is **skipped** before any MLS processing: it is not listed in `new_seqs`, no ratchet step is spent, and `next_seq` moves to `seq + 1` as for any row. Rule 2 alone changes a stored row. Handshake rows are not skipped on occupancy (rule 1).

*The commitment of a served row, and the matching outbox row (amended, `085a441`, `410c543`).* The delivery service stores `C`, read from the upload's `private_message.authenticated_data`, as `mls_app_messages.commitment_c`, keeps it when the message is deleted, and serves it as element 4 (`commitment`) of every `GET …/messages` row, deleted rows included (protocol/02 "`commitment` … is the stored value of `C`"); gateway op 19 carries none (normalised to `null`, L-TS-07 rule 3). The commitment **a row carries** is that served field, else the blob's own 32-byte `authenticated_data` when the blob is a `PrivateMessage`; when both are present and differ the row carries none. **The matching outbox row** is the group's outbox row in **any state** (0 queued, 1 in flight, 2 failed), the first in `created, msg_id` order, whose stored envelope's `Envelope::commitment()` equals the commitment the row carries. `C` is keyed by the envelope's random `k_f`, which `send_prepare` fixes and every `send_encrypt` of the row reuses, so it names exactly one outbox row and every upload of it.

2. *Message row with `deleted = 1`.* When a row is stored at `(group, seq)`: update it to status 2 (body `''`, envelope NULL, reason `''`; its sender columns stay); listed in `new_seqs`. When none is stored: if `uploader_device` is this device, the served `commitment` is present and a matching outbox row exists, insert status 2 with body `''`, envelope NULL, this device's `sender_user`, `sender_device`, `sender_leaf`, `sender_kind`, `sender_tier`, and the outbox envelope's `msg_id` and `type`, delete that outbox row and set **bit 1** (the server stored the upload, so it is never resent; a late `send_confirm` reads the marker back by `msg_id`); otherwise insert the plain marker (status 2, sender columns NULL except `sender_device = uploader_device`) and leave the outbox as it is. Listed in `new_seqs` either way.
3. *Message row with `blob = null`, `deleted = 0`.* Insert status 1, reason `E_PRUNED`.
4. *Message row whose `uploader_device` is this device.* Never handed to OpenMLS. (A stored seq was skipped above.) With a matching outbox row for the commitment the row carries: insert the message row from that row's envelope (status 0, this device's identity, the row's `seq`, `epoch`, `recv_ts`, `franking_tag`), delete the outbox row, set bit 1. Otherwise insert status 1, reason `E_OWN_UNKNOWN`, leave every outbox row as it was and do not set bit 1 (the row in flight is never adopted for another upload's echo).
5. *Any other message row.* `process_message`; on `Application(r)`: if `r.sender.device_id != uploader_device` insert status 1, reason `E_SENDER_MISMATCH`; else insert status 0 with `sender_user`, `sender_device`, `sender_leaf`, `sender_kind`, `sender_tier` from `r.sender`, `msg_id`, `type`, `body` and the envelope bytes. On error insert status 1 with `sender_device = uploader_device` and reason = the `ClientError.code` the error maps to (`E_CREDENTIAL` for an undecodable sender credential, an `E_ENVELOPE_*` or `E_FRANK_MISMATCH` code for the envelope checks, `E_CORE_MLS` for an OpenMLS failure). A cannot-decrypt row never stops the group. Every seq inserted or changed by rules 2–5 is listed in `new_seqs`.

A message row framed in an epoch ahead of the group's is stored `cannot_decrypt` like any other undecryptable row; the core does not stop on it (any member can frame a message in a future epoch, so stopping would hand a member a way to stall the group or force resyncs). That a commit is never skipped is the caller's obligation under the `through` contract, which L-TS-07 rule 2 now meets by construction.

*The credential of a joined leaf (amended, `f1f8917`, `e770bf6`; protocol/01 "Client policy for proposals from members", protocol/02 invariant 4).* A receiving core refuses, with `E_CREDENTIAL` and no state change, a member commit whose UpdatePath leaf carries a credential that is not byte-identical to the committer's pre-commit leaf credential, a commit that applies an `Update` whose leaf node changes its proposer's credential, and a standalone `Update` proposal that does so (it is never queued). (hardening G) The same three refusals apply when the new leaf node's **signature key** differs from the leaf's pre-commit key: a leaf's credential and key are its identity together. Under rule 1 such a commit row is a processing error like any other: it sets state 3 and stops (the engine resyncs, L-TS-07 rule 7), and such a proposal row is skipped. The delivery service runs the same check (`DillaPublicGroup::process_message` and `queue_proposal`) and answers `POST …/commit` and `…/proposal` with `422 E_COMMIT_INVALID` (rule `structural`) and `/heal` with `422` (rule `tail`), so an honest server never serves such a commit; the engine's existing `422` handling covers its own commits. An external commit's path leaf is a new leaf; two rules bind it to the leaf it replaces. `64c9fd7`: for every Remove in an external commit whose removed leaf names the same device as the new leaf, the two credentials must be byte-identical, otherwise `E_CREDENTIAL`. (hardening G) A device holds at most one leaf: when the pre-commit tree holds exactly one leaf of the joiner's device, the external commit must remove it; when it holds two or more, the external commit is refused; otherwise `E_CREDENTIAL`. At the delivery service a credential refusal of an external commit (`…/resync`, an external join) answers `422 E_COMMIT_INVALID` with rule `external_joiner` (hardening G; before it, `structural`). The core builds every resync with the stock builder, which removes the device's own leaf, and never changes a leaf's key, so no TypeScript task builds such a commit by hand. Everything else about a credential (its signatures, the device list as the client verifies it, tier, TOFU pins) is not validated in web-1 (Deferred).

**L-CORE-10 the parity fixture** (`core/dilla-core/tests/fixtures/group_apply_parity.json`, committed by task 6; ruling 15 as amended)

The Rust core is the authority for `group_apply`; the TypeScript engine is unit-tested against `ModelCore`, a hand-written model. The fixture ties the two together. It is one JSON object `{"v":1,"cases":[…]}`; each case is `{"name": tstr, "rows": [{"stream": "h"|"m", "seq": n, "what": tstr}], "through": n, "expect": {"state": n, "epoch": n, "next_seq": n, "new_seqs": [n], "proposals_pending": n, "flags": n}, "result": "<hex of the returned CBOR>"}`. Every case starts from the same state, which both tests build and assert before applying the rows: this device ("me") created and registered the group (the relay or model answers registration with `next_seq = 1`), a peer joined by external commit at seq 1, and "me" applied it — state 2, epoch 1, `next_seq` 2, no proposal, no pending commit, empty outbox. `what` is one of `peer-message` (a type-0 message by the peer in the epoch current at that seq), `peer-commit` (a self-update commit by the peer, kind 1), `bad-commit` (a kind-1 row whose blob cannot be processed), `own-echo` (a message row whose `uploader_device` is this device, after "me" ran `send_prepare` and `send_encrypt` for one message; served, as the delivery service serves it, with that upload's commitment `C` in element 4, which its blob also carries as `authenticated_data`), `pruned` (`blob = null`, `deleted = 0`), `deleted` (`deleted = 1`), `add-proposal` (an Add of a third device signed by the instance's external sender, kind 0). The eight cases, exactly:

| name | rows (stream seq what) | through | expect `[state, epoch, next_seq, new_seqs, proposals_pending, flags]` | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `peer message` | m 2 peer-message | 2 | `[2, 1, 3, [2], 0, 0]` | `8602010381020000` |
| `commit before the message of its epoch` | m 3 peer-message, h 2 peer-commit (given in this order; the message is framed in epoch 2) | 3 | `[2, 2, 4, [3], 0, 1]` | `8602020481030001` |
| `through beyond the rows` | m 2 peer-message | 5 | `[2, 1, 6, [2], 0, 0]` | `8602010681020000` |
| `a row above through is ignored` | m 2 peer-message, m 3 peer-message | 2 | `[2, 1, 3, [2], 0, 0]` | `8602010381020000` |
| `own echo is adopted` | m 2 own-echo | 2 | `[2, 1, 3, [2], 0, 2]` | `8602010381020002` |
| `a commit that cannot be processed stops the group` | h 2 bad-commit, m 3 peer-message | 3 | `[3, 1, 2, [], 0, 0]` | `86030102800000` |
| `pruned and deleted rows` | m 2 pruned, m 3 deleted | 3 | `[2, 1, 4, [2, 3], 0, 0]` | `860201048202030000` |
| `a proposal is queued` | h 2 add-proposal | 2 | `[2, 1, 3, [], 1, 0]` | `86020103800100` |

Task 6 (`tests/client_sync.rs`, test `the_parity_fixture_holds`) builds each case with its relay and real groups, calls `group_apply`, and asserts both the decoded tuple and that the returned bytes equal `result`. Task 16 (`src/sync/testing/parity.test.ts`) reads the same file, and for each case (a) builds the same rows with `ModelDs`, calls `ModelCore.groupApply` and expects an `ApplyResult` equal to `expect`, and (b) passes `result` through `wrapCore`'s `groupApply` decoder (a stub handle that returns those bytes) and expects the same `ApplyResult`. If a case's expected values turn out to contradict the row rules above when task 6 runs it natively, the rules win: task 6 stops and reports (a "Ledger conflict"), and the fixture is corrected by a ruling, never by the implementer. *Checked after the core hardening (2026-10-05):* the fixture file is unchanged since task 6, and the hardening fixer's full test run at `410c543` passed `the_parity_fixture_holds` with all eight `result` values as written; no case meets a stored seq, a gone row, a rejoin or a send confirmation, and `own echo is adopted` is adopted through the commitment the test relay now serves (and the blob carries).

**L-CORE-09 sending and reading** (`src/client/messages.rs`)

```rust
/// State 2. Builds Envelope { v: 1, msg_id: random, kind: message (0), thread_id: None, reply_to: None,
/// body, attachments: [], previews: [], k_f: random } and validates it (E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT above 4000
/// UTF-8 bytes — `MAX_BODY_LONG`, `envelope/mod.rs:15-16, 362`; the limit is bytes, not characters —
/// E_CORE_INPUT for an empty body after trimming). Inserts the outbox row in state 0.
/// Returns [msg_id b16].
pub fn send_prepare(&mut self, group_id: &[u8; 16], body: &str, now: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// Outbox state 0 -> 1 and `create_message`, in one unit; the row's `epoch` is set to the group's.
/// E_CORE_STATE, with nothing changed, when: the row is not in state 0; the group is not in state 2;
/// another outbox row of the group is in state 1 (one message of a group is in flight at a time);
/// the group has a row in app_proposals ("proposals are pending"); the group holds a pending commit
/// ("a commit is pending"). The last two are OpenMLS's own rule (it frames no application message
/// while a proposal or a commit is pending) made before `create_message` is reached. The caller
/// tells the cases apart by reading `groups()`, not by the detail (L-TS-07 rule 5).
/// Returns [group_id b16, message_body bstr] — message_body is the POST /v1/groups/{id}/message body
/// [epoch uint, private_message bstr].
pub fn send_encrypt(&mut self, msg_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// `response`: the 200 body [seq uint, franking_tag b32, recv_ts uint]. The outbox row must be in
/// state 1 (E_CORE_STATE "outbox row in state <n>" otherwise). Inserts the message row (status 0, own
/// identity, `epoch` = the outbox row's epoch: the 200 body carries none and the group may already be
/// one epoch on) and deletes the outbox row; when group_apply already adopted the row (rules 2 and 4)
/// there is no outbox row and it only reads the stored row back by msg_id. When a message row is
/// already stored at (group, seq) (amended, `f79424a`): if it is a status-2 row whose sender_device is
/// this device and whose msg_id is NULL or this msg_id (the deleted marker of this upload, served
/// before the answer was read) the confirm succeeds — the outbox row is deleted, a NULL msg_id is
/// filled in, and [group_id, seq] is returned; any other row means the answer contradicts what is
/// stored — the outbox row moves to state 2 (failed) with error "E_CORE_STATE" in a committed unit,
/// and the call still returns E_CORE_STATE "message seq exists"; the caller must not call send_fail
/// after it (the row is already failed, so that would be E_CORE_STATE too), and nothing is resent
/// unless the person retries. Returns [group_id b16, seq uint].
pub fn send_confirm(&mut self, msg_id: &[u8; 16], response: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

pub fn send_requeue(&mut self, msg_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), ClientError>;              // 1 -> 0
pub fn send_fail(&mut self, msg_id: &[u8; 16], error: &str) -> Result<(), ClientError>;    // 0|1 -> 2, error <= 64 bytes
pub fn send_retry(&mut self, msg_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), ClientError>;                // 2 -> 0
pub fn send_discard(&mut self, msg_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), ClientError>;              // deletes a row in state 0 or 2

/// [[msg_id b16, state uint, error tstr, created uint, body tstr]] ordered by created, msg_id.
pub fn outbox(&self, group_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;

/// The `limit` (1..=200) rows with the highest seq below `before_seq` (0 means from the newest),
/// ascending by seq:
/// [[seq uint, epoch uint, recv_ts uint, status uint, reason tstr, sender_user b16|null,
///   sender_device b16, sender_kind uint|null, sender_tier uint|null, msg_id b16|null, type uint|null,
///   body tstr]]
/// A status-2 row may carry sender_user, sender_kind, sender_tier, msg_id and type: a row deleted
/// after it was stored keeps them, and this device's own deleted upload (L-CORE-08 rule 2) is
/// inserted with them; a status-1 row and a plain deleted marker have them null.
pub fn timeline(&self, group_id: &[u8; 16], before_seq: u64, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientError>;
```

### L-WASM — `dilla-core-wasm`

**L-WASM-01 `StoreHandle` owns a shared handle** (`src/store.rs`; B1.1)

`StoreHandle.conn` becomes `RefCell<Option<dilla_core::mls::ConnHandle>>` (on this target `Rc<RefCell<rusqlite::Connection>>`). The exported surface (`exec`, `query_scalar_i64`, `capacity`, `reserve_capacity`, `pause`, `resume`, `close`) keeps its names and error strings, and its signatures with one exception: `close` becomes `pub fn close(self) -> Result<(), JsError>` (it returned nothing, `store.rs:226-228`, and a busy check needs a `Result`; the generated TypeScript is still `close(): void`, which now throws). New, crate-private: `pub(crate) fn share(&self) -> Result<ConnHandle, JsError>` (a clone of the `Rc`; `E_STORE_PAUSED: the store is paused` when there is none). `pause()` first checks `Rc::strong_count`: when it is greater than 1 it changes nothing and fails with `E_STORE_BUSY: <n> handles are still open`, where `<n>` is the number of lent clones still alive, `Rc::strong_count - 1` (one held clone reads exactly `E_STORE_BUSY: 1 handles are still open`; task 7's mutation depends on that text); otherwise it drops the handle and calls `pause_vfs()` as today. `close()` has the same check and the same error. `exec` and `query_scalar_i64` use `try_borrow` on the connection and fail with `E_STORE_SQL: the connection is in use` instead of panicking. `open_encrypted` is unchanged (DELETE journal, C15).

**L-WASM-02 `store_mls_probe`** (`src/store.rs`; a test probe beside `unencrypted_vfs_probe`)

```rust
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub fn store_mls_probe(handle: &StoreHandle, op: &str) -> Result<String, JsError>;
```

`op = "create"`: over `handle.share()`, build a `DillaProvider`, `migrate()`, create and store a signer, create one group with a fixed binding (group id sixteen `0x11` bytes), then `self_update` and `merge_pending_commit` so the group stands at epoch 1. `op = "load"`: build a provider, read the signer back, `DillaGroup::load`. Both return the JSON `{"epoch": <n>, "authenticator": "<64 hex>"}` and drop the provider and every group before returning (so `pause()` succeeds afterwards). `create` records the signer's public key under key `signer_pub` in a probe table `probe_mls (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v BLOB NOT NULL)` of the same encrypted database, because `SignatureKeyPair::read` needs it and `DillaGroup` exposes no own-leaf key; `load` reads it there. Two more ops exist so that a page can hold a clone across `pause()` (`create` and `load` drop theirs, and `share()` is crate-private): `op = "hold"` keeps one clone of `handle.share()` in a thread-local and returns `{"held":1}` (a second `hold` is `E_STORE_PROBE: a handle is already held`); `op = "release"` drops it and returns `{"held":0}`. Any failure is `E_STORE_PROBE: <detail>`.

**L-WASM-03 `core_open` and `CoreHandle`** (`src/facade.rs`, module `facade`)

```rust
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub async fn core_open(cfg: StoreOpenConfig) -> Result<CoreHandle, JsValue>;   // store_open, then ClientCore::open(store.share())

#[wasm_bindgen]
pub struct CoreHandle { /* store: StoreHandle, core: RefCell<Option<ClientCore>> */ }

#[wasm_bindgen]
impl CoreHandle {
    pub fn capacity(&self) -> u32;
    pub async fn reserve_capacity(&self, n: u32) -> Result<(), JsError>;
    /// Drops the ClientCore (provider and every group), then StoreHandle::pause.
    pub fn pause(&self) -> Result<(), JsError>;
    /// StoreHandle::resume, then ClientCore::open over the reopened connection. Groups reload lazily.
    pub async fn resume(&self) -> Result<(), JsError>;
    /// Drops the ClientCore, then StoreHandle::close, whose Result it returns (after the drop no
    /// clone is left, so the busy branch is unreachable; the error is propagated, not discarded).
    pub fn close(self) -> Result<(), JsError>;
    // + one method per ClientCore method of L-CORE-06…09 (L-WASM-04)
}
```

`core_open` rejects with whatever `store_open` rejects with (the raw DOMException for contention, so `is_sah_contention` still works) or with an `Error` whose message is a `ClientError` rendering. Every other method throws a `JsError` whose message is the `ClientError`'s `Display` (`"<code>"` or `"<code>: <detail>"`); a call while paused throws `E_STORE_PAUSED: the store is paused`. Besides open and paused the facade has two transient private phases, reported under the existing `E_CORE_STATE` code with the details `the core is not open` (a `ClientCore::open` that failed after the store resumed), `resume in progress` and `the core is busy`; no new code, nothing TypeScript-visible.

`abi_version()` returns `4` through a constant of the browser binding, `pub const BROWSER_ABI_VERSION: u32 = 4;` in `core/dilla-core-wasm/src/lib.rs`. It no longer returns `dilla_core::ABI_VERSION`: that constant is the **wasi** request ABI, element 0 of every wasi request, asserted to be 3 by the wasi crate (`core/dilla-core-wasi/src/exports.rs:1251`) and by dillad's host (`internal/mlswasi/host_test.go:138-146`), and it stays 3.
