### L-HTTP — routes

Common to every row: CBOR bodies per `interfaces.md` A1; `E` = enrolled session required (`401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED` without a valid token, `403 E_FORBIDDEN` for a pending scope, `403 E_PROVISIONAL_OUTSIDE_PAIRING` for a provisional one); every GET is on the server's read bucket (`429 E_RATE_LIMITED` with `retry_after_ms`) except `GET /i/{code}`, which is on the invite bucket (pre-flight ruling, task 9). Every route can also answer `429` and `500`; a "No other status" below does not exclude them.

**L-HTTP-01 `GET /v1/communities`** (new; C11; F13: a caller sees only its own memberships) — auth E; no parameters; `200 [[community_id b16, name tstr, owner b16, policy_version uint]]`, ordered by `community_id`, unpaginated, `[]` for none (never `null`). Mounted by `Communities.Register`. No other status (beyond the `429` and `500` every route can answer).

**L-HTTP-02 `text_group_id` on the channel reads** (changed; C11) — `GET /v1/channels/{id}` answers the eleven existing elements followed by element 11 `text_group_id (b16|null)`; each row of `GET /v1/communities/{id}/channels` answers its ten existing elements followed by element 10 `text_group_id (b16|null)`. The value is the `GroupID` of the first row of `MLS.GroupsForTarget(ctx, channel_id, 0)` (the oldest open text group, epoch-unknown or not) when the channel's `mode` is 0 and its `kind` is 0, 3 or 4; otherwise `null` without a store call. Authorisation, statuses and ordering of both routes are unchanged (a member who cannot view a channel still gets 404 or no row).

**L-HTTP-03 names on member rows** (changed; C11, F13: only members of the community reach the route) — each row of `GET /v1/communities/{id}/members` becomes `[user_id b16, joined uint, nick tstr, [role_id b16], username tstr, display tstr, kind uint (0 user | 1 bot)]`, read with `Accounts.GetUser` per row; a member whose user row is not found answers `"", "", 0`. Paging, ordering and statuses are unchanged.

**L-HTTP-10 the embedded web client** (new; C9; `internal/web`)

```go
package web
// Embedded is the committed placeholder, or the real build when CI copied it in before `go build`.
func Embedded() fs.FS                                   // the `dist` directory of //go:embed all:dist
// New verifies fsys against its dilla-manifest.json (L-HTTP-11) and returns the handler.
func New(fsys fs.FS) (*Handler, error)
// Fallback returns the handler dillad.New serves in place of the bare mux: a request the mux has a
// pattern for (any method), or whose cleaned path is reserved, goes to mux exactly as before;
// every other request goes to h.
func (h *Handler) Fallback(mux *server.Mux) http.Handler
func (h *Handler) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)
const ManifestName = "dilla-manifest.json"
```

The client is **not** registered on the mux. `mux.Handle("GET /", h)` conflicts with the method-less LiveKit proxy patterns `"/rtc"` and `"/rtc/"` (`internal/dillad/routes.go:241-242`): Go's `ServeMux` panics on that pair, so `dillad.New` would panic whenever an SFU is configured; and a method-qualified catch-all would turn `POST /v1/<unknown>` from 404 into 405. `Fallback` is implemented with `(*http.ServeMux).Handler(r)` (an empty pattern means "no route for this path and method"). `dillad.Options` gains `Web fs.FS // nil means web.Embedded()`; `dillad.New` builds `web.New` and uses `webHandler.Fallback(mux)` where it uses the bare mux today (`server.go:411`), so API answers (404 bodies, 405 with `Allow`, trailing-slash redirects) are byte-for-byte unchanged, no pattern is added and `Options.Extra` keeps full precedence; a manifest mismatch makes `New` fail with an error that starts `dillad: web client: `. Behaviour of the handler, in this order:

1. Method other than GET or HEAD → `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD`, body `method not allowed\n` (`text/plain; charset=utf-8`).
2. Path equal to or under a reserved prefix — `/v1/`, `/gateway`, `/rtc`, `/i/`, `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`, `/debug/` — → `404`, body `404 page not found\n` (`text/plain; charset=utf-8`): the catch-all never answers for the API.
3. Path `/` → the file `index.html`. Any other path is cleaned with `path.Clean`; a path containing `..` or a NUL byte → 404 as in 2.
4. A path that names a file of the manifest → that file.
5. Otherwise, when the last path segment contains no `.` → `index.html` with status 200 (the client router owns the path); else 404 as in 2.

Headers. On every 200 (a 304 carries neither `Content-Type` nor `Content-Length`: `net/http` strips them from a 304 whatever the handler sets, so the handler sets neither there): `Content-Type` from this table by extension, never sniffed — `.html` `text/html; charset=utf-8`, `.js` `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `.css` `text/css; charset=utf-8`, `.wasm` `application/wasm`, `.json` `application/json`, `.woff2` `font/woff2`, `.woff` `font/woff`, `.svg` `image/svg+xml`, `.png` `image/png`, `.ico` `image/x-icon`, `.txt` `text/plain; charset=utf-8`; `New` fails for a manifest file with any other extension. On every 200 and 304: `ETag: "<sha256 hex from the manifest>"`; a request whose `If-None-Match` matches it → `304` with no body (it matches when the header is `*`, or when any comma-separated entry, with an optional `W/` prefix removed, equals the ETag). `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for paths under `/assets/`, `Cache-Control: no-cache` for everything else. `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), display-capture=(), geolocation=()`. And **on every 200 and 304 of every file, whatever its extension**, `Content-Security-Policy`, exactly:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://HOST wss://HOST; worker-src 'self'; media-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```

The policy is on every file because a dedicated worker loaded from a network URL takes its policy from **its own script response**, not from the document that created it (HTML "run a worker", CSP3; only `blob:` and `data:` workers inherit), and the worker is where the KEK, the device key, the token, all plaintext and every network call live: a policy on `.html` alone would leave that worker with none. web-1 has no camera, microphone, screen capture, attachment or decrypted media, so the policy grants none of them; the attachment card (web-2) and the voice plan (web-3) widen `img-src`, `media-src` and `Permissions-Policy` with their own protocol/09 edit and 07 row.

`HOST` is the request's `Host` header when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,253}(:[0-9]{1,5})?$` or `^\[[0-9A-Fa-f:.]{2,45}\](:[0-9]{1,5})?$`; when it does not, the two `ws` sources are omitted (`connect-src 'self'`). No COOP, COEP, CORS or HSTS header is set (C4, F4; TLS termination and HSTS belong to the operator's proxy).

Tests of the embedded tree live in two files with opposite build tags. `internal/web/placeholder_test.go` (`//go:build !webdist`, task 11) holds every assertion that `web.Embedded()` is the committed 288-byte placeholder. `internal/web/webdist_test.go` (`//go:build webdist`, task 22) proves a real build: it reads the directory named by the environment variable `DILLA_WEB_DIST`, default `../../packages/web/dist`, through `os.DirFS`. So `go test -tags webdist ./internal/web/...` is green both in `web-build` (the default directory, right after the build) and in `go-release` (`DILLA_WEB_DIST` = the downloaded `internal/web/dist`), and the untagged module-wide run never sees a real build.

This page never asks for a password." (task 11 writes the two template lines out exactly).
```json
{"v":1,"files":[{"path":"assets/index-AbC123.js","sha256":"<64 lowercase hex>","size":12345},{"path":"index.html","sha256":"…","size":678}]}
```

One line, `JSON.stringify` of that object plus a trailing newline. `files` lists every regular file under the directory except the manifest itself, with forward-slash relative paths, sorted by `path` in byte order. `web.New` fails when a listed file is missing, when a size or SHA-256 differs, when a file exists that is not listed, when `index.html` is not listed, or when `v` is not 1. ### L-GW — gateway

**L-GW-01 `SeedGateway`** (`internal/ds/seed.go`; C12)

```go
// SeedGateway rebuilds the gateway's fan-out list and leaf map for every open group from
// mls_members, so a restarted instance delivers group frames and elects committers before the
// group's next commit. It returns how many groups it seeded. A nil gateway seeds nothing.
func (d *DS) SeedGateway(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
```

It pages `Store.ListOpenGroups(ctx, after, 256)` to the end; for each group reads `Store.ListMembers` and, from the rows whose `RemovedEpoch` is nil, calls `Gateway.SetGroupMembers(groupID, devices)` and `Gateway.SetGroupLeaves(groupID, leaves)` with the same device order and leaf map `replaceMembersTx` would have produced (`internal/ds/registry.go:338`). `(*DS).Start` calls it before it starts the watchdog and returns its error. A store error aborts start-up; it is not logged and skipped.

**L-GW-02 gateway behaviours the client relies on** (existing; `interfaces.md` A4; nothing here changes server code)

- Connect: `POST /v1/gateway/ticket` then `new WebSocket(url, ['dilla.v1', 'dilla.ticket.<ticket>'])`, binary frames only; the server echoes `dilla.v1`. A same-host page passes the Origin check.
- Frame: `[op uint, n uint, group_id b16|null, payload array]`. First server frame is `hello` (op 0) `[wire[], e2ee[], media[], heartbeat_ms, max_frame_bytes, instance_id, generation, backoff_ms, backoff_jitter_ms]`; the client answers `identify` (op 1, `n = 1`) `["", 1, 1, 1, 0]` (`caps` is a uint, `protocol/02-delivery-service.md:157` and the `identify` vector of `frames.json`) and waits for `ready` (op 3) `[device_id, user_id, generation, resume_token, wire, e2ee, media, keypackages_remaining, groups[[group_id, epoch, last_seq, proposals_outstanding]]]`.
- Client frames sent: `identify` (1), `heartbeat` (6) `[last_n, 1]`, `commit_ack` (12) `[round]` with `group_id` set. Never `resume` (2), `subscribe` (10) or `unsubscribe` (11).
- Server frames handled: 7 `heartbeat_ack`, 8 `reconnect [reason, after_ms]`, 9 `error [cid, code, detail]`, 5 `invalid_session`, 16 `mls.handshake [seq, epoch, kind, sender|null, blob]`, 17 `mls.commit_needed [epoch, proposal_refs, deadline_ms, round]`, 18 `mls.epoch_changed [epoch, seq]`, 19 `message.ct [seq, epoch, uploader_device, blob, franking_tag, recv_ts]`, 20 `mls.welcome [welcome_id, epoch, commit_seq, blob, ratchet_tree, tree_hash]`, 21 `message.deleted [seq, deleted_at]`. Every other op is ignored.
- Close codes: 4004 `session_revoked` means the token is gone (re-establish; a **confirmed** 401 on establish — L-TS-06 — means the device is revoked or unknown); every other close is a reconnect. A browser cannot close a socket with 1002 or 1009 (`WebSocket.close` throws `InvalidAccessError` for any code but 1000 and 3000–4999), so the client closes with codes of its own in **4100–4199**, a range protocol/02 "Close codes" reserves for client-initiated closes in task 10 (`CLIENT_CLOSE`, L-TS-04); they carry no meaning for the instance.
- After task 10 a quiet group delivers live frames after a restart; the client still catches every group up over HTTP on every `ready` (frames fanned out between `ready` and registration are lost either way).

### L-TS — `@dilla/client-core`

**L-TS-01 CBOR codec** (`src/cbor/index.ts`; C20)

```ts
export type CborValue = bigint | Uint8Array | string | null | CborValue[];
export type CborInput = number | bigint | Uint8Array | string | null | readonly CborInput[];
export type CborErrorCode = 'E_CBOR_TRUNCATED' | 'E_CBOR_TRAILING' | 'E_CBOR_TYPE' | 'E_CBOR_NONCANONICAL'
  | 'E_CBOR_UTF8' | 'E_CBOR_DEPTH' | 'E_CBOR_RANGE' | 'E_CBOR_SHAPE';
export class CborError extends Error { readonly code: CborErrorCode; }
export const MAX_DEPTH = 8;
export function encode(value: CborInput): Uint8Array;
export function decode(bytes: Uint8Array): CborValue;
export function arr(v: CborValue, length?: number): CborValue[];   // E_CBOR_SHAPE on anything else
export function u64(v: CborValue): bigint;
export function u53(v: CborValue): number;                           // E_CBOR_RANGE above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
export function bin(v: CborValue, length?: number): Uint8Array;
export function str(v: CborValue): string;
export function opt<T>(v: CborValue, read: (v: CborValue) => T): T | null;
```

`decode` accepts exactly the dilla subset and nothing else: major types 0 (unsigned), 2 (definite byte string), 3 (definite text, valid UTF-8 checked with `TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true })`), 4 (definite array) and the simple value `null` (0xf6). It rejects: major 1, 5, 6, 7 other than 0xf6 (`E_CBOR_TYPE`); indefinite lengths (`E_CBOR_TYPE`); a non-shortest integer or length head (`E_CBOR_NONCANONICAL`); nesting deeper than 8 arrays (`E_CBOR_DEPTH`); input that ends early (`E_CBOR_TRUNCATED`); bytes after the first item (`E_CBOR_TRAILING`). Every unsigned integer decodes to `bigint`. `encode` writes shortest heads; a `number` must be a non-negative safe integer and a `bigint` in `0..2^64-1` (`E_CBOR_RANGE` otherwise); nesting deeper than 8 is `E_CBOR_DEPTH`. Tested against every `cases[].frame` and `rejects[].frame` of `protocol/vectors/frames.json` and every `cases[].cbor` of `protocol/vectors/envelope.json` (decode then encode is byte-identical).

**L-TS-02 HTTP client** (`src/http/client.ts`, `errors.ts`, `pacing.ts`)

```ts
export type Bucket = 'read' | 'write' | 'message' | 'commit' | 'proposal' | 'none';
export interface HttpRequest {
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';
  path: string;                       // starts with '/'
  body?: Uint8Array;                  // CBOR; sent with Content-Type: application/cbor
  bucket: Bucket;
  idempotent: boolean;
  auth?: boolean;                     // default true
  accept?: string;                    // sets the Accept header
  ok?: readonly number[];             // default [200, 201, 204]
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}
export interface HttpResponse { status: number; body: Uint8Array; }
export class DillaHttpError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;            // 0 for a network failure
  readonly code: string;              // the E_* of the error array; 'E_HTTP' when the body is not a dilla error array; 'E_NETWORK'
  readonly detail: string;
  readonly retryAfterMs: number | null;
  readonly extra: CborValue[];        // elements after the third (winning commit, proposal refs, rule)
}
export interface HttpDeps {
  baseUrl: string;                                             // the page origin
  fetch: typeof fetch;
  now(): number;                                               // ms
  sleep(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
  random(): number;                                            // [0, 1)
  token(): string | null;
  reauthenticate(): Promise<boolean>;                          // true: a new token is in place
  onGeneration(generation: bigint): void;                      // from X-Dilla-Generation
}
export class HttpClient { constructor(deps: HttpDeps); request(r: HttpRequest): Promise<HttpResponse>; }
export const RETRY = { maxAttempts: 5, baseMs: 500, capMs: 8000, jitterMs: 250, maxWaitMs: 60000 } as const;
export const PACING = {                                        // 80 % of interfaces.md A2.9, per device
  read: { perSecond: 8, burst: 48 }, write: { perSecond: 1.6, burst: 16 },
  message: { perSecond: 0.8, burst: 16 }, commit: { perSecond: 1.6, burst: 32 },
  proposal: { perSecond: 0.4, burst: 8 },
} as const;
```

Behaviour. Before each attempt the request waits for a token of its bucket (`none` never waits). A status in `ok` resolves. Any other status is decoded as `[code, detail, retry_after_ms|null, …extra]`; a body that is not that shape (the mux's `text/plain` 404/405, a proxy page) gives `code = 'E_HTTP'`, `detail = ''`. `401` on a request with `auth !== false`: call `reauthenticate()` once per request; `true` retries with the new token, `false` throws. A `401` on an `auth: false` request throws at once and never calls `reauthenticate()` (challenge and establish are `auth: false`, and `reauthenticate` is wired to `Session.establish()`: the other reading recurses or deadlocks the single-flight establish). `429` and `503`: wait `retry_after_ms` (body; else the `Retry-After` header in seconds; else 1000), throw instead when the wait exceeds `maxWaitMs`, then retry, for any verb (the server stored nothing). `500` and a network failure: retry only when `idempotent`, after `min(capMs, baseMs × 2^attempt) + random() × jitterMs`. `501` and every other status: throw at once. `409 E_COMMIT_CONFLICT` and `425 E_COMMIT_REQUIRED` are **not** retried here (L-TS-07 owns them). At most `maxAttempts` attempts in total. An aborted `signal` rejects with the `AbortError`.

**L-TS-03 `CorePort`** (`src/core-port.ts`): the typed face of `CoreHandle`. `wrapCore(handle: CoreHandle): CorePort` is the only code that calls a handle method; it decodes results with L-TS-01 and converts thrown errors to `CoreError`.

`CoreHandle` here is **not** the generated class. The `node` CI job lints (type-aware) with no wasm build, and `packages/core-wasm/pkg/` is git-ignored, so an `import type … from '@dilla/core-wasm'` would resolve to an error type there and trip the `no-unsafe-*` rules. `src/core-port.ts` therefore declares `export interface CoreHandle` structurally (the members of L-WASM-05 without `free`) and `export interface CoreWasmModule` (the free functions the client uses: `core_open`, `StoreOpenConfig`, `is_sah_contention`, `probe_persistence`); `src/core-wasm-conformance.ts` is the only file of the package that names `@dilla/core-wasm` and holds nothing but two type-level assertions that the generated class and module are assignable to them, so `npm run typecheck -w @dilla/client-core` (which needs the wasm build) fails when the generated surface drifts from L-WASM-05. The worker loads the wasm through a dynamic `import()` cast to `CoreWasmModule & { default(): Promise<unknown> }` (`src/worker/runtime.ts`).

Two doubles, one per half, and no overlap. `src/testing/fake-core.ts` (task 15) exports `class FakeCore implements CorePort`, the **account half** only (identity phases, signup, session record, device list flags, KeyPackages, pause/resume/close), with `FAKE_RECOVERY_KEY`, `new FakeCore(opts?: { deviceId?: Id; tier?: number; idSeed?: number })`, `FakeCore.identified({ instanceId, userId, deviceId, username, tier?, listPublished? })`, `calls: string[]` and `failOnce(method, error)`; every group, commit, send, outbox and timeline method throws `CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'not modelled')`. `src/sync/testing/model.ts` (task 16) exports `ModelCore implements CorePort`, the **group half** per L-CORE-07…09 (its account half throws the same `not modelled` error), and `ModelDs`, a modelled delivery service; `ModelCore` is held to the Rust core by L-CORE-10. Neither file is exported from `src/index.ts`.

Error codes this layer adds, all shown raw and all ending in `AccountState.phase = 'error'` when they reach boot: `E_CORE_DECODE` (a core result that is not the documented CBOR shape), `E_CORE_WASM` (a throw from the wasm glue that is not a `ClientError` rendering: a panic's `RuntimeError`, wasm-bindgen's "null pointer passed to rust").

**L-TS-04 gateway client** (`src/gateway/gateway.ts`, `frames.ts`; C19)

```ts
export interface Frame { op: number; n: bigint; groupId: Uint8Array | null; payload: CborValue[]; }
export function encodeFrame(op: number, n: number, groupId: Uint8Array | null, payload: readonly CborInput[]): Uint8Array;
export function decodeFrame(bytes: Uint8Array): Frame;          // CborError, or Error('E_FRAME_SHAPE'); an opcode outside the table passes
                                                                 // the envelope checks only (the client ignores unknown opcodes; E_FRAME_TYPE is the server's refusal)
export const CLIENT_CLOSE = { normal: 1000, version: 4006, helloTimeout: 4100, heartbeatTimeout: 4101,
  undecodable: 4102, tooLarge: 4109 } as const;                 // 41xx never collides with the server's 4000–4010; 4006 reuses its meaning
export const Op = { hello: 0, identify: 1, ready: 3, invalidSession: 5, heartbeat: 6, heartbeatAck: 7, reconnect: 8, error: 9,
  commitAck: 12, handshake: 16, commitNeeded: 17, epochChanged: 18, messageCt: 19, welcome: 20, messageDeleted: 21 } as const;
export type GatewayStatus = 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'ready' | 'waiting';
export interface ReadyInfo { deviceId: Uint8Array; userId: Uint8Array; generation: bigint; keypackagesRemaining: number;
  groups: { groupId: Uint8Array; epoch: bigint; lastSeq: bigint; proposalsOutstanding: number }[];
  heartbeatMs: number; maxFrameBytes: number; backoffMs: number; backoffJitterMs: number; }
export type GatewayEvent =
  | { type: 'status'; status: GatewayStatus; closeCode: number | null }
  | { type: 'ready'; info: ReadyInfo }
  | { type: 'frame'; frame: Frame }                            // ops 16–21 only
  | { type: 'revoked' };                                       // close 4004, or a ticket mint refused with 401
export interface GatewayDeps {
  url: string;                                                 // ws(s)://<page host>/gateway
  mintTicket(): Promise<string>;
  WebSocket: typeof WebSocket;
  now(): number; random(): number;
  setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): number; clearTimeout(id: number): void;
}
export class Gateway {
  constructor(deps: GatewayDeps);
  start(): void; stop(): void;
  subscribe(listener: (e: GatewayEvent) => void): () => void;
  commitAck(groupId: Uint8Array, round: bigint): void;         // dropped unless status is 'ready'
  readonly status: GatewayStatus;
}
export const GATEWAY = { heartbeatMaxMs: 15000, ackTimeoutMs: 10000, helloTimeoutMs: 15000,
  reconnectBaseMs: 500, reconnectCapMs: 30000, reconnectJitterMs: 500 } as const;
```

Behaviour. `start` mints a ticket, opens the socket with `binaryType = 'arraybuffer'`, expects `hello` within `helloTimeoutMs` and then `ready` within the same bound re-armed after `identify` (a server that says hello and then nothing must not hang the client until its 65 s grace), refuses a hello whose three version arrays do not each contain 1 (stop and report status `idle` with close code `CLIENT_CLOSE.version`), sends `identify`, and emits `ready` when op 3 arrives. Heartbeat every `min(heartbeat_ms / 2, heartbeatMaxMs)` with the highest `n` seen; a missing `heartbeat_ack` within `ackTimeoutMs` closes the socket with `CLIENT_CLOSE.heartbeatTimeout`. A message larger than `max_frame_bytes` closes it with `CLIENT_CLOSE.tooLarge`, one that does not decode with `CLIENT_CLOSE.undecodable`, a missing hello or ready with `CLIENT_CLOSE.helloTimeout`. The status event's `closeCode` is the code the client sent when the client closed the socket, the server's code otherwise. On any close, `invalid_session` or `reconnect`: status `waiting`, then reconnect after `max(after_ms, min(reconnectCapMs, reconnectBaseMs × 2^failures) + random() × reconnectJitterMs)`; `failures` resets on `ready`. Close 4004 emits `revoked` and does not reconnect (the account layer re-establishes and calls `start`). A ticket that fails to mint counts as a failure and is retried the same way, **except a mint rejected with a `DillaHttpError` whose `status` is 401**: the HTTP layer has already tried `reauthenticate()` and it answered `false`, so the device cannot establish; the gateway treats it as close 4004 (status `idle`, emit `revoked`, no reconnect). Without this a device revoked while its socket is down retries for ever and never reaches the `revoked` splash. `stop` closes with 1000 and cancels every timer.

**L-TS-05 device KEK** (`src/account/kek.ts`; C7)

```ts
export interface KekStore { load(instanceHex: string): Promise<Uint8Array | null>; create(instanceHex: string): Promise<Uint8Array>; remove(instanceHex: string): Promise<void>; }
export function indexedDbKekStore(idb: IDBFactory, subtle: SubtleCrypto, getRandomValues: (a: Uint8Array) => Uint8Array): KekStore;
export const KEK_DB = 'dilla-device'; export const KEK_DB_VERSION = 1; export const KEK_STORE = 'kek';
```

IndexedDB database `dilla-device` version 1, one object store `kek` with out-of-line keys. The record under key `<instance id, 32 hex>` is `{ v: 1, wrapKey: CryptoKey, iv: Uint8Array(12), ct: Uint8Array(48) }`: `wrapKey = subtle.generateKey({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt'])` (non-extractable), `ct = AES-GCM(wrapKey, iv, kek, additionalData = UTF-8 "dilla kek v1" ‖ instance_id)`, `kek` 32 random bytes. `create` fails with `Error('E_KEK_EXISTS')` when a record exists. `load` returns the 32 bytes or `null`; a record that fails to decrypt throws `Error('E_KEK_UNWRAP')`. The caller hex-encodes the KEK for `StoreOpenConfig`, and zero-fills the byte array as soon as `core_open` settles. The store lives at OPFS directory `dilla/<instance hex>`, database name `dilla.db`, and the worker calls `reserve_capacity(16)` after opening.

**L-TS-06 account** (`src/account/boot.ts`, `signup.ts`, `session.ts`, `keypackages.ts`)

```ts

  | { kind: 'store-lost' }                                     // an OPFS database exists and the KEK record does not, or the key is refused
  | { kind: 'opened'; core: CorePort; instance: Instance };
export interface OpenedStore { core: CorePort; reserveCapacity(n: number): Promise<void>; }
export interface BootDeps {

  probePersistence(): Promise<string>;
  storeExists(directory: string): Promise<boolean>;
  kek: KekStore;
  openCore(directory: string, dbName: string, kekHex: string): Promise<OpenedStore>;
}
export const STORE_DB_NAME = 'dilla.db'; export const RESERVE_CAPACITY = 16;
export function boot(deps: BootDeps): Promise<BootOutcome>;
/** The real wiring: a fresh StoreOpenConfig per attempt, contention retried on the spike's schedule. */
export function wasmCoreOpener(mod: CoreWasmModule, sleep: (ms: number) => Promise<void>): BootDeps['openCore'];
export function opfsDirectoryExists(root: FileSystemDirectoryHandle, path: string): Promise<boolean>;
export class Session {
  constructor(deps: { core: CorePort; routes: Routes; now(): number });
  token(): string | null;
  /** Challenge + establish with purpose 0. false only for a CONFIRMED 401 (see below). Single-flight. */
  establish(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** establish() when there is no token, or it expires or idles out within RENEW_MARGIN_S. */
  ensure(): Promise<boolean>;
}
export const RENEW_MARGIN_S = 3600;
export class Signup {
  constructor(deps: { core: CorePort; routes: Routes; session: Session; now(): number });
  begin(instanceId: Id): string[];                                               // the recovery key as 13 groups of 4
  submit(input: { invite: string; username: string; display: string; password: string | null }): Promise<void>;
  /** After a reload in phase 1: establish; on success complete (2). On a confirmed 401: with no stored
   *  session record the registration never happened — reset (0); with one, the account exists and its
   *  device key is never destroyed — 'revoked'. */
  resume(): Promise<0 | 2 | 'revoked'>;
}

export function refillKeyPackages(core: CorePort, routes: Routes, remaining: number, limits: { perDevice: number; threshold: number }): Promise<number>;
```

**What one 401 from establish proves: nothing.** The server answers the same empty `401 E_UNAUTHENTICATED` for a nonce it no longer holds (nonces are in memory, single use, 60 s — a frozen tab or a restart between challenge and establish loses it), for any error of its device lookup including a transient store error, for a revoked row and for a bad signature (`internal/auth/session.go:335-362`). So `Session.establish()` treats the first 401 from `postSession` as inconclusive and runs challenge + establish **once more with a fresh nonce**; only a second consecutive 401 is a confirmed one and resolves `false`. On a confirmed 401 it calls `core.sessionClear()` **only when the identity phase is 2**; in phase 1 the session record is the only proof that `POST /v1/accounts` succeeded, and it is kept. A scope other than 0 rejects with `Error('E_SESSION_SCOPE')` and stores nothing. `Signup.resume()` in phase 1: `establish()` true → `getAccountMe`, `signupComplete`, publish, refill → 2; confirmed false and `core.session() === null` → `core.signupReset()` → 0; confirmed false and a session record exists → `'revoked'`, nothing is deleted (the core would refuse the reset anyway, L-CORE-06). Residual, accepted: an instance that answers two false 401s in a row to a browser whose registration response was lost makes that browser start over while its username stays taken.

`boot` classifies a failed open narrowly, because `store-lost` offers a reset and in web-1 a reset is the permanent loss of the account: `store-lost` only when (a) an OPFS database exists and the KEK record does not, (b) `KekStore.load` throws `E_KEK_UNWRAP`, or (c) `openCore` rejects with a message that starts `E_STORE_KEY` **and** contains SQLite's wrong-key text `file is not a database`. Any other rejection, including any other `E_STORE_KEY` (the code raises it for every failure of the first read, `core/dilla-core-wasm/src/store.rs:125-128`, for example `unable to open database file`), propagates and ends in the `error` phase, whose splash offers a reload and no reset.

`Signup.submit` order: `signupRequest` → `postAccount` (never retried by the HTTP layer; a thrown `DillaHttpError` propagates unchanged and the phase stays 1) → `sessionStore` of the returned token (`idle_expires = expires`) → `signupComplete(userId, username, now)` → `publishDeviceList` → `refillKeyPackages(…, 0, …)`. `publishDeviceList`: no-op when `listPublished`; `putDeviceList`; on `409` read `getDeviceList` and treat a `version` of 1 or more as published, else rethrow; then `deviceListPublished()`. `refillKeyPackages`: when `remaining < threshold` publish `perDevice - remaining` packages (first publish, `remaining = 0`: `perDevice` packages with `lastResort = true`), returning how many were sent; the count is clamped to 32 (`key_packages` refuses more). `publishDeviceList` lives in `src/account/signup.ts`, `refillKeyPackages` in `src/account/keypackages.ts`. The username rule (3..32 of `a-z 0-9 . _ -`, no leading or trailing `.`) and display limit (≤ 64 characters) are validated by the page before `submit`, and the 4000-**byte** body limit by the composer (L-UI-13); the server and the core are still the authority.

**L-TS-07 sync engine** (`src/sync/engine.ts`, `group-queue.ts`, `channel.ts`, `send.ts`; C1's TypeScript half)

```ts
// Structural views, so a test can pass a modelled delivery service and a scripted gateway (a class with
// a private member is not structurally satisfiable). `keyof` of a class lists public members only, so the
// real Routes and Gateway stay assignable and task 18's composition root is unaffected.
export type SyncRoutes = Pick<Routes, 'listChannels' | 'postGroup' | 'getGroupInfo' | 'getGroupTree' | 'getHandshakes'
  | 'getMessages' | 'getProposals' | 'postCommit' | 'postMessage' | 'postCursor' | 'postResync' | 'getWelcomes' | 'deleteWelcome'>;
export type SyncGateway = Pick<Gateway, 'subscribe' | 'commitAck'>;
export interface SyncDeps { core: CorePort; routes: SyncRoutes; gateway: SyncGateway; instance: Instance; deviceId: Id;
  now(): number; random(): number; setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): number; clearTimeout(id: number): void;
  onGroupChanged(groupId: Id, result: ApplyResult): void; onOutboxChanged(groupId: Id): void;
  /** Called when a resync starts and when it is refused; success is reported by onGroupChanged with state 2. */
  onMembership(groupId: Id, status: 'resyncing' | 'not-member'): void; }
// src/sync/errors.ts, re-exported from engine.ts: the errors the engine raises itself.
export class SyncError extends Error {
  readonly code: 'E_SYNC_STOPPED' | 'E_REGISTER_RACE' | 'E_CHANNEL_GONE' | 'E_NO_COMMUNITY'; readonly detail: string; }
export class SyncEngine {
  constructor(deps: SyncDeps);
  start(): void; stop(): void;
  /** Channels the page knows, so Welcomes can be matched and channels opened. Replaces the previous set. */
  setChannels(channels: ExpectedGroup[]): void;
  /** Ensures the device is in the channel's text group: adopt a Welcome, else external join, else register. */
  openChannel(channel: { communityId: Id; channelId: Id; textGroupId: Id | null }): Promise<{ groupId: Id; state: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 }>;
  send(groupId: Id, text: string): Id;
  retry(msgId: Id): void; discard(msgId: Id): void;

export const SYNC = { handshakePage: 512, messagePage: 256, commitRetryMax: 5, commitJitterMs: 400,
  membershipWaitMs: 2000, echoWaitMs: 5000, registerRetryMax: 3, cursorDebounceMs: 30000 } as const;
```

Rules (each is a test in task 16):

1. *One serial queue per group.* Every core call and every HTTP call about a group runs on that group's queue; two groups run concurrently.
2. *Catch-up on every `ready`* (C12, C19): `welcomes` first (`getWelcomes` until a short page → `welcomesApply` with the known channels → `deleteWelcome` for outcome 0, and for outcome 1 **only when the group's row is in state 2**; a Welcome for a row in state 0 or 1 stays on the server, because the external join in flight may still be refused and the Welcome is then the way in — `DELETE /v1/welcomes/{id}` is "only after a successful join"). Outcomes 2 and 3 leave the Welcome on the server, whatever the reason (since the hardening a Welcome at or below the epoch floor, one whose epoch or tree hash differs from its served label (`3f26670`) and one for a row bound to another channel are outcome 2 too); it is judged again at the next welcome step until the server expires it. Then every group in state 2 is caught up.

   *The `through` computation.* Handshakes and messages share one sequence space, are read by two requests, and the two reads are not a snapshot: a row stored between them must never be skipped. `through` may therefore only name a seq that **both** streams are known to be complete up to. One catch-up keeps `carry: bigint | null`, the highest handshake seq seen in an earlier round (null in the first). Each round, with `from = nextSeq`: read **messages first** (`m` = its `lastSeq`), **then handshakes** (`h` = its `lastSeq`); a page is full when its `count` equals its page size. `boundM = m` when the message page is full, else `max(m ?? 0, carry ?? 0)` (a short message page holds every message that existed when it was read, and that was after the earlier round's handshake read). `boundH = h` when the handshake page is full, else `max(h ?? 0, m ?? 0)` (a short handshake page holds every handshake that existed when it was read, and that was after this round's message read). `through = min(boundM, boundH)`. `groupApply(g, hs.raw, ms.raw, through)` only when `through >= nextSeq`; then `carry = h`. Another round runs while the group is still in state 2 and (a page was full, or `h !== null && h > through`); otherwise the catch-up ends. Cost: two reads when only messages are new (the common case), four when a handshake is new. Taking the highest `lastSeq` instead skips, for good, a row stored between the two reads: with handshakes read first, a commit (the message of its epoch is then stored unreadable, `next_seq` passes the commit, and the live frame for it is dropped as old); with messages read first, a message that sits below a later handshake. Task 16 has two tests, "a message stored between the two reads, below a later commit, is not skipped" and "a commit stored between the two reads is applied before the message of its epoch", and shows the first red under the mutation "through = the highest `lastSeq`".

   After the last round, when the group is still in state 2: `cursorBody` → `postCursor` → `cursorAcked`. `410 E_PRUNED` on either stream → the group goes to resync (rule 7).
3. *Live frames.* Frames for a group in state 0 or 1 are held and replayed after it becomes active. Op 16 and op 19 are normalised to the row shapes of L-CORE-08 (op 19: `commitment = null`, `deleted = 0`). A frame with `seq == nextSeq` is applied with `through = seq`; `seq < nextSeq` is dropped; `seq > nextSeq` triggers a catch-up of that group. Op 21 (`message.deleted [seq, deleted_at]`) for a group that is not in state 4 runs `messageDeleted(g, seq)` on the group's queue and reports the result through `onGroupChanged`; the delivery service fans op 21 only for the uploader's own deletes, so no author rule is needed, and a message deleted before this device first fetched it arrives as a row with `deleted = 1` instead (L-CORE-08 rule 2). Type-2 delete envelopes are web-2. Op 20 is normalised to a welcomes row and goes through `welcomesApply`. Op 18 carries nothing the rows do not. *Cursor after live frames:* after a live `groupApply` the engine arms one timer per group of `cursorDebounceMs` (re-arming does not extend a running timer) that runs `cursorBody` → `postCursor` → `cursorAcked` on the group's queue; a catch-up of the group cancels it (it posts the cursor itself). Without it a session that stays connected for days never moves the server's retention floor.
4. *Commit duty.* On op 17 for a group in state 2: `commitAck(group, round)` at once, then commit. Op 17 for a group that is not in state 2 is neither acknowledged nor held (it is never replayed, and an unacknowledged round only advances the election; the volunteer path covers the proposals once the group is active). On a `ready` whose row has `proposalsOutstanding > 0`, and after any `groupApply` that leaves `proposalsPending > 0`, with no op 17 within `backoff_ms + random() × backoff_jitter_ms`: volunteer a commit. Commit = `getProposals` → `commitBuild` → `postCommit` → `commitConfirm`. `409 E_COMMIT_CONFLICT` → `commitAbort`, catch up, and when proposals are still pending retry after `random() × commitJitterMs`, at most `commitRetryMax` times. The catch-ups that the commit path itself runs do not arm the volunteer timer, and a group whose retries are exhausted is commit-quiet (no volunteer) until the next `ready` or the next op 17 for it; otherwise the volunteer rule would re-arm a commit after every capped attempt and the cap would end nothing. `425`, `403 E_LEAF_NOT_CURRENT`, `422` → `commitAbort` and catch up (403 → rule 7). A `422 E_COMMIT_INVALID` (whatever its rule: `structural`, `group_info` (hardening G), `add_key_package`, …) is a permanent refusal of that commit, never retried in a loop: after the catch-up the group is commit-quiet, as after exhausted conflict retries, until the next `ready` or op 17 for it. Any other failure → `commitAbort`.
5. *Sending.* `send` = `sendPrepare`, then the group's queue drains its outbox oldest first, one row at a time: `sendEncrypt` → `postMessage` → `sendConfirm`. `sendEncrypt` refusing with `E_CORE_STATE` is not a failure of the row; the engine reads the group's row from `core.groups()` and: `pendingCommit` → return (the commit path in flight requests a drain when it confirms or aborts); `proposalsPending > 0` → run the commit duty for the group now (this is the normal state right after someone joined, and the 425 path below would never be reached because the core refuses first), and request a drain after it, whatever its outcome; a commit-quiet group requests the drain on the next epoch change instead; otherwise (another row in flight, or the group not active) → return. Any other `CoreError` from `sendEncrypt` → `sendFail(code)`. `425 E_COMMIT_REQUIRED` → `sendRequeue`, run the commit duty (or wait for the epoch to change, at most `membershipWaitMs`), retry. `403 E_LEAF_NOT_CURRENT` → `sendRequeue`, rule 7. `429`/`503` are already retried by the HTTP layer; when it gives up → `sendFail(code)`. A network failure or `500` after the request left: **do not resend**; catch the group up; if the row is no longer in the outbox it was adopted and is done; otherwise wait `echoWaitMs`, catch up once more, then `sendRequeue` and retry. `413`, `422`, `404` and every other refusal → `sendFail(code)`. A `CoreError` from `sendConfirm` → no `sendFail` and no `sendRequeue` (at a seq that holds another row the core has already failed the row with error `E_CORE_STATE`, L-CORE-09): report the outbox change, catch up, drain on. *Since the hardening (`410c543`) a catch-up can adopt any unresolved outbox row whose upload the server stored — queued, in flight or failed —, so after every apply that reports `ownAdopted` the engine re-reads `outbox(g)` and assumes nothing about a row it held before (a failed row may be gone, a requeued row may be gone).*
6. *Opening a channel.* `textGroupId` set and a local group in state 2 → done. `textGroupId` set and no local group (a row of the group in state 4 counts as none: a rejoin over it keeps its history, and a discarded rejoin returns it to state 4): run the welcome step of rule 2; still none → `getGroupInfo` + `getGroupTree` → `groupJoinExternal` → `postResync` → `groupJoined`. `groupJoinExternal` refusing with `E_CORE_INPUT` (the two reads straddled a commit, which a re-read cures; or the GroupInfo names another group, or it would rejoin at or below an epoch this device has held, which a re-read does not cure while the server serves the same state) → re-read info and tree and call it again; such a refusal writes nothing and counts as one join against the budget below, and when the budget is spent that `CoreError` propagates (pre-flight ruling, task 16; bounded so a refusal that survives every re-read ends the call). Any other `CoreError` from `groupJoinExternal` (`E_CORE_STATE`: a join in progress, the row bound to another channel, another group holding the channel) propagates at once. A refused `postResync` → `groupDiscard`, then: `425 E_COMMIT_REQUIRED` → wait `membershipWaitMs` and start again from the welcome step; `409 E_COMMIT_CONFLICT` (the join raced another member's commit) → start again at once with a fresh info and tree; every join attempt (a `postResync`, or a `groupJoinExternal` refused with `E_CORE_INPUT`) counts against one budget of `commitRetryMax` joins per `openChannel` call, after which the last refusal propagates. Every other refusal propagates at once (`403` means the account may not join). *Why 425 is handled (pre-flight ruling, task 16):* the delivery service holds an external join while one of its proposals is outstanding; today a community join adds nobody to a channel that can carry a group (`internal/api/communities.go:432-441`, `private.go:213-219`) — the joiner enters by external commit — so the handling is defence against a later dillad that proposes the joiner's Add, not the expected path right after a community join. `textGroupId` null → `groupCreate` with a fresh random id → `postGroup` → `groupRegistered`; `409 E_GROUP_EXISTS` → `groupDiscard`, re-read the channel with `listChannels`, and continue from the top, at most `registerRetryMax` times (then `SyncError('E_REGISTER_RACE')`; a channel that is no longer listed is `SyncError('E_CHANNEL_GONE')`). Any other refusal of `postGroup` → `groupDiscard` and propagate, never retried: in particular `400 E_INVALID_REQUEST`, which the delivery service answers when the registered group is not exactly one leaf of this device under its registered key, or when the device is not in its user's newest signed device list (hardening G). The core's `group_create` always builds a one-leaf group of this device, and the engine is started only after the account's device list v1 is published (L-TS-09 enter ready: `publishDeviceList` precedes `SyncEngine.start`, and `openChannel` is a command of the `ready` phase only), so the engine does not check the list itself; a `400` here is a server-side state the engine cannot repair. Likewise a `422 E_COMMIT_INVALID` from `postResync` (rule `external_joiner` or `group_info`, hardening G) is "every other refusal": it propagates from an open and is a refused resync under rule 7. `send` and `openChannel` after `stop()` reject with `SyncError('E_SYNC_STOPPED')`.
7. *Resync.* A group in state 3 (from `groupApply`), or one that met `E_LEAF_NOT_CURRENT` or `E_PRUNED`: `onMembership(g, 'resyncing')`, then the external join of rule 6 over the existing id (no 425 wait and no 409 restart; an `E_CORE_INPUT` from `groupJoinExternal` is re-read at most `commitRetryMax` times in all). A refusal — including a GroupInfo below the epoch floor, which survives every re-read — leaves it in state 3 (a refused `postResync` is followed by `groupDiscard`, which returns a resync row to state 3) and calls `onMembership(g, 'not-member')`; background triggers retry at most once per `ready`.

```ts
export const TIMELINE_PAGE = 100;
```

A timeline holds stored rows of `type` 0 and status 0/1/2 (rows of envelope types 1–6 are kept in the database and not shown in web-1), followed by the group's outbox rows (`pending` for outbox states 0 and 1, `failed` for 2). `web` is `senderTier == 1`, `bot` is `senderKind == 1`. A channel of `mode` 1 or `kind` other than 0 has `group: 'unsupported'`. `channels:<id>` holds every row the server lists, in the server's order, **categories included** (`kind: 2`, `internal/api/channels.go:22-24`), and `parentId` is passed through; the page never lists a category as a channel and orders children under their category. `ChannelGroupState` is derived from the group's row and from what `onMembership` last reported for it: `resync` while a resync runs, `not-member` after a refused one or a 403 on open. `ConnectionState.status` is `connecting` from `gateway.start()` until the first `ready` or the first `waiting`; `online` on `ready`; **`offline` from a `waiting` until the next `ready`** (so the reconnect banner shows while the connection is down and does not flicker between attempts) and for `idle`. `ConnectionState.reason` is `'version'` only while the gateway is `idle` after closing with `CLIENT_CLOSE.version` (4006, the server refused this client's version; the gateway does not reconnect): the controller sets it with `status: 'offline'` on that idle, any other idle publishes `offline` without it, and the next `connecting` or `online` drops it (controller ruling amending L-TS-08, task 24 fix round 6).

**L-TS-09 worker protocol** (`src/worker/protocol.ts`; the worker is created by `new Worker(new URL('./worker/entry.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module', name: 'dilla-core' })`)

```ts
export type Command =
  | { m: 'start' }
  | { m: 'signupBegin' }
  | { m: 'signupSubmit'; invite: string; username: string; display: string; password: string | null; recoveryKeyAcknowledged: true }
  | { m: 'signupReset' }
  | { m: 'resetDevice' }
  | { m: 'joinCommunity'; invite: string }
  | { m: 'selectCommunity'; communityId: string }
  | { m: 'openChannel'; channelId: string }
  | { m: 'closeChannel'; channelId: string }
  | { m: 'loadEarlier'; channelId: string }
  | { m: 'send'; channelId: string; text: string }
  | { m: 'retrySend'; msgId: string }
  | { m: 'discardSend'; msgId: string };
export type ToWorker = { t: 'call'; id: number; command: Command };
export type FromWorker =
  | { t: 'ret'; id: number; ok: true; value: unknown }
  | { t: 'ret'; id: number; ok: false; error: WorkerError }
  | { t: 'slice'; name: SliceName; rev: number; value: unknown };
/** Not part of ToWorker. Honoured only by a worker started with { testHooks: true }, which only
 *  packages/client-core/harness/worker.ts does; src/worker/entry.ts (what createCoreWorker() loads) passes false. */
export type TestHook = { t: 'test'; op: 'gateway-stop' | 'gateway-start' };
export const LOCK_PREFIX = 'dilla-core:';        // + instance id hex
```

Results: `joinCommunity` → `{ communityId: string }`, resolved only **after** the new `communities` slice was published (so a page that navigates to the new server finds it); `signupSubmit` → `{ communityId: string | null; joinError: WorkerError | null }` (below); `send` → `{ msgId: string }`; every other command → `null`. Error codes are a `DillaHttpError.code`, a `CoreError.code` (including `E_CORE_DECODE`, `E_CORE_WASM`), a `CborError.code`, a `SyncError.code` (`E_SYNC_STOPPED`, `E_REGISTER_RACE`, `E_CHANNEL_GONE`, `E_NO_COMMUNITY`), the account layer's `E_KEK_EXISTS`, `E_KEK_UNWRAP`, `E_SESSION_SCOPE`, or one of the controller's own: `E_INVITE_NOT_COMMUNITY` (the invite names no community), `E_BAD_INPUT` (a malformed id or an empty message), `E_NOT_READY` (a command the current phase does not accept; detail `the phase is <phase>`), `E_UNSUPPORTED` (`account.error.code` beside `phase: 'unsupported'`; detail = the probe's reason), `E_INTERNAL` (any other exception; its `message`, never a value that could hold a key, a token or a body). The bridge rejects a failed call with `class CoreCallError extends Error { readonly code; readonly detail; readonly status; readonly retryAfterMs }` (typescript-eslint forbids rejecting with a plain object); it is exported from the package root.

`signupSubmit` and the invite. `POST /v1/accounts` redeems the invite it is given and joins nothing (`internal/api/accounts.go:164-176`), so a person who signs up with a friend's server invite would land in an empty shell and have to paste the same invite again. The controller therefore: (1) when the invite is non-empty, calls `routes.getInvite(invite)` **before** `Signup.submit`: `E_INVITE_INVALID` fails the command there (nothing was registered, the phase returns to `signup-keys`); any other failure of this read is ignored and treated as "names no community" (the server stays the authority at registration); (2) runs `Signup.submit`; (3) after entering `ready`, when the invite named a community, runs the `joinCommunity` path for it and resolves `{ communityId: <hex>, joinError: null }`; a refused join resolves `{ communityId: null, joinError: <the error> }` — never a failed signup; with no community it resolves `{ communityId: null, joinError: null }`. Joining spends a second use of the invite (`internal/api/communities.go:462-491`), so a one-use server invite registers and then fails to join; that limit is a row of "Deferred". When `Signup.submit` throws after the core reached phase 2 (the account exists; publishing the device list or the KeyPackages failed), the controller does not return to `signup-keys`: it enters `ready`, which retries the publish; if that fails too the phase is `error` and the command rejects with that error.

Worker rules: `start` is idempotent; the worker fetches `/v1/instance`, then requests the Web Lock `dilla-core:<instance hex>` with `{ ifAvailable: true }`; without it the worker at once queues a plain `request` for the same lock and boots when it is granted, and publishes the phase `other-tab` only if the lock is still not held 1500 ms after the failed attempt (`LEADER.otherTabGraceMs = 1500`, a constant task 18's worker defines) — until then the phase stays `loading` (an in-place reload finds the lock still held by the dying worker of the old page, and must not flash "open in another tab"; pre-flight ruling 4, task 18). Holding the lock it runs `boot`, then by `identity().phase`: 0 → `needs-signup`; 1 → `Signup.resume()` (0 → `needs-signup`, 2 → enter ready, `'revoked'` → `revoked`); 2 → enter ready: `Session.ensure()` (false → `revoked`), `publishDeviceList`, `SyncEngine.start` **then** gateway `start` (so the engine is subscribed before the first `ready`; pre-flight ruling 2, task 18), load communities → `ready`. Durable storage is asked for by the **page**, not the worker (`StorageManager.persist()` is exposed on `Window` only): when the account phase first becomes `ready`, `@dilla/web`'s `App` calls `navigator.storage.persist()` once through its `browser` wrapper and ignores a refusal or a rejection — web-1 keeps the only copy of the device key in storage a browser may otherwise evict. **`revoked` has one path, whatever found it** — `sync.stop()`, `gateway.stop()`, `phase: 'revoked'` — and two ways in: the gateway's `revoked` event runs `Session.establish()` (`true` → `gateway.start()`; `false` → the path); and `HttpDeps.reauthenticate`, which is `Session.establish()`, runs the path itself whenever it resolves `false`, for whatever request asked. On every gateway `ready` the worker refreshes `communities` and the two slices of the selected community (a channel or a member added while the page was open appears without a reload), and a timeline row whose `senderUser` is not in the loaded member list re-runs `listMembers` for that community once per unknown user. `SyncDeps.onMembership` drives `ChannelGroupState` (L-TS-08). `rev` increases by one per slice name; the page ignores a slice whose `rev` is not greater than the one it holds. On `pagehide` the page posts nothing: the worker dies with the page and the lock is released by the browser (drafts are the only loss; every state change is already committed in its unit).

**L-TS-10 bridge** (`src/bridge.ts`, exported from `src/index.ts`)

```ts
export interface CoreClient {
  call<C extends Command>(command: C): Promise<unknown>;
  get<N extends SliceName>(name: N): SliceTypes[N] | undefined;
  subscribe(name: SliceName, listener: () => void): () => void;
  dispose(): void;
}
export function connectCore(worker: Worker): CoreClient;
export function createCoreWorker(): Worker;
```

`get` returns the same object identity until the slice changes (so `useSyncExternalStore` does not loop). `dispose` terminates the worker and rejects pending calls with `CoreCallError('E_DISPOSED')`. `src/index.ts` gains exactly five lines (specifiers extension-less, as task 12's `export * from './cbor';` is): `export { connectCore, createCoreWorker, CoreCallError } from './bridge';`, `export type { CoreClient } from './bridge';`, `export type * from './state/types';`, `export type { Command, ToWorker, FromWorker, TestHook } from './worker/protocol';` and `export { LOCK_PREFIX } from './worker/protocol';`. `@dilla/web` imports every state and command type from the package root.

### L-TS — `@dilla/web`

**L-TS-11 strings** (`src/strings/en.ts`, `index.ts`): `export const en = { … } as const` (flat keys, dot-separated names such as `'onboarding.identity.title'`); `export type StringKey = keyof typeof en`; `export function t(key: StringKey, vars?: Record<string, string | number>): string` replacing `{name}` placeholders and throwing on a missing variable; `export function formatTime(ts: number): string` and `formatDay(ts: number): string` on `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the browser locale. No component of `@dilla/web` contains a user-visible literal; a unit test greps `src/screens` for JSX text and fails on any.

**L-TS-12 core context** (`src/core/context.tsx`, `use-slice.ts`): `export function CoreProvider(props: { client: CoreClient; children: React.ReactNode })`; `export function useCore(): CoreClient`; `export function useSlice<N extends SliceName>(name: N): SliceTypes[N] | undefined` built on `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => client.get(name))` with `subscribe = useCallback((l: () => void) => client.subscribe(name, l), [client, name])` (binding `this` to `null` would break a class-based `CoreClient` and resubscribe on every render). There is no other state container; local UI state is `useState`/`useReducer`.

**L-TS-13 router** (`src/router.ts`; C24): `export type Route = { name: 'root' } | { name: 'welcome'; invite: string | null } | { name: 'channel'; communityId: string; channelId: string | null }`; `export function parseRoute(pathname: string, search: string): Route` (`/` → root, `/welcome` with optional `?invite=` → welcome, `/c/<32 hex>` and `/c/<32 hex>/<32 hex>` → channel, anything else → root); `export function routePath(r: Route): string`; `export function useRoute(): [Route, (r: Route, replace?: boolean) => void]` over `history.pushState`/`replaceState` and `popstate`. `/welcome?invite=<code>` is where the invite landing page links (L-HTTP-10). For a person who is not signed up it prefills the onboarding's invite field. For a person whose phase is `ready` the shell opens the join dialog prefilled with that invite **before** it replaces the route with the first server (or `/`), so the invite is never dropped.

Fifty keys; `en.ts` has exactly these `onboarding.*` entries and no `recovery.*` key. Flow rules, equally binding:

- Five steps — connect, identity, recovery key, what this browser keeps, done — each one `OnboardingFrame` whose `stepLabel` is `onboarding.step`. Each of the first four is one `<form noValidate>`: `Enter` in a field submits the step, as does its forward button (`type="submit"`: `Continue` on steps 1–3, `Create account` on step 4); `Back` is `type="button"`, comes first in the footer and never submits. Step 5's only button is `onboarding.done.next`. Keys come before registration (ruling 6): the account is created only by step 4's submit.
- Focus: when the shown step changes (the first render, forward, back, the closed and done frames) focus moves to that step's `<h1>`. A submit that leaves one or more fields in error moves focus to the **first field in error** (every failing field shows its message at once); a refusal that returns to an earlier step for a field moves focus to that field. A banner never moves focus.
- Step 3: while `Continue` is disabled because the box is not ticked, `onboarding.keys.ackHint` is its description. Step 4 shows the four `onboarding.browser.*` paragraphs in the order `device`, `clear`, `oneBrowser`, `private`.
- Refusals of `signupSubmit`, switched on `code` and `status` only (never on `detail`), each clearing the in-flight state:

| `code` | `status` | goes to | shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| `E_INVITE_INVALID` | any | connect, focus on the invite field | field error `onboarding.error.inviteInvalid` |
| `E_INVALID_REQUEST` | 409 | identity, focus on the username field | field error `onboarding.error.usernameTaken` |
| `E_INVALID_REQUEST` | any other | identity, focus on the heading | danger banner `onboarding.error.detailsRefused` (the page already validates both fields with the server's rules, so this is the rare case) |
| `E_FORBIDDEN` | any | the closed frame | — |
| `E_RATE_LIMITED` | any | stays | warn banner: `onboarding.error.rateLimited` with `seconds = Math.ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000)` when `retryAfterMs` is not null, else `onboarding.error.rateLimitedNoWait` |
| `E_NETWORK`, or any code with `status` ≥ 500 | — | stays | danger banner `onboarding.error.network` with the action `onboarding.error.reload` → `browser.reload()`. The response may have been lost after the account was created; the reload runs `Signup.resume()` (L-TS-06). The page never sends `signupSubmit` again in this case: a second `POST /v1/accounts` would answer "username taken" for the person's own account |
| anything else | below 500 (0 for an error that is not an HTTP answer) | stays | danger banner `onboarding.error.other` with `{code}`, no action (the server answered with a refusal, or the request was never sent, so nothing was created; `Create account` may be pressed again) |

- After `signupSubmit` resolves and the phase is `ready`, step 5 is shown; its button calls `onFinish(result)`. `App` navigates, with `replace`: to `/c/<communityId>` when `result.communityId` is set; to `/welcome?invite=<the invite>` when `result.joinError` is set (the shell then opens the join dialog prefilled, L-TS-13); otherwise to `/`.
- The boot-phase strings (`boot.*`, task 22) follow the same truth rule: `boot.storeLost.detail` says the account cannot be used here and that resetting clears this browser so the person can sign up again (it does not mention the recovery key), and `boot.revoked.detail` is `Your account no longer accepts this browser. Ask the host if you did not expect this. To start over here, clear this site’s data in the browser’s settings.` (`resetDevice` stays off the `revoked` splash: a `revoked` phase can be a false alarm, L-TS-06, and a reset would destroy a key that still works).

### L-UI — `@dilla/ui` components added (props are exact; every string is a prop)

Class rule: each component's root carries `d-<kebab-case component name>` — `d-text-field`, `d-banner`, `d-empty-state`, `d-splash`, `d-onboarding-frame`, `d-recovery-key`, `d-app-shell`, `d-community-rail`, `d-channel-list`, `d-channel-header`, `d-message-log`, `d-message-row`, `d-composer` (the older primitives abbreviate, `d-btn`, `d-chrow`; the thirteen new ones do not). Story titles, which fix the story-id prefixes the screenshot runs use: task 20 `Form/TextField`, `Form/Banner`, `Form/EmptyState`, `Ceremony/Splash`, `Ceremony/OnboardingFrame`, `Ceremony/RecoveryKey`; task 21 `Shell/AppShell`, `Shell/CommunityRail`, `Shell/ChannelList`, `Shell/ChannelHeader`, `Conversation/MessageLog`, `Conversation/MessageRow`, `Conversation/Composer`; task 23 `Screens/Onboarding`; task 24 `Screens/Shell`. The prefixes are therefore `form-`, `ceremony-`, `shell-`, `conversation-`, `screens-`.


DOM contract of these components that the screens' tests (tasks 22–24) and the e2e (task 25) rely on; tasks 20 and 21 test each line:

- `Splash`: the root is a `<main>`; `status` and `detail` are text inside its one `role="status"` `aria-atomic="true"` region; `action` is a `<button>` named by its label.
- `TextField`: a visible `<label>` whose text is exactly `label` names the input (no added asterisk text); `hint` and `error` are referenced by `aria-describedby`; `error` is inside `role="alert"`.
- `Banner` and `EmptyState`: `action` is a `<button>` named by its label; `EmptyState`'s `title` is a heading.
- `OnboardingFrame`: the `<h1 tabIndex={-1}>` holds `title` and receives focus on mount and whenever `title` changes; `stepLabel` and `footer` are rendered as given. Print: the frame's top bar, step line and footer are `display: none` under `@media print`.
- `RecoveryKey`: each group is its own text node; the checkbox is named `acknowledgeLabel`; the print button `printLabel`; no copy control. Print (owned by task 20, in `RecoveryKey.css` and `OnboardingFrame.css`): under `@media print` the heading, the label and the grid take `color: CanvasText; background: Canvas; border-color: CanvasText` (system colours, so the tokens rule holds) and the actions are not displayed; a story test under `page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' })` asserts that the first group's computed colour equals the computed `CanvasText` and that the frame's footer is not displayed.
- `CommunityRail`: each item is a `<button>` whose accessible name is `name`; the join control is a button named `joinLabel` inside the same roving group (the rail is one tab stop, join included).
- `ChannelList`: `title` is rendered as text inside the `<nav>`; rows are the existing `ChannelRow` buttons.
- `ChannelHeader`: with `readable`, a glyph with `role="img"` named `readableLabel`.
- `MessageLog`: `tabIndex={0}` on the `role="log"` element (a scrollable region); `earlier` is a button named by its label; with no children it shows `emptyLabel`.
- `MessageRow`: the root carries `data-state="<state>"`; `author`, `time`, `body`, `stateLabel` and `detail` are separate text nodes; each action is a button named by its label; `tag` uses the existing `Tag`; `MessageRowProps` is exported from `MessageRow.tsx`.
- `Composer`: the `<textarea>`'s accessible name is `label` and its value is `value`; `disabledReason` is visible text and the first part of the textarea's description; `onSend` receives the text as typed and the field keeps it until the caller changes `value`.
- `AppShell`: the skip link is an `<a>` named `skipLabel` and is the first tab stop. `data-theme` is set on `<html>` by `@dilla/web`, never on `.d-root`.

**L-UI-15 `packages/ui/scripts/shoot-stories.mjs`**: `node packages/ui/scripts/shoot-stories.mjs <port> <out-dir> <story-id-prefix>…` serves `packages/ui/storybook-static` on `127.0.0.1:<port>`, opens `iframe.html?id=<story id>&globals=theme:<theme>&viewMode=story` for every story of `index.json` whose id starts with one of the prefixes, in each of `mesh`, `light`, `high-contrast`, with Playwright Chromium at 1280×800, waits for `document.fonts.ready`, and writes `<out-dir>/<story id>.<theme>.png`. It exits 1 when a prefix matched no story or a page logged a console error. The module also exports its pure helpers (story selection, URL, file name, media types, path containment), which `scripts/shoot-stories.test.mjs` tests with `node:test`. (There is no L-UI-14.)

### L-E2E — test host and native peer

**L-E2E-01 `dilla-testkit web-driver --ds <url> --seed <n>`** (`testkit/src/web_driver.rs`; one JSON object per line on stdin, one answer per line on stdout carrying the request's `id`, `"ok"`, and the op's fields or `"error"`, exactly as `media-driver` frames them; invites come from `DILLA_TESTKIT_INVITE`, the control URL from `DILLA_TESTKIT_CONTROL`)

| op | request fields | answer fields | what it does through the public routes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setup` | `community` (name), `channel` (name) | `username`, `display` (the display name the driver registered; equal to `username`), `user_id`, `device_id`, `community_id`, `channel_id`, `invite_code` (all ids 32 hex) | registers the peer account `peer<seed hex>` as a **native-tier** device, publishes its device list and 32 KeyPackages, creates the community, one text channel (`kind 0, mode 0, visibility 0`) and a community invite (`max_uses 100, ttl_seconds 3600, grants_admin 0`) |
| `register` | — | `group_id`, `epoch` | registers the channel's text group with the instance's external sender |
| `send` | `body` | `seq` | uploads one type-0 envelope |
| `sync` | — | `epoch`, `members` (leaf count), `received`: `[{ seq, body, sender_user, sender_device, tier }]` | drains gateway frames, catches up over HTTP, commits outstanding proposals, returns every message decrypted since the previous `sync` |
| `members` | — | `devices`: `[device_id]` in leaf order | drains and applies as `sync` does, then reads the roster of the text group |
| `join` | `community_id`, `channel_id`, `group_id`, `invite_code` | `group_id`, `epoch` | `POST /v1/communities/{id}/join [code]`, then the external join of the text group (`TestClient::join_external`) with the binding `register` uses. It is what lets a second driver enter the first one's group (joining a community enters no group), which task 17's two-driver harness test needs |
| `update` | — | `epoch` | drains and applies, then commits a self Update (`TestClient::commit`, which also carries any outstanding proposal) and answers the new epoch; task 25's "a message sent while the peer commits an Update still arrives once" |

`username` is `peer` followed by the six lower-case hex digits of `seed & 0xffffff`. The driver reaches the testkit through two additive `TestClient` methods (`send_seq`, `roster`; `testkit/src/client.rs`, task 17).

**L-E2E-04 the TypeScript surface of `e2e/web/support/*`** (task 17 produces; tasks 18 and 25 consume and do not modify these four files)

```ts
// host.ts — default export: Playwright globalSetup returning its teardown. It builds the test host with the Go
// toolchain named by process.env.GO, starts it, and before it returns sets process.env.DILLA_TESTKIT_INVITE (the
// comma-separated codes of the host banner; the browser signs up with the first), DILLA_TESTKIT_CONTROL (the
// control URL) and DILLA_TEST_HOST (the public URL).
// driver.ts
export class WebDriver {
  static start(dsUrl: string, env: Record<string, string>, seed?: number): Promise<WebDriver>;
  request<T>(op: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<T>;   // rejects with Error('web-driver: <error>')
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
// persistent.ts — `test` extends Playwright's with: profileDir (/tmp/dw/<project>-<workerIndex>), context (the
// persistent context launched on it), page (context.pages()[0]) and
//   relaunch: () => Promise<{ context: BrowserContext; page: Page }>   // close(), then open the same profileDir again
// The fixture never calls context.tracing.start/stop: in Playwright 1.63.0 the runner's own hook
// (runAfterCreateBrowserContext → artifactsRecorder.didCreateBrowserContext, node_modules/playwright/lib/index.js:134-145,
// 648-651) already starts tracing on a context made by launchPersistentContext when `trace` is configured, and a
// second start throws "Tracing has been already started". context.browser() is NOT null for a persistent context.
// axe.ts
export interface AxeFinding { id: string; impact: 'serious' | 'critical'; help: string; targets: string[] }
export function injectAxe(page: Page): Promise<void>;   // page.evaluate of the axe-core source (pin table)
export function runAxe(page: Page): Promise<AxeFinding[]>;   // target-size enabled; serious and critical only
```
