- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `errors.ts`, `pacing.ts` and `client.ts`**

`packages/client-core/src/http/errors.ts` (opens with a comment naming `internal/server/errors.go` as the shape's source):
- `DillaHttpError extends Error` with the constructor and message of "Produces"; all five fields `readonly`; `name = 'DillaHttpError'`.
- `decodeErrorBody(status, body, retryAfterHeader)` per requirement 4: try `decode(body)`, catch any `CborError` into the `E_HTTP` path (any other exception is rethrown); check the three leading elements with `typeof`/`instanceof`, never with the accessors (a wrong shape is `E_HTTP`, not a throw); the code regex is `/^E_[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$/`; the header regex is `/^[0-9]{1,9}$/`; the body delay is clamped with `bigint` comparison before `Number(...)`.

`packages/client-core/src/http/pacing.ts` (opens with a comment: per-device token buckets at 80 % of the server's, ruling 20):
- `export type Bucket = 'read' | 'write' | 'message' | 'commit' | 'proposal' | 'none';` and `PACING` exactly as in "Produces".
- `TokenBuckets`: private state per bucket `{ tokens: number; last: number }`, created lazily on first take with `tokens = burst`, `last = now()`; a private `tails: Map<Bucket, Promise<void>>`. `take(bucket, signal)`: when `signal?.aborted`, reject with the `AbortError` `DOMException` (requirement 11) and touch nothing; when `bucket === 'none'`, resolve at once; otherwise chain a private `acquire(bucket, signal)` on the bucket's tail, store `result.catch(() => undefined)` as the new tail (a rejected waiter does not block the next), and return `result`. `acquire` loops: refill (`elapsed = max(0, now() − last)`, `tokens = min(burst, tokens + elapsed × perSecond / 1000)`, `last = now()`); if `tokens ≥ 1 − 1e-9`, subtract 1 (not below 0) and return; else `await sleep(Math.ceil((1 − tokens) × 1000 / perSecond), signal)`. A rejected `sleep` propagates.

`packages/client-core/src/http/client.ts` (opens with a comment: the one HTTP transport of the client core; every route goes through `request`):
- Re-export `export { PACING, type Bucket } from './pacing';` (and nothing else: `DillaHttpError` is imported from `./errors` by every caller, its one export site); import `DillaHttpError` and `decodeErrorBody` from `./errors` for internal use; define `HttpRequest`, `HttpResponse`, `HttpDeps`, `RETRY` exactly as in "Produces".
- `HttpClient` constructor: keep `deps`, store `deps.fetch` in a private field (requirement 1: detached call), strip one trailing `/` from `baseUrl`, create one `TokenBuckets` over `{ now: deps.now, sleep: deps.sleep }` (wrap them in arrow functions so they are not called unbound).
- `request(r)` is an `async` loop with `attempt` (starts 0) and `reauthenticated` (false). Each iteration: if `r.signal?.aborted` throw the `AbortError`; `attempt += 1`; `await buckets.take(r.bucket, r.signal)`; build headers and `init` per requirement 1; call fetch and read `arrayBuffer()` inside one `try`: on an exception, if `r.signal?.aborted` throw the `AbortError`, else build the `E_NETWORK` error (detail = `e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'network failure'`) and go to the retry decision for status 0. On a response: requirement 2 (generation), then requirement 3 (`ok`), else `decodeErrorBody`. Retry decision, in this order: 401 with `auth !== false` and not `reauthenticated` → set the flag, `await deps.reauthenticate()`; `true` and `attempt < maxAttempts` → continue, else throw. 429 or 503 → if `attempt ≥ maxAttempts` or the wait (`retryAfterMs ?? 1000`) exceeds `maxWaitMs` throw, else `await deps.sleep(wait, r.signal)` and continue. Status 0 or 500 → if `r.idempotent` and `attempt < maxAttempts`, `await deps.sleep(Math.min(RETRY.capMs, RETRY.baseMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)) + Math.floor(deps.random() * RETRY.jitterMs), r.signal)` and continue, else throw. Anything else → throw. A rejected `sleep` with an aborted signal becomes the `AbortError`.
- Nothing in `client.ts` logs (the `no-console` rule covers `src`), and nothing puts `token()` or a body into an error.

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { encode } from '../cbor';
import { toHex } from '../hex';
import { type Bucket } from './client';
import { DillaHttpError } from './errors';
import {
  RecordingClient, bytesReply, cborReply, fakeTransport, noContent, refusal, textReply, type FakeOptions,
} from './fake-fetch';
import { HANDSHAKES_MAX, MEMBERS_PAGE, MESSAGES_MAX, Routes, WELCOMES_PAGE } from './routes';

const fill = (n: number, b: number): Uint8Array => new Uint8Array(n).fill(b);
const INSTANCE = fill(16, 0x01);
const USER = fill(16, 0x02);
const DEVICE = fill(16, 0x03);
const COMMUNITY = fill(16, 0x04);
const CHANNEL = fill(16, 0x05);
const CATEGORY = fill(16, 0x06);
const GROUP = fill(16, 0x07);
const KEY_ID = fill(16, 0x08);
const BOT = fill(16, 0x13);
const ROLE = fill(16, 0x14);
const PUB = fill(32, 0x09);
const NONCE = fill(32, 0x0a);
const BLOB = fill(40, 0x0b);
const SIG = fill(64, 0x0c);
const ZERO32 = fill(32, 0x00);
const TAG = fill(32, 0x0d);
const COMMITMENT = fill(32, 0x0e);
const TREE = fill(24, 0x0f);
const HASH = fill(32, 0x10);
const REF = fill(32, 0x11);
const WIN = fill(48, 0x12);

const BODY = encode(['request body built by the core', 1]);
const EMPTY_ARRAY = encode([]);
const INFO = encode([3, BLOB, HASH, 12]);
const TREE_BODY = encode([3, TREE, HASH]);
const HANDSHAKES = encode([[1, 0, 1, null, BLOB], [2, 1, 0, 0, BLOB]]);
const MESSAGES = encode([[3, 1, DEVICE, BLOB, COMMITMENT, TAG, 1_800_000_000, 0]]);
const PROPOSALS = encode([[REF, 1, 2, BLOB, 0]]);
const UPLOADED = encode([10, TAG, 1_800_000_001]);
const WELCOMES = encode([[5, GROUP, 1, 4, BLOB, TREE, HASH]]);
const INSTANCE_DOC = [[1], [1], [1], INSTANCE, 7, 'dilla.test', 0, [0, 3], 2, KEY_ID, PUB];

const hex = toHex;

function setup(opts: FakeOptions = {}) {
  const t = fakeTransport(opts);
  const http = new RecordingClient(t.deps);
  return { t, http, routes: new Routes(http) };
}

function member(i: number): Uint8Array {
  const id = new Uint8Array(16);
  id[15] = i;
  return id;
}

interface Case {
  name: string;
  call(r: Routes): Promise<unknown>;
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE';
  path: string;
  bucket: Bucket;
  idempotent: boolean;
  auth: boolean;
  accept?: string;
  sent: Uint8Array | null;
  reply(): Response;
  expected: unknown;
}

const CASES: Case[] = [
  {
    name: 'getInstance reads elements 3 to 8 and 10', call: (r) => r.getInstance(),
    method: 'GET', path: '/v1/instance', bucket: 'read', idempotent: true, auth: false, sent: null,

    expected: { instanceId: INSTANCE, generation: 7n, name: 'dilla.test', registrationMode: 0, authMethods: [0, 3], policyVersion: 2n, externalSenderPub: PUB },
  },
  {
    name: 'getInvite asks for CBOR and escapes the code', call: (r) => r.getInvite('AB/CD EF'),
    method: 'GET', path: '/i/AB%2FCD%20EF', bucket: 'none', idempotent: true, auth: false, accept: 'application/cbor', sent: null,
    reply: () => cborReply(200, ['dilla.test', COMMUNITY, 1_900_000_000, 'loot']),
    expected: { communityId: COMMUNITY, communityName: 'loot', expires: 1_900_000_000n },

  {
    name: 'getInvite of an instance invite', call: (r) => r.getInvite('ABCD'),
    method: 'GET', path: '/i/ABCD', bucket: 'none', idempotent: true, auth: false, accept: 'application/cbor', sent: null,
    reply: () => cborReply(200, ['dilla.test', null, 1_900_000_000, null]),

  },

    name: 'postChallenge sends an empty array', call: (r) => r.postChallenge(DEVICE),
    method: 'POST', path: `/v1/devices/${hex(DEVICE)}/sessions/challenge`, bucket: 'none', idempotent: true, auth: false, sent: EMPTY_ARRAY,
    reply: () => cborReply(201, [NONCE, 1_800_000_060]),

  {
    name: 'postSession reads all seven elements', call: (r) => r.postSession(DEVICE, BODY),

    name: 'putDeviceList', call: (r) => r.putDeviceList(USER, BODY),

    reply: () => noContent(), expected: undefined,
  },
  {
    name: 'getDeviceList', call: (r) => r.getDeviceList(USER),

  {

  {

describe('Routes: one request per call, decoded as the server answers it', () => {
  for (const c of CASES) {
    it(c.name, async () => {
      const { t, http, routes } = setup();
      t.replies.push(c.reply());
      expect(await c.call(routes)).toEqual(c.expected);
      expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(1);
      const s = t.seen[0];
      expect(s.method).toBe(c.method);
      expect(s.url).toBe(`https://dilla.test${c.path}`);
      expect(s.headers.get('authorization')).toBe(c.auth ? 'Bearer tok-1' : null);
      expect(s.headers.get('accept')).toBe(c.accept ?? null);
      expect(s.body).toEqual(c.sent);
      expect(http.requests[0].bucket).toBe(c.bucket);
      expect(http.requests[0].idempotent).toBe(c.idempotent);
      expect(http.requests[0].auth ?? true).toBe(c.auth);
    });
  }
});

interface RefusalCase { name: string; call(r: Routes): Promise<unknown>; reply(): Response; status: number; code: string; }

const REFUSALS: RefusalCase[] = [
  { name: 'getInstance 501', call: (r) => r.getInstance(), reply: () => refusal(501, 'E_INTERNAL'), status: 501, code: 'E_INTERNAL' },
  { name: 'getInvite 410', call: (r) => r.getInvite('ABCD'), reply: () => refusal(410, 'E_INVITE_INVALID', 'the invite is spent, expired, revoked or unknown'), status: 410, code: 'E_INVITE_INVALID' },
  { name: 'postAccount 409 username taken', call: (r) => r.postAccount(BODY), reply: () => refusal(409, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST', 'username taken'), status: 409, code: 'E_INVALID_REQUEST' },
  { name: 'postChallenge 400', call: (r) => r.postChallenge(DEVICE), reply: () => refusal(400, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST'), status: 400, code: 'E_INVALID_REQUEST' },
  { name: 'postSession 401', call: (r) => r.postSession(DEVICE, BODY), reply: () => refusal(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED'), status: 401, code: 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' },
  { name: 'putDeviceList 409', call: (r) => r.putDeviceList(USER, BODY), reply: () => refusal(409, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST', 'device-list version 1 already published'), status: 409, code: 'E_INVALID_REQUEST' },
  { name: 'getDeviceList 403', call: (r) => r.getDeviceList(USER), reply: () => refusal(403, 'E_FORBIDDEN'), status: 403, code: 'E_FORBIDDEN' },
  { name: 'postKeyPackages 413', call: (r) => r.postKeyPackages(BODY), reply: () => refusal(413, 'E_TOO_LARGE'), status: 413, code: 'E_TOO_LARGE' },
  { name: 'postTicket 401', call: (r) => r.postTicket(), reply: () => refusal(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED'), status: 401, code: 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' },
  { name: 'listCommunities 403', call: (r) => r.listCommunities(), reply: () => refusal(403, 'E_FORBIDDEN'), status: 403, code: 'E_FORBIDDEN' },
  { name: 'joinCommunity 410', call: (r) => r.joinCommunity(COMMUNITY, 'AB12'), reply: () => refusal(410, 'E_INVITE_INVALID'), status: 410, code: 'E_INVITE_INVALID' },
  { name: 'listChannels 404', call: (r) => r.listChannels(COMMUNITY), reply: () => refusal(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND', 'no such object'), status: 404, code: 'E_NOT_FOUND' },
  { name: 'listMembers 404', call: (r) => r.listMembers(COMMUNITY), reply: () => refusal(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND'), status: 404, code: 'E_NOT_FOUND' },
  { name: 'postGroup 409', call: (r) => r.postGroup(BODY), reply: () => refusal(409, 'E_GROUP_EXISTS'), status: 409, code: 'E_GROUP_EXISTS' },
  { name: 'getGroupInfo 404', call: (r) => r.getGroupInfo(GROUP), reply: () => refusal(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND'), status: 404, code: 'E_NOT_FOUND' },
  { name: 'getGroupTree 404', call: (r) => r.getGroupTree(GROUP), reply: () => refusal(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND'), status: 404, code: 'E_NOT_FOUND' },
  { name: 'getHandshakes 410', call: (r) => r.getHandshakes(GROUP, 1n, 512), reply: () => refusal(410, 'E_PRUNED'), status: 410, code: 'E_PRUNED' },
  { name: 'getMessages 410', call: (r) => r.getMessages(GROUP, 1n, 256), reply: () => refusal(410, 'E_PRUNED'), status: 410, code: 'E_PRUNED' },
  { name: 'getProposals 404', call: (r) => r.getProposals(GROUP), reply: () => refusal(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND'), status: 404, code: 'E_NOT_FOUND' },
  { name: 'postCommit 409', call: (r) => r.postCommit(GROUP, BODY), reply: () => refusal(409, 'E_COMMIT_CONFLICT', 'another commit won this epoch', null, [WIN, [REF]]), status: 409, code: 'E_COMMIT_CONFLICT' },
  { name: 'postMessage 425', call: (r) => r.postMessage(GROUP, BODY), reply: () => refusal(425, 'E_COMMIT_REQUIRED', 'outstanding proposals must be committed first', 1500, [[REF]]), status: 425, code: 'E_COMMIT_REQUIRED' },
  { name: 'postCursor 400', call: (r) => r.postCursor(GROUP, BODY), reply: () => refusal(400, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST'), status: 400, code: 'E_INVALID_REQUEST' },
  { name: 'postResync 403', call: (r) => r.postResync(GROUP, BODY), reply: () => refusal(403, 'E_FORBIDDEN'), status: 403, code: 'E_FORBIDDEN' },
  { name: 'getWelcomes 401', call: (r) => r.getWelcomes(0n), reply: () => refusal(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED'), status: 401, code: 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' },
  { name: 'deleteWelcome 403', call: (r) => r.deleteWelcome(5n), reply: () => refusal(403, 'E_FORBIDDEN'), status: 403, code: 'E_FORBIDDEN' },
  { name: 'getAccountMe 401', call: (r) => r.getAccountMe(), reply: () => refusal(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED'), status: 401, code: 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' },
  { name: 'getLimits 501', call: (r) => r.getLimits(), reply: () => refusal(501, 'E_INTERNAL'), status: 501, code: 'E_INTERNAL' },

describe('Routes: a refusal propagates unchanged and is sent once', () => {
  for (const c of REFUSALS) {
    it(c.name, async () => {
      const { t, routes } = setup();
      t.replies.push(c.reply());
      const outcome = await c.call(routes).then(() => 'resolved', (e: unknown) => e);
      expect(outcome).toBeInstanceOf(DillaHttpError);
      expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ status: c.status, code: c.code });
      expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(t.sleeps).toEqual([]);
    });
  }

  it('keeps the extras of a commit conflict', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    t.replies.push(refusal(409, 'E_COMMIT_CONFLICT', 'another commit won this epoch', null, [WIN, [REF]]));
    const outcome = await routes.postCommit(GROUP, BODY).then(() => 'resolved', (e: unknown) => e);
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ code: 'E_COMMIT_CONFLICT', extra: [WIN, [REF]] });
  });

  it('postSession 401 never re-authenticates', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup({ reauth: () => ({ ok: true, token: 'tok-2' }) });
    t.replies.push(refusal(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED'));
    await routes.postSession(DEVICE, BODY).then(() => 'resolved', (e: unknown) => e);
    expect(t.reauthCalls).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('Routes: retries and inputs', () => {
  it('postMessage is sent once after a network failure', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    t.replies.push(new TypeError('fetch failed'), bytesReply(200, UPLOADED));
    const outcome = await routes.postMessage(GROUP, BODY).then(() => 'sent', (e: unknown) => e);
    expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(outcome).toBeInstanceOf(DillaHttpError);
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ status: 0, code: 'E_NETWORK' });
  });

  it('postAccount is sent once after a 500', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    t.replies.push(refusal(500, 'E_INTERNAL'), cborReply(200, [USER, DEVICE, 'tok-new', 1]));
    const outcome = await routes.postAccount(BODY).then(() => 'sent', (e: unknown) => e);
    expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ status: 500, code: 'E_INTERNAL' });
  });

  it('a read is retried after a network failure', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    t.replies.push(new TypeError('fetch failed'), bytesReply(200, MESSAGES));
    expect(await routes.getMessages(GROUP, 3n, 256)).toEqual({ raw: MESSAGES, count: 1, lastSeq: 3n });
    expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(t.sleeps).toEqual([625]);
  });

  it('refuses bad inputs before sending', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    // Thunks, not promises: each call starts only when its expectation is attached, so no
    // rejection is ever unhandled between two awaits.
    const attempts: (() => Promise<unknown>)[] = [
      () => routes.getHandshakes(GROUP, 1n, HANDSHAKES_MAX + 1),
      () => routes.getHandshakes(GROUP, 1n, 0),
      () => routes.getHandshakes(GROUP, -1n, 1),
      () => routes.getMessages(GROUP, 1n, MESSAGES_MAX + 1),
      () => routes.getWelcomes(-1n),
      () => routes.deleteWelcome(-1n),
      () => routes.listChannels(new Uint8Array(15)),
      () => routes.postCommit(new Uint8Array(17), BODY),
      () => routes.postChallenge(new Uint8Array(0)),
    ];
    for (const [i, attempt] of attempts.entries()) {
      await expect(attempt(), `attempt ${i}`).rejects.toThrow(/^E_ROUTE_INPUT: /);
    }
    expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(0);
  });

describe('Routes: response shapes', () => {
  it('refuses an answer with an element missing', async () => {

  });

    const { t, routes } = setup();

    await expect(routes.getInstance()).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'E_CBOR_RANGE' });
    await expect(routes.listMembers(COMMUNITY)).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'E_CBOR_RANGE' });
  });

describe('Routes: member paging', () => {
  const row = (i: number) => [member(i), 1_700_000_000, '', [], `u${i}`, `U ${i}`, 0];

  it('follows ?after= until a short page', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    const first = Array.from({ length: MEMBERS_PAGE }, (_, i) => row(i + 1));
    const second = [row(201), row(202), row(203)];
    t.replies.push(cborReply(200, first), cborReply(200, second));
    const members = await routes.listMembers(COMMUNITY);
    expect(t.seen.map((s) => s.url)).toEqual([
      `https://dilla.test/v1/communities/${hex(COMMUNITY)}/members`,
      `https://dilla.test/v1/communities/${hex(COMMUNITY)}/members?after=${hex(member(200))}`,
    ]);
    expect(members).toHaveLength(203);
    expect(members[0]).toEqual({ userId: member(1), username: 'u1', display: 'U 1', kind: 0, nick: '' });
    expect(members[202].userId).toEqual(member(203));
  });

  it('asks once more after a full last page and stops at an empty one', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    t.replies.push(cborReply(200, Array.from({ length: MEMBERS_PAGE }, (_, i) => row(i + 1))), cborReply(200, []));
    expect(await routes.listMembers(COMMUNITY)).toHaveLength(200);
    expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it('stops with a shape error when a full page does not advance', async () => {
    const { t, routes } = setup();
    const page = Array.from({ length: MEMBERS_PAGE }, (_, i) => row(i + 1));
    t.replies.push(cborReply(200, page), cborReply(200, page));
    await expect(routes.listMembers(COMMUNITY)).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'E_CBOR_SHAPE' });
    expect(t.seen).toHaveLength(2);
  });
});
```

  ```ts
  // frames.ts
  export interface Frame { op: number; n: bigint; groupId: Uint8Array | null; payload: CborValue[]; }
  export function encodeFrame(op: number, n: number, groupId: Uint8Array | null, payload: readonly CborInput[]): Uint8Array;
  export function decodeFrame(bytes: Uint8Array): Frame;          // CborError, or Error('E_FRAME_SHAPE')
  export const Op = { hello: 0, identify: 1, ready: 3, invalidSession: 5, heartbeat: 6, heartbeatAck: 7, reconnect: 8, error: 9,
    commitAck: 12, handshake: 16, commitNeeded: 17, epochChanged: 18, messageCt: 19, welcome: 20, messageDeleted: 21 } as const;

  // gateway.ts
  export type GatewayStatus = 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'ready' | 'waiting';
  export interface ReadyInfo { deviceId: Uint8Array; userId: Uint8Array; generation: bigint; keypackagesRemaining: number;
    groups: { groupId: Uint8Array; epoch: bigint; lastSeq: bigint; proposalsOutstanding: number }[];
    heartbeatMs: number; maxFrameBytes: number; backoffMs: number; backoffJitterMs: number; }
  export type GatewayEvent =
    | { type: 'status'; status: GatewayStatus; closeCode: number | null }
    | { type: 'ready'; info: ReadyInfo }
    | { type: 'frame'; frame: Frame }                            // ops 16–21 only
    | { type: 'revoked' };                                       // close 4004, or a ticket mint refused with 401
  export interface GatewayDeps {
    url: string;                                                 // ws(s)://<page host>/gateway
    mintTicket(): Promise<string>;
    WebSocket: typeof WebSocket;
    now(): number; random(): number;
    setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): number; clearTimeout(id: number): void;
  }
  export class Gateway {
    constructor(deps: GatewayDeps);
    start(): void; stop(): void;
    subscribe(listener: (e: GatewayEvent) => void): () => void;
    commitAck(groupId: Uint8Array, round: bigint): void;         // dropped unless status is 'ready'
    readonly status: GatewayStatus;
  }
  export const GATEWAY = { heartbeatMaxMs: 15000, ackTimeoutMs: 10000, helloTimeoutMs: 15000,
    reconnectBaseMs: 500, reconnectCapMs: 30000, reconnectJitterMs: 500 } as const;
  // L-TS-04: the codes a browser client may legally close with (41xx never collides with the server's 4000–4010).
  export const CLIENT_CLOSE = { normal: 1000, version: 4006, helloTimeout: 4100, heartbeatTimeout: 4101,
    undecodable: 4102, tooLarge: 4109 } as const;
  ```

**Requirements:**

Frames (`frames.ts`):
1. `encodeFrame` writes the deterministic CBOR array `[op, n, group_id, payload]` with `encode` (protocol/02:129-144). `op` must be an integer 0..255, `n` a non-negative safe integer, `groupId` `null` or exactly 16 bytes; anything else throws `new Error('E_FRAME_SHAPE')` before encoding. Every one of the 25 `frames.json` cases encodes byte for byte (`frames.json` `cases[].frame`).
2. `decodeFrame` decodes with `decode` and lets a `CborError` propagate unchanged (non-shortest head → `E_CBOR_NONCANONICAL`, a map → `E_CBOR_TYPE`; L-TS-01). It then requires, else throws `new Error('E_FRAME_SHAPE')` (message exactly `E_FRAME_SHAPE`): a 4-element array; element 0 an unsigned integer ≤ 255; element 1 an unsigned integer (returned as `bigint`); element 2 `null` or a 16-byte byte string; element 3 an array (`internal/gateway/frame.go:176-236`).
3. For each of the 25 opcodes of `internal/gateway/frame.go:94-129` `decodeFrame` also checks the payload element count and the group rule, else `E_FRAME_SHAPE`: counts 0:9, 1:5, 2:4, 3:9, 4:3, 5:2, 6:2, 7:1, 8:2, 9:3, 10:1, 11:1, 12:1, 16:5, 17:4, 18:2, 19:6, 20:6, 21:2, 32:7, 33:4, 48:4, 49:4, 50:4; ops 12 and 16–21 must carry a `group_id`, every other listed op must carry `null` (protocol/02:236-240). An opcode outside the table passes with the envelope checks of R2 only: the client ignores unknown opcodes (L-GW-02 "Every other op is ignored"), unlike the server's `E_FRAME_TYPE` (`frame.go:195-199`).
4. The client's verdict on each `frames.json` reject is fixed (table in Step 1): nine refuse with `E_FRAME_SHAPE` or a `CborError`, and `unknown opcode` is accepted (R3).
5. `decodeFrame(encodeFrame(...))` round-trips every case: `op`, `n` (as `bigint`), `groupId`, and `encode(payload)` equal to the vector's `payload` bytes.

Gateway (`gateway.ts`; L-TS-04, L-GW-02, interfaces.md A4.1–A4.5, C19):
6. `start()` is a no-op unless `status` is `'idle'`. Otherwise it sets `'connecting'`, emits `{ type: 'status', status: 'connecting', closeCode: null }`, and begins an attempt: `await deps.mintTicket()`; then `new deps.WebSocket(deps.url, ['dilla.v1', 'dilla.ticket.' + ticket])` — both subprotocols, in that order (A4.1; `session.go:207-223`, `gateway.go:665-675`) — and sets `binaryType = 'arraybuffer'`. Listeners are attached with `addEventListener` for `message`, `close` and `error`.
7. Every attempt carries a private attempt number; a ticket that resolves, a socket event, or a timer that fires for an attempt that is no longer current (after `stop()` or after a teardown) is ignored. A ticket that resolves after `stop()` opens no socket.
8. Hello: a timer of `GATEWAY.helloTimeoutMs` starts when the socket is created. The first frame must be op 0; any other first frame is treated as undecodable (R12). The hello payload is read as `[wire[], e2ee[], media[], heartbeat_ms, max_frame_bytes, instance_id(16), generation, backoff_ms, backoff_jitter_ms]` (protocol/02:156); a malformed hello is undecodable (R12). When any of the three version arrays lacks `1`, the gateway closes with `CLIENT_CLOSE.version` (4006), cancels every timer, sets status `'idle'`, emits `{ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: 4006 }`, and does not reconnect. Otherwise it sends `identify` exactly `encodeFrame(Op.identify, 1, null, ['', 1, 1, 1, 0])` (`caps = 0`, a uint: L-GW-02, protocol/02:157 and the `identify` vector) and re-arms the same timer for `ready` (L-TS-04 "Behaviour": `ready` within the same bound re-armed after `identify`). Expiry of that timer closes with `CLIENT_CLOSE.helloTimeout` (4100) and reconnects.
9. Ready: op 3's payload `[device_id(16), user_id(16), generation, resume_token(bstr), wire, e2ee, media, keypackages_remaining, groups[[group_id(16), epoch, last_seq, proposals_outstanding]]]` (A4.3) becomes `ReadyInfo` together with the hello's `heartbeat_ms`, `max_frame_bytes`, `backoff_ms`, `backoff_jitter_ms`; `resume_token` and the three versions are read for shape and discarded (no resume, C19). On ready: clear the handshake timer, reset `failures` to 0, set status `'ready'`, emit the status event (`closeCode: null`), emit `{ type: 'ready', info }`, start the heartbeat. A malformed ready is undecodable (R12).
10. Heartbeat: interval `min(Math.floor(heartbeat_ms / 2), GATEWAY.heartbeatMaxMs)` (A4.5 item 2), chained with `deps.setTimeout`. Each tick sends `encodeFrame(Op.heartbeat, 0, null, [lastN, 1])` where `lastN` is the highest `n` of any frame received on this socket (0n before any) (protocol/02:162), and arms an ack timer of `GATEWAY.ackTimeoutMs`; op 7 clears it. Ack timer expiry closes with `CLIENT_CLOSE.heartbeatTimeout` (4101) and reconnects. Heartbeats run only while status is `'ready'`.
11. Frames: after ready, ops 16–21 are emitted as `{ type: 'frame', frame }` in arrival order; op 7 is R10; ops 5 and 8 are R14; op 9 and every other opcode (including 32, 33, 48–50) are dropped. Before ready only ops 0 and 3 advance the handshake; ops 5, 8 are handled as R14; every other op is dropped. The gateway never sends ops 2 (`resume`), 10, 11 (C19, L-GW-02).
12. Undecodable input closes with `CLIENT_CLOSE.undecodable` (4102) and reconnects: a `message` whose `data` is not an `ArrayBuffer` (text frame), a `decodeFrame` throw, a hello or ready whose payload elements are not the shapes of R8/R9, a first frame that is not hello. (A browser refuses `close(1002)`; L-GW-02 "Close codes", L-TS-04.)
13. Oversize: a binary message whose `byteLength` exceeds the hello's `max_frame_bytes` (before hello: 131584, protocol/02:619-622) closes with `CLIENT_CLOSE.tooLarge` (4109) and reconnects, before decoding. (A browser refuses `close(1009)`; L-GW-02 "Close codes", L-TS-04.)
14. `reconnect` (op 8 `[reason, after_ms]`) records `afterMs = after_ms` for the next schedule only; `invalid_session` (op 5) records `afterMs = 0`. Both close the socket with `CLIENT_CLOSE.normal` (1000) and reconnect.
15. Teardown (every client-initiated close): mark the attempt stale, cancel the handshake, heartbeat and ack timers, call `socket.close(code)` inside `try`/`catch` (a throw is ignored), then either reconnect (R16) or go idle. The `close` event that the socket fires afterwards is ignored (R7), so one teardown schedules exactly one reconnect.
16. Reconnect: a server-initiated `close` event (any code but 4004), every teardown of R8 (timeout), R10, R12, R13, R14, a socket constructor that throws, and a `mintTicket` rejection other than the one of R16a each set status `'waiting'` and emit `{ type: 'status', status: 'waiting', closeCode }` — `closeCode` is the event's `code` for a server close, the code the client sent for a teardown, `null` for a mint or constructor failure — then schedule the next attempt after `Math.floor(Math.max(afterMs, Math.min(GATEWAY.reconnectCapMs, GATEWAY.reconnectBaseMs * 2 ** failures) + deps.random() * GATEWAY.reconnectJitterMs))` and then increment `failures`; `afterMs` resets to 0 once used. When the timer fires the status becomes `'connecting'` (event emitted) and R6's attempt runs.
16a. A refused ticket is revocation (L-TS-04 "Behaviour" as amended; L-GW-02 "Close codes"). A `mintTicket` rejection that is `instanceof DillaHttpError` (imported from `../http/errors`) with `status === 401`, for the current attempt: the HTTP layer has already called `reauthenticate()` and it answered `false`, so this device cannot establish a session. Cancel every timer (handshake, heartbeat, ack, reconnect), set status `'idle'`, emit `{ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: null }` then `{ type: 'revoked' }`, and schedule nothing; `failures` is not incremented. A later `start()` connects afresh, as after R17. Every other rejection — a `DillaHttpError` of any other status (0, 429, 500, 503, …) and any other thrown value — is R16. Without this rule a device revoked while its socket is down retries for ever and never reaches the `revoked` splash.
17. Close 4004 (`session_revoked`, protocol/02:57, 249): cancel timers, status `'idle'`, emit `{ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: 4004 }` then `{ type: 'revoked' }`, schedule nothing. A later `start()` connects afresh (the account layer re-establishes first, L-GW-02).
18. `stop()`: no-op when `'idle'`; otherwise teardown with `CLIENT_CLOSE.normal` and no reconnect, cancel a pending reconnect timer, set `'idle'`, emit `{ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: null }`.
19. `commitAck(groupId, round)` sends `encodeFrame(Op.commitAck, 0, groupId, [round])` only when status is `'ready'` and the socket's `readyState` is 1; otherwise it does nothing (no queue, no throw). Every send checks `readyState === 1` (the literal; `deps.WebSocket.OPEN` is not read, a test double need not define it).
20. `subscribe` adds a listener and returns its removal; listeners are called synchronously in subscription order; a listener that throws does not stop the gateway: the error is rethrown from `queueMicrotask` so it still surfaces.
21. `deps.now` is accepted and unused in web-1 (kept for the interface).
22. No string literal or comment in `src/gateway/*` contains a word `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs` forbids (`FORBIDDEN`, lines 5-11; the extractor also reads text between any `>` and `<` of a `.ts` file).

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { arr, CborError, decode, encode } from '../cbor';
import { fromHex, toHex } from '../hex';
import { decodeFrame, encodeFrame, Op } from './frames';

interface FrameCase { name: string; op: number; n: number; group_id: string; payload: string; frame: string }
interface FrameReject { name: string; frame: string; code: string }
const vectors = JSON.parse(
  readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../protocol/vectors/frames.json', import.meta.url)), 'utf8'),
) as { cases: FrameCase[]; rejects: FrameReject[] };

/** What this client does with each server-side reject vector: an error code, or null for "accepted". */
const CLIENT_VERDICT: Record<string, string | null> = {
  'three elements': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'five elements': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'unknown opcode': null,
  'server opcode from a client': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'payload is not an array': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'subscribe with the wrong element count': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'group_id on a control frame': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'group_id of the wrong length': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'commit_ack with no group_id': 'E_FRAME_SHAPE',
  'non-minimal op': 'E_CBOR_NONCANONICAL',
  'map instead of an array': 'E_CBOR_TYPE',
};

function verdict(bytes: Uint8Array): string | null {
  try {
    decodeFrame(bytes);
    return null;
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof CborError) return err.code;
    if (err instanceof Error) return err.message;
    throw err;
  }
}

describe('frames.json', () => {
  it('holds the 25 cases and 11 rejects this codec was written against', () => {
    expect(vectors.cases).toHaveLength(25);
    expect(vectors.rejects).toHaveLength(11);
    expect(Object.keys(CLIENT_VERDICT).sort()).toEqual(vectors.rejects.map((r) => r.name).sort());
  });

  for (const c of vectors.cases) {
    it(`encodes ${c.name} byte for byte`, () => {
      const payload = arr(decode(fromHex(c.payload)));
      const groupId = c.group_id === '' ? null : fromHex(c.group_id);
      expect(toHex(encodeFrame(c.op, c.n, groupId, payload))).toBe(c.frame);
    });

    it(`decodes ${c.name}`, () => {
      const frame = decodeFrame(fromHex(c.frame));
      expect(frame.op).toBe(c.op);
      expect(frame.n).toBe(BigInt(c.n));
      expect(frame.groupId === null ? '' : toHex(frame.groupId)).toBe(c.group_id);
      expect(toHex(encode(frame.payload))).toBe(c.payload);
    });
  }

  for (const r of vectors.rejects) {
    it(`gives the client verdict on the reject "${r.name}"`, () => {
      expect(verdict(fromHex(r.frame))).toBe(CLIENT_VERDICT[r.name]);
    });
  }
});

describe('frame shape', () => {
```

Create `packages/client-core/src/gateway/gateway.test.ts`:

```ts
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { DillaHttpError } from '../http/errors';
import { decodeFrame, encodeFrame, Op, type Frame } from './frames';
import { CLIENT_CLOSE, GATEWAY, Gateway, type GatewayDeps, type GatewayEvent } from './gateway';

const INSTANCE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x01);
const DEVICE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x08);
const USER = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x09);
const GROUP = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x07);

function hello(over: { wire?: number[]; heartbeatMs?: number; maxFrameBytes?: number } = {}): Uint8Array {
  return encodeFrame(Op.hello, 0, null, [over.wire ?? [1], [1], [1], over.heartbeatMs ?? 30000,
    over.maxFrameBytes ?? 131584, INSTANCE, 1, 300, 300]);
}

function ready(): Uint8Array {
  return encodeFrame(Op.ready, 1, null, [DEVICE, USER, 7, new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x0b), 1, 1, 1, 32, [[GROUP, 6, 4127, 2]]]);
}

/** A manual clock: timers run only inside advance(), in deadline order, ties in creation order. */
class FakeClock {
  now = 0;
  private nextId = 1;
  private readonly timers = new Map<number, { at: number; fn: () => void }>();
  readonly setTimeout = (fn: () => void, ms: number): number => {
    const id = this.nextId;
    this.nextId += 1;
    this.timers.set(id, { at: this.now + ms, fn });
    return id;
  };
  readonly clearTimeout = (id: number): void => {
    this.timers.delete(id);
  };
  advance(ms: number): void {
    const end = this.now + ms;
    for (;;) {
      let due: [number, { at: number; fn: () => void }] | undefined;
      for (const entry of this.timers) {
        if (entry[1].at <= end && (due === undefined || entry[1].at < due[1].at)) due = entry;
      }
      if (due === undefined) break;
      this.timers.delete(due[0]);
      this.now = due[1].at;
      due[1].fn();
    }
    this.now = end;
  }
  /** Delays of the pending timers from now, ascending. */
  pending(): number[] {
    return [...this.timers.values()].map((t) => t.at - this.now).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  }
}

type Listener = (event: unknown) => void;

/** A WebSocket double with the browser's close-code rule. */
class FakeSocket {
  static instances: FakeSocket[] = [];
  readonly url: string;
  readonly protocols: string[];
  binaryType = 'blob';
  readyState = 0;
  readonly sent: Uint8Array[] = [];
  closedWith: { code: number; reason: string } | null = null;
  private readonly listeners = new Map<string, Listener[]>();

  constructor(url: string, protocols: string | string[]) {
    this.url = url;
    this.protocols = typeof protocols === 'string' ? [protocols] : [...protocols];
    FakeSocket.instances.push(this);
  }
  addEventListener(type: string, fn: Listener): void {
    this.listeners.set(type, [...(this.listeners.get(type) ?? []), fn]);
  }
  removeEventListener(type: string, fn: Listener): void {
    this.listeners.set(type, (this.listeners.get(type) ?? []).filter((l) => l !== fn));
  }
  send(data: Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer): void {
    if (this.readyState !== 1) throw new Error('send on a socket that is not open');
    this.sent.push(data instanceof Uint8Array ? data.slice() : new Uint8Array(data));
  }
  close(code?: number, reason = ''): void {
    if (code !== undefined && code !== 1000 && (code < 3000 || code > 4999)) {
      throw new DOMException(`close code ${code} is not allowed`, 'InvalidAccessError');
    }
    if (this.readyState === 3) return;
    this.closedWith = { code: code ?? 1005, reason };
    this.readyState = 3;
    this.emit('close', { code: code ?? 1005, reason, wasClean: true });
  }
  open(): void {
    this.readyState = 1;
    this.emit('open', {});
  }
  receive(data: Uint8Array | string): void {
    this.emit('message', { data: typeof data === 'string' ? data : data.slice().buffer });
  }
  serverClose(code: number): void {
    this.readyState = 3;
    this.emit('close', { code, reason: '', wasClean: true });
  }
  sentFrames(): Frame[] {
    return this.sent.map((b) => decodeFrame(b));
  }
  private emit(type: string, event: unknown): void {
    for (const l of this.listeners.get(type) ?? []) l(event);
  }
}

const flush = (): Promise<void> => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve));

function harness(opts: { random?: number; mint?: () => Promise<string> } = {}) {
  const clock = new FakeClock();
  const events: GatewayEvent[] = [];
  let minted = 0;
  const deps: GatewayDeps = {
    url: 'ws://127.0.0.1:8453/gateway',
    mintTicket: opts.mint ?? (() => {
      minted += 1;
      return Promise.resolve(`t${minted}`);
    }),
    WebSocket: FakeSocket as unknown as typeof WebSocket,
    now: () => clock.now,
    random: () => opts.random ?? 0,
    setTimeout: clock.setTimeout,
    clearTimeout: clock.clearTimeout,
  };
  const gw = new Gateway(deps);
  gw.subscribe((e) => events.push(e));
  const last = (): FakeSocket => {
    const s = FakeSocket.instances.at(-1);
    if (s === undefined) throw new Error('no socket was opened');
    return s;
  };
  return { gw, clock, events, last, minted: () => minted };
}

async function connected(h: ReturnType<typeof harness>, helloFrame = hello()): Promise<FakeSocket> {
  h.gw.start();
  await flush();
  const s = h.last();
  s.open();
  s.receive(helloFrame);
  s.receive(ready());
  return s;
}

const statuses = (events: GatewayEvent[]) =>
  events.flatMap((e) => (e.type === 'status' ? [`${e.status}:${String(e.closeCode)}`] : []));

beforeEach(() => {
  FakeSocket.instances = [];
});

describe('Gateway connect', () => {
  it('pins the timing constants', () => {
    expect(GATEWAY).toEqual({ heartbeatMaxMs: 15000, ackTimeoutMs: 10000, helloTimeoutMs: 15000,
      reconnectBaseMs: 500, reconnectCapMs: 30000, reconnectJitterMs: 500 });
    expect(CLIENT_CLOSE).toEqual({ normal: 1000, version: 4006, helloTimeout: 4100, heartbeatTimeout: 4101,
      undecodable: 4102, tooLarge: 4109 });
  });

  it('offers dilla.v1 and the ticket as subprotocols and reads binary frames', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.gw.start();
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('connecting');
    await flush();
    expect(FakeSocket.instances).toHaveLength(1);
    const s = h.last();
    expect(s.url).toBe('ws://127.0.0.1:8453/gateway');
    expect(s.protocols).toEqual(['dilla.v1', 'dilla.ticket.t1']);
    expect(s.binaryType).toBe('arraybuffer');
    expect(h.events[0]).toEqual({ type: 'status', status: 'connecting', closeCode: null });
  });

  it('answers hello with a fresh identify and reports ready', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.gw.start();
    await flush();
    const s = h.last();
    s.open();
    expect(s.sent).toHaveLength(0);
    s.receive(hello());
    expect(s.sent).toEqual([encodeFrame(Op.identify, 1, null, ['', 1, 1, 1, 0])]);
    s.receive(ready());
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('ready');
    expect(h.events.find((e) => e.type === 'ready')).toEqual({
      type: 'ready',
      info: {
        deviceId: DEVICE, userId: USER, generation: 7n, keypackagesRemaining: 32,
        groups: [{ groupId: GROUP, epoch: 6n, lastSeq: 4127n, proposalsOutstanding: 2 }],
        heartbeatMs: 30000, maxFrameBytes: 131584, backoffMs: 300, backoffJitterMs: 300,
      },
    });
    expect(statuses(h.events)).toEqual(['connecting:null', 'ready:null']);
  });

  it('refuses a hello without version 1 and stays down', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.gw.start();
    await flush();
    const s = h.last();
    s.open();
    s.receive(hello({ wire: [2] }));
    expect(s.closedWith?.code).toBe(4006);
    expect(s.sent).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('idle');
    expect(h.events.at(-1)).toEqual({ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: 4006 });
    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([]);
    h.clock.advance(600_000);
    await flush();
    expect(FakeSocket.instances).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(h.minted()).toBe(1);
  });

  it('gives up on a socket that sends no hello, and on one that sends no ready', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.gw.start();
    await flush();
    const first = h.last();
    first.open();
    h.clock.advance(14_999);
    expect(first.closedWith).toBeNull();
    h.clock.advance(1);
    expect(first.closedWith?.code).toBe(CLIENT_CLOSE.helloTimeout);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('waiting');
    h.clock.advance(h.clock.pending()[0] ?? 0);
    await flush();
    const second = h.last();
    second.open();
    second.receive(hello());
    h.clock.advance(15_000);
    expect(second.closedWith?.code).toBe(CLIENT_CLOSE.helloTimeout);
  });
});

describe('Gateway heartbeat', () => {
  it('beats every min(heartbeat_ms / 2, 15 s) with the highest n seen', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const s = await connected(h);
    const beats = () => s.sentFrames().filter((f) => f.op === Op.heartbeat);
    h.clock.advance(14_999);

    h.clock.advance(1);
    expect(beats()).toEqual([{ op: Op.heartbeat, n: 0n, groupId: null, payload: [1n, 1n] }]);
    s.receive(encodeFrame(Op.heartbeatAck, 0, null, [1_700_000_000]));
    s.receive(encodeFrame(Op.messageCt, 5, GROUP, [9, 6, DEVICE, new Uint8Array([1]), new Uint8Array(32), 1_700_000_000]));
    h.clock.advance(15_000);

    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([500]);

    s1.serverClose(4010);
    h.clock.advance(h.clock.pending()[0] ?? 0);
    await flush();
    const s2 = h.last();
    s2.open();
    s2.receive(hello());
    s2.receive(ready());
    h.gw.commitAck(GROUP, 3n);
    const ops = [...s1.sentFrames(), ...s2.sentFrames()].map((f) => f.op);
    expect(ops).toEqual([Op.identify, Op.heartbeat, Op.identify, Op.commitAck]);
    expect(s2.sent[0]).toEqual(encodeFrame(Op.identify, 1, null, ['', 1, 1, 1, 0]));
    expect(s2.protocols).toEqual(['dilla.v1', 'dilla.ticket.t2']);
  });
});

describe('Gateway revocation and stop', () => {
  it('reports revoked on close 4004 and does not reconnect by itself', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const s = await connected(h);
    s.serverClose(4004);
    expect(h.events.slice(-2)).toEqual([{ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: 4004 }, { type: 'revoked' }]);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('idle');
    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([]);
    h.clock.advance(120_000);
    await flush();
    expect(FakeSocket.instances).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(h.minted()).toBe(1);
    h.gw.start();
    await flush();
    expect(FakeSocket.instances).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  /** A mint that succeeds until `refuseWith` is set, then rejects with a DillaHttpError of that status. */
  function refusingMint() {
    const m = { calls: 0, refuseWith: null as number | null };
    const mint = (): Promise<string> => {
      m.calls += 1;
      if (m.refuseWith === null) return Promise.resolve(`t${m.calls}`);
      return Promise.reject(new DillaHttpError({
        status: m.refuseWith, code: m.refuseWith === 401 ? 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' : 'E_HTTP', detail: '', retryAfterMs: null, extra: [],
      }));
    };
    return { m, mint };
  }

  it('a revoked device with a dead socket reaches revoked', async () => {
    const { m, mint } = refusingMint();
    const h = harness({ mint });
    const s = await connected(h);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('ready');
    s.serverClose(1006);
    expect(h.events.at(-1)).toEqual({ type: 'status', status: 'waiting', closeCode: 1006 });
    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([500]);
    m.refuseWith = 401;
    const seen = h.events.length;
    h.clock.advance(500);
    await flush();
    expect(h.events.slice(seen)).toEqual([
      { type: 'status', status: 'connecting', closeCode: null },
      { type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: null },
      { type: 'revoked' },
    ]);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('idle');
    expect(m.calls).toBe(2);
    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([]);
    h.clock.advance(120_000);
    await flush();
    expect(m.calls).toBe(2);
    expect(FakeSocket.instances).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('a mint that fails for another reason is retried', async () => {
    const { m, mint } = refusingMint();
    const h = harness({ mint });
    const s = await connected(h);
    s.serverClose(1006);
    m.refuseWith = 503;
    const seen = h.events.length;
    h.clock.advance(500);
    await flush();
    expect(h.events.slice(seen)).toEqual([
      { type: 'status', status: 'connecting', closeCode: null },
      { type: 'status', status: 'waiting', closeCode: null },
    ]);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('waiting');
    expect(h.events.some((e) => e.type === 'revoked')).toBe(false);
    expect(m.calls).toBe(2);
    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([1000]);
    h.clock.advance(1000);
    await flush();
    expect(m.calls).toBe(3);
  });

  it('stop closes with 1000, cancels every timer and reports idle', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const s = await connected(h);
    h.gw.stop();
    expect(s.closedWith?.code).toBe(1000);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('idle');
    expect(h.clock.pending()).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.events.at(-1)).toEqual({ type: 'status', status: 'idle', closeCode: null });
    h.gw.stop();
    expect(statuses(h.events).filter((x) => x === 'idle:null')).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('opens no socket for a ticket that arrives after stop', async () => {
    let release: (ticket: string) => void = () => undefined;
    const h = harness({ mint: () => new Promise<string>((resolve) => { release = resolve; }) });
    h.gw.start();
    h.gw.stop();
    release('late');
    await flush();
    expect(FakeSocket.instances).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(h.gw.status).toBe('idle');
  });

  it('drops commitAck unless ready', async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.gw.commitAck(GROUP, 1n);
    h.gw.start();
    await flush();
    const s = h.last();
    s.open();
    s.receive(hello());
    h.gw.commitAck(GROUP, 2n);
    expect(s.sentFrames().map((f) => f.op)).toEqual([Op.identify]);
    s.receive(ready());
    h.gw.commitAck(GROUP, 9n);
    expect(s.sent.at(-1)).toEqual(encodeFrame(Op.commitAck, 0, GROUP, [9n]));
  });

  it('keeps running when a listener throws, and rethrows the error from a microtask', async () => {
    const deferred: (() => void)[] = [];
    const spy = vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'queueMicrotask').mockImplementation((cb: () => void) => {
      deferred.push(cb);
    });
    try {
      const h = harness();
      h.gw.subscribe(() => {
        throw new Error('listener failed');
      });
      const s = await connected(h);
      expect(h.gw.status).toBe('ready');
      expect(s.closedWith).toBeNull();
      expect(h.events.map((e) => e.type)).toEqual(['status', 'status', 'ready']);
      expect(deferred.length).toBe(3);
      expect(() => deferred[0]?.()).toThrow('listener failed');
    } finally {
      spy.mockRestore();
    }
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `frames.ts`**

- `Op`: the object of the Interfaces block, `as const`.
- A private table `SPECS: ReadonlyMap<number, { elements: number; grouped: boolean }>` with exactly the 25 entries of Requirement 3 (copied from `internal/gateway/frame.go:94-129`; `grouped` true for 12 and 16–21).
- `encodeFrame(op, n, groupId, payload)`: check `Number.isInteger(op) && op >= 0 && op <= 255`, `Number.isSafeInteger(n) && n >= 0`, and `groupId === null || groupId.length === 16`; on any failure `throw new Error('E_FRAME_SHAPE')`. Return `encode([op, n, groupId, payload])`. It does not apply the per-op table (the caller chooses the payload; the vectors include client frames).
- `decodeFrame(bytes)`: `const v = decode(bytes)` (a `CborError` propagates). If `v` is not an array of length 4 → `E_FRAME_SHAPE`. Element 0 must be a `bigint` ≤ 255n, element 1 a `bigint`, element 2 `null` or a `Uint8Array` of length 16, element 3 an array; else `E_FRAME_SHAPE`. When `SPECS` has the op: `payload.length !== spec.elements` → `E_FRAME_SHAPE`; `spec.grouped !== (groupId !== null)` → `E_FRAME_SHAPE`. Return `{ op: Number(op), n, groupId, payload }`. Type tests use `typeof x === 'bigint'`, `x instanceof Uint8Array`, `Array.isArray(x)`; no cast.

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement `gateway.ts`**

Private state of `Gateway`: `deps`; `listeners: Set<(e: GatewayEvent) => void>`; `current: GatewayStatus = 'idle'` (exposed by the `status` getter); `attempt = 0` (increments for every attempt and every teardown); `socket: WebSocket | null`; `phase: 'minting' | 'hello' | 'ready-wait' | 'ready'`; `hello: { heartbeatMs: number; maxFrameBytes: number; backoffMs: number; backoffJitterMs: number } | null`; `lastN = 0n`; `failures = 0`; `afterMs = 0`; four timer ids (`reconnectTimer`, `handshakeTimer`, `heartbeatTimer`, `ackTimer`), each `number | null`, always cleared through one private `cancel(name)` that calls `deps.clearTimeout`. A private constant `DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 131584` (protocol/02:619-622).

Functions, in the order they run:
- `emit(e)`: for each listener in insertion order, call it inside `try`; on a throw `queueMicrotask(() => { throw err; })` (Requirement 20).
- `setStatus(status, closeCode)`: assign `current`, emit the status event.
- `start()`: return unless `current === 'idle'`; `failures = 0`, `afterMs = 0`; `setStatus('connecting', null)`; `connect()`.
- `connect()` (synchronous; spawns the async part with `void this.open(id)` where `id = ++this.attempt` and `open` never rejects): `phase = 'minting'`. `open(id)`: `try { ticket = await deps.mintTicket() } catch (err) { … }` where the catch returns at once when `id !== this.attempt`, else, when `err instanceof DillaHttpError && err.status === 401`, runs `goIdle()`, `setStatus('idle', null)`, `emit({ type: 'revoked' })` and returns (R16a), else runs `this.fail(null)` and returns; return if `id !== this.attempt`; `try { ws = new deps.WebSocket(deps.url, ['dilla.v1', `dilla.ticket.${ticket}`]) } catch { this.fail(null); return; }`; `ws.binaryType = 'arraybuffer'`; reset `lastN = 0n`, `hello = null`, `phase = 'hello'`; attach the three listeners, each first checking `id === this.attempt` and returning otherwise; arm `handshakeTimer` for `GATEWAY.helloTimeoutMs` → `teardown(CLIENT_CLOSE.helloTimeout, true)`.
- `onMessage(event)`: `data` not an `ArrayBuffer` → `teardown(undecodable, true)`. `data.byteLength > (hello?.maxFrameBytes ?? DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_BYTES)` → `teardown(tooLarge, true)`. `decodeFrame(new Uint8Array(data))` in `try`; a throw → `teardown(undecodable, true)`. `if (frame.n > lastN) lastN = frame.n`. Then by `phase`:
  - `'hello'`: op other than 0 → `teardown(undecodable, true)`. Read the hello with the L-TS-01 readers (`arr`, `u64`, `u53`, `bin(…, 16)`) inside `try` (any `CborError` → `teardown(undecodable, true)`). If one of `wire`, `e2ee`, `media` lacks `1n` → `teardown(CLIENT_CLOSE.version, false)` then `setStatus('idle', 4006)`. Else store `hello`, send `encodeFrame(Op.identify, 1, null, ['', 1, 1, 1, 0])` (L-GW-02), `phase = 'ready-wait'`, re-arm `handshakeTimer` (same duration and action).
  - `'ready-wait'`: op 3 → read the payload as R9 inside `try` (a throw → `teardown(undecodable, true)`); `cancel('handshakeTimer')`; `failures = 0`; `phase = 'ready'`; `setStatus('ready', null)`; emit `{ type: 'ready', info }`; `scheduleBeat()`. Op 5 or 8 → `reconnectFrame(frame)`. Any other op is dropped.
  - `'ready'`: op 7 → `cancel('ackTimer')`; ops 16–21 → emit `{ type: 'frame', frame }`; ops 5, 8 → `reconnectFrame(frame)`; anything else dropped.
- `reconnectFrame(frame)`: op 8 → `afterMs = u53(payload[1])` (a malformed payload → `afterMs = 0`); op 5 → `afterMs = 0`; then `teardown(CLIENT_CLOSE.normal, true)`.
- `scheduleBeat()`: `interval = Math.min(Math.floor(hello.heartbeatMs / 2), GATEWAY.heartbeatMaxMs)`; arm `heartbeatTimer` for `interval`; on fire: `send(encodeFrame(Op.heartbeat, 0, null, [lastN, 1]))`, arm `ackTimer` for `GATEWAY.ackTimeoutMs` → `teardown(CLIENT_CLOSE.heartbeatTimeout, true)`, then `scheduleBeat()` again.
- `send(bytes)`: only when `socket?.readyState === 1`; calls `socket.send(bytes)`.
- `onClose(event)` (only for the current attempt): `event.code === 4004` → `goIdle()` with no socket close, `setStatus('idle', 4004)`, emit `{ type: 'revoked' }`. Otherwise `fail(event.code)`.
- `teardown(code, reconnect)`: `const ws = socket`; `attempt += 1` (the socket's later events are now stale); cancel `handshakeTimer`, `heartbeatTimer`, `ackTimer`; `socket = null`; `try { ws?.close(code) } catch { /* the socket is already gone */ }`; if `reconnect` → `fail(code)`.
- `fail(closeCode)`: cancel the three socket timers (idempotent); `socket = null`; `setStatus('waiting', closeCode)`; `delay = Math.floor(Math.max(afterMs, Math.min(GATEWAY.reconnectCapMs, GATEWAY.reconnectBaseMs * 2 ** failures) + deps.random() * GATEWAY.reconnectJitterMs))`; `failures += 1`; `afterMs = 0`; arm `reconnectTimer` for `delay` → `setStatus('connecting', null); connect()`.
- `goIdle()`: `attempt += 1`, cancel all four timers, `socket = null`, `phase = 'minting'`.
- `stop()`: return when `current === 'idle'`; `teardown(CLIENT_CLOSE.normal, false)`; `goIdle()`; `setStatus('idle', null)`.
- `commitAck(groupId, round)`: when `current === 'ready'` → `send(encodeFrame(Op.commitAck, 0, groupId, [round]))`.
- `subscribe(listener)`: add; return `() => { listeners.delete(listener); }`.
- `error` events are ignored (a `close` always follows in a browser).

No `console` call, no `setInterval`, no `Date.now()` (time comes only through `deps`).

**Requirements:**

`CorePort` and `wrapCore` (`core-port.ts`; L-TS-03, L-WASM-04/05):
- R15-1. `wrapCore` is the only code in `@dilla/client-core` that calls a `CoreHandle` method. Each `CorePort` method calls the snake_case method of L-WASM-05 with the arguments in the ledger's order: `signupRequest(…, password)` passes `password` (`null` stays `null`); `sessionSign(nonce, purpose: 0 | 1)` passes `purpose` as a number — the generated signature is `session_sign(nonce: Uint8Array, purpose: number)`, and the facade itself refuses any value but 0 and 1 with `E_CORE_INPUT: purpose: <n> is not 0 or 1` (L-WASM-04: `u8` crosses as a range-checked `u32`), so `wrapCore` adds no check of its own; `messageDeleted(groupId, seq)` → `message_deleted(groupId, seq)`; `sessionStore(s)` → `session_store(s.token, s.expires, s.idleExpires)`; `groupJoinExternal(g, info, tree)` → `group_join_external(g.groupId, g.communityId, g.channelId, g.policyVersion, info, tree)`; `welcomesApply(body, expected)` → `welcomes_apply(body, encode(expected.map(e => [e.groupId, e.communityId, e.channelId, e.policyVersion])))`. `pause`, `resume`, `close` forward unchanged.
- R15-2. Results: request bodies (`signupRequest`, `signupComplete`, `deviceListBody`, `sessionSign`, `keyPackages`, `groupCreate`, `groupJoinExternal`, `commitBuild`) return the bytes unchanged; `signupBegin` returns the string; `cursorBody` returns `null` when the bytes decode to CBOR `null`, else the bytes unchanged. Every other result is decoded with L-TS-01 per the shapes of L-CORE-06…09: `identity` (6 elements, `listPublished = (element 5 === 1n)`); `session` (`null` or 3 elements); `groups` (rows of 9, `pendingCommit = (element 8 === 1n)`); `groupApply`/`commitConfirm`/`messageDeleted` (one decoder, `readApply`, for all three: `[state, epoch, next_seq, new_seqs, proposals_pending, flags]`, `epochChanged = (flags & 1n) !== 0n`, `ownAdopted = (flags & 2n) !== 0n`); `welcomesApply` (rows of 4); `sendPrepare` (`[msg_id]` → the 16 bytes); `sendEncrypt` (`[group_id, message_body]`); `sendConfirm` (`[group_id, seq]`); `outbox` (rows of 5); `timeline` (rows of 12, nullable elements 5, 7, 8, 9, 10). `u64` fields become `bigint`; `phase`, `state`, `kind`, `outcome`, `status`, `proposalsPending`, `type`, `senderKind`, `senderTier` become numbers with `u53`; every 16-byte id is read with `bin(v, 16)`. A `phase` outside 0..2, a `state` outside 0..4, an outbox state outside 0..2, a `status` outside 0..2, an `outcome` outside 0..3, or any `CborError` becomes `CoreError('E_CORE_DECODE', '<method>: <reason>')` (L-TS-03 error codes).
- R15-3. Every throw from a handle method is converted by `CoreError.from`: a `CoreError` is returned as is; an `Error` whose `message` matches `/^(E_[A-Z0-9_]+)(?:: ([\s\S]*))?$/` becomes `CoreError(match[1], match[2] ?? '')`; any other `Error` becomes `CoreError('E_CORE_WASM', err.message)`; a non-`Error` value becomes `CoreError('E_CORE_WASM', String(value))` (L-TS-03 error codes). `wrapCore` throws the converted error synchronously (and rejects with it for `resume`).
- R15-4. `core-wasm-conformance.ts` contains no runtime statement other than two exported constants whose types are conditional type checks, and is the only file of the package that names `@dilla/core-wasm`: `export const handleConforms: Generated extends CoreHandle ? true : never = true;` and `export const moduleConforms: typeof import('@dilla/core-wasm') extends CoreWasmModule ? true : never = true;` with `import type { CoreHandle as Generated } from '@dilla/core-wasm'`. `npm run typecheck -w @dilla/client-core` fails when the generated surface drifts from L-WASM-05 (L-TS-03). The generated class has `message_deleted` from task 7 on, so the conformance file needs nothing for it. No vitest file imports it.

`FakeCore` (`testing/fake-core.ts`; L-TS-03 "Two doubles": the account half only):
- R15-21. Ids: `new FakeCore()` draws ids from a counter: 16 bytes, byte 0 = `idSeed` (default `0xf0`), bytes 12–15 the counter big-endian starting at 1. `opts.deviceId` (when given) is the device id `signupBegin` uses; else the next drawn id. `opts.tier` (default 1) is stored and read by no account method; it is accepted so that the option set is the one L-TS-03 names. Opaque fields the account half returns are CBOR byte strings holding a CBOR array with a text tag first: credential `encode(['fake.cred', 16 zero bytes, device_id])`, device list blob `encode(['fake.list', user_id, device_id, now])`, KeyPackage `encode(['fake.kp', device_id, index, last_resort])` (`index` 0..count-1 and `last_resort` 0 for the regular packages; `index = count` and `last_resort` 1 for the last-resort package).
- R15-22. Identity (L-CORE-06 phases and error table): `identity()` as the ledger. `signupBegin(instanceId)`: phase 0 only (else `CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'a signup is pending')` in phase 1 and `CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'the identity is complete')` in phase 2), sets phase 1, the instance and device ids, returns `FAKE_RECOVERY_KEY` and stores it nowhere. `signupRequest` (phase 1, else `E_CORE_STATE` with detail `no signup is pending` in phase 0 and `the identity is complete` in phase 2) returns `encode([invite, username, display, 32×0x01, 32×0x02, 64×0x03, password, [device_id, 32×0x04, 1, 1, credential]])`. `signupComplete(userId, username, now)` (phase 1, else `E_CORE_STATE` with the same details) sets phase 2, `listPublished = false`, stores and returns `encode([1, list_blob, 64×0x05, 32 zero bytes])`. `signupReset()` mirrors L-CORE-06: phase 1 only (else `E_CORE_STATE` with the same details), and **with a stored session record it throws `CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'the account is registered')` and changes nothing**; otherwise it returns to phase 0 with every identity field cleared. `deviceListBody()` / `deviceListPublished()` / `keyPackages()` need phase 2 (else `CoreError('E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY')`). `sessionSign(nonce, purpose)` needs phase ≥ 1 (else `E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY`), a 32-byte nonce and purpose 0 or 1 (else `E_CORE_INPUT`) and returns `encode([nonce, purpose, 64×0x06, null, null])`. `sessionStore` needs phase ≥ 1 (else `E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY`) and replaces the one record; `session` and `sessionClear` answer in every phase. `keyPackages(count, lastResort)`: count 1..32 (else `E_CORE_INPUT`), returns `encode([[kp × count], lastResort ? kp_lr : null])`. `FakeCore.identified(…)` is a phase-2 core with the given ids, `listPublished` (default true) and the device list body that `signupComplete(userId, username, 0n)` would have produced.
- R15-23. Every `CorePort` method of L-CORE-07…09 — `groups`, `groupCreate`, `groupRegistered`, `groupDiscard`, `groupJoinExternal`, `groupJoined`, `welcomesApply`, `groupApply`, `commitBuild`, `commitConfirm`, `commitAbort`, `cursorBody`, `cursorAcked`, `messageDeleted`, `sendPrepare`, `sendEncrypt`, `sendConfirm`, `sendRequeue`, `sendFail`, `sendRetry`, `sendDiscard`, `outbox`, `timeline` — logs its name to `calls` (R15-30, so a queued `failOnce` error and the paused check still apply first) and then throws `new CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'not modelled')`. The group half is modelled by `ModelCore` (task 16), which is held to the Rust core by the parity fixture of L-CORE-10.
- R15-29. `pause()` makes every method but `resume` throw `CoreError('E_STORE_PAUSED', 'the store is paused')` until `resume()` resolves; `close()` makes every later call throw the same.
- R15-30. Every `CorePort` call appends its method name to `calls` before anything else; `failOnce(method, error)` makes the next call of that method throw `error` after logging it, with no state change.
- R15-31. No string literal of `fake-core.ts` contains a word of `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs:5-11` (tags are `fake.*`).

KEK (`account/kek.ts`; L-TS-05, C7):
- R15-40. Database `KEK_DB` version `KEK_DB_VERSION`; `onupgradeneeded` creates object store `KEK_STORE` (out-of-line keys) when `db.objectStoreNames.contains(KEK_STORE)` is false. The only IndexedDB members used are those of R15-45 (the test double implements exactly those).
- R15-41. `create(hex)`: `wrapKey = await subtle.generateKey({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt'])` — non-extractable (C7); `kek` = 32 bytes from `getRandomValues`; `iv` = 12 bytes from `getRandomValues`; `ct = AES-GCM(wrapKey, iv, kek, additionalData = UTF-8 "dilla kek v1" ‖ fromHex(hex))` (48 bytes); `store.add({ v: 1, wrapKey, iv, ct }, hex)` in a `readwrite` transaction; resolves with `kek` on `oncomplete`. An `add` that fails with a `ConstraintError` rejects with `Error('E_KEK_EXISTS')` (L-TS-05); any other request or transaction error rejects with that error.
- R15-42. `load(hex)`: `get(hex)` in a `readonly` transaction; `undefined` → `null`. A record whose `v !== 1`, whose `iv` is not a 12-byte `Uint8Array`, whose `ct` is not a 48-byte `Uint8Array`, whose `wrapKey` is not a `CryptoKey`-shaped object, or whose decryption with the R15-41 additional data fails → `Error('E_KEK_UNWRAP')` (L-TS-05). The decrypted 32 bytes are returned in a fresh array.
- R15-43. `remove(hex)`: `delete(hex)` in a `readwrite` transaction, resolves on `oncomplete`.
- R15-44. Every operation opens the database, does one transaction and calls `db.close()` before settling. Nothing is cached between calls. No key, IV or KEK is logged or put in an error message.
- R15-45. IndexedDB surface used: `idb.open(name, version)` with `onupgradeneeded`, `onsuccess`, `onerror` and `result`; `db.objectStoreNames.contains`, `db.createObjectStore(name)`, `db.transaction(name, mode)`, `db.close()`; `tx.objectStore(name)`, `tx.oncomplete`, `tx.onerror`, `tx.onabort`; `store.get`, `store.add(value, key)`, `store.delete`; request `onsuccess`, `onerror`, `result`, `error`. Byte arrays passed to `subtle` are allocated as `new Uint8Array(n)` (type `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>`).

Boot (`account/boot.ts`; L-TS-06, C5, C7):
- R15-50. `boot(deps)` in this order: (1) `JSON.parse(await deps.probePersistence())`; JSON that does not parse or has no `mode` → `{ kind: 'unsupported', reason: 'probe' }`; `mode !== 'opfs'` → `{ kind: 'unsupported', reason: <the reason field, '' when absent> }` (A5.2: run before `store_open`); nothing else is touched. (2) `hex = toHex(deps.instance.instanceId)`, `dir = storeDirectory(hex)`. (3) `kek = await deps.kek.load(hex)`; a rejection with message `E_KEK_UNWRAP` → `{ kind: 'store-lost' }`; any other rejection propagates. (4) `kek === null`: `await deps.storeExists(dir)` true → `{ kind: 'store-lost' }` with no KEK created; false → `kek = await deps.kek.create(hex)`. (5) `opened = await deps.openCore(dir, STORE_DB_NAME, toHex(kek))`, and in a `finally` around that await, `kek.fill(0)` (L-TS-05 "zero-fills the byte array as soon as core_open settles"; the hex string cannot be wiped and is not kept). A rejection that is an `Error` whose `message` starts with `E_STORE_KEY` **and** contains `WRONG_KEY_TEXT` (`'file is not a database'`, SQLite's answer to a wrong key) → `{ kind: 'store-lost' }`. Every other rejection, including any other `E_STORE_KEY` (the store raises that code for every failure of its first read, `core/dilla-core-wasm/src/store.rs:125-128`, for example `E_STORE_KEY: unable to open database file`), propagates unchanged (the same object), and ends in the `error` phase, whose splash offers a reload and no reset (L-TS-06: in web-1 a reset is the permanent loss of the account). (6) `await opened.reserveCapacity(RESERVE_CAPACITY)` (16, L-TS-05; spike `worker.ts:172`). (7) `{ kind: 'opened', core: opened.core, instance: deps.instance }`.
- R15-51. `wasmCoreOpener(mod, sleep)` returns `openCore` that tries at most `OPEN_BACKOFF_MS.length + 1` (6) times: each attempt constructs a **fresh** `new mod.StoreOpenConfig(directory, dbName, kekHex)` (wasm-bindgen consumes it, spike `worker.ts:117-131`) and awaits `mod.core_open(cfg)`; a rejection for which `mod.is_sah_contention(err)` is true and that is not the last attempt sleeps `OPEN_BACKOFF_MS[attempt - 1]` and retries; any other rejection, or the last one, is rethrown unchanged. Success returns `{ core: wrapCore(handle), reserveCapacity: (n) => handle.reserve_capacity(n) }`.
- R15-52. `opfsDirectoryExists(root, path)` walks `path.split('/')` (empty segments skipped) with `getDirectoryHandle(segment)` (no `create`); a `DOMException` named `NotFoundError` or `TypeMismatchError` → `false`; any other rejection propagates; reaching the end → `true`.

Session (`account/session.ts`; L-TS-06, protocol/02:21-65):
- R15-60. `token()` returns `core.session()?.token ?? null`, read from the core on every call (so a record stored by `Signup` is seen at once).
- R15-61. `establish()` is single-flight: while one runs, every call returns the same promise; it is cleared when that promise settles. Steps: `id = core.identity()`; `id.phase === 0` or `id.deviceId === null` → reject with `CoreError('E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY', '')`. **Attempt 1:** `{ nonce } = await routes.postChallenge(id.deviceId)`; `body = core.sessionSign(nonce, 0)` (purpose 0 = session, L-TS-06); `r = await routes.postSession(id.deviceId, body)`. A `DillaHttpError` with `status === 401` from this **first** `postSession` proves nothing (a nonce the server no longer holds — nonces live in memory, single use, 60 s — a transient error of its device lookup, a revoked row and a bad signature all answer the same empty 401, `internal/auth/session.go:335-362`), so it runs **attempt 2** once: a fresh `routes.postChallenge(id.deviceId)`, `core.sessionSign(nonce, 0)` on the new nonce, `routes.postSession(id.deviceId, body)`. Only when this second `postSession` also answers 401 is the refusal confirmed: then, **when `core.identity().phase === 2`** (read again at this point), `core.sessionClear()`; in phase 1 the session record is kept (it is the only proof that `POST /v1/accounts` succeeded, L-TS-06); resolve `false`. A 401 from either `postChallenge`, and any other error at any point (any other status, `E_NETWORK`, a `CoreError` from `sessionSign`), propagates unchanged and stores and clears nothing. For whichever attempt succeeded: `r.scope !== 0` → reject with `Error('E_SESSION_SCOPE')` and store nothing (L-TS-06); else `core.sessionStore({ token: r.token, expires: r.expires, idleExpires: r.idleExpires })`, resolve `true`. At most two `postChallenge` and two `postSession` calls per `establish()`.
- R15-62. `ensure()`: `nowS = BigInt(Math.floor(now() / 1000))`; `rec = core.session()`; `rec === null`, or `rec.expires - nowS <= BigInt(RENEW_MARGIN_S)`, or `rec.idleExpires - nowS <= BigInt(RENEW_MARGIN_S)` → `establish()`; else resolve `true` with no request. `RENEW_MARGIN_S = 3600`.
- R15-63. Wired as `HttpDeps.reauthenticate`, `establish()` gives an authenticated request that met 401 one fresh token (L-TS-02). `postChallenge` and `postSession` are `auth: false` requests, and L-TS-02 never calls `reauthenticate()` for them (task 13's code), so `establish()` never re-enters itself.

Signup (`account/signup.ts`; L-TS-06, Ruling 6, F2):
- R15-70. `begin(instanceId)`: `rk = core.signupBegin(instanceId)`; a length other than 52 → `CoreError('E_CORE_DECODE', 'recovery key length')`; returns the 13 consecutive 4-character slices. `Signup` keeps no reference to `rk` or the groups.
- R15-71. `submit(input)` in exactly this order (L-TS-06): `body = core.signupRequest(invite, username, display, password)`; `acc = await routes.postAccount(body)` — **one call; a thrown `DillaHttpError` (including `E_NETWORK`, status 0) propagates unchanged, nothing after it runs, and the phase stays 1** (`POST /v1/accounts` is not idempotent, interfaces.md A1.14); `core.sessionStore({ token: acc.token, expires: acc.expires, idleExpires: acc.expires })`; `core.signupComplete(acc.userId, input.username, BigInt(Math.floor(now() / 1000)))`; `await publishDeviceList(core, routes)`; `limits = await routes.getLimits()`; `await refillKeyPackages(core, routes, 0, { perDevice: limits.keypackagesPerDevice, threshold: limits.keypackageRefillThreshold })`.
- R15-72. `resume(): Promise<0 | 2 | 'revoked'>`: `phase = core.identity().phase`; 0 → resolve 0 and 2 → resolve 2, with no call; 1 → `ok = await session.establish()`. `false` (a confirmed refusal, R15-61): when `core.session() === null` the registration never happened → `core.signupReset()`, resolve `0`; when a session record exists the account exists → resolve `'revoked'` and call nothing (the core refuses `signupReset` in that state with `E_CORE_STATE` `the account is registered`, L-CORE-06, and the device key of an existing account is never destroyed). `true` → `me = await routes.getAccountMe()`, `core.signupComplete(me.userId, me.username, nowS)`, `publishDeviceList`, `getLimits`, `refillKeyPackages(…, 0, …)` as in R15-71, resolve 2. Errors other than establish's `false` propagate with the phase unchanged. (Residual, accepted by L-TS-06: an instance that answers two false 401s in a row to a browser whose registration response was lost makes that browser start over while its username stays taken.)
- R15-73. `publishDeviceList(core, routes)`: `id = core.identity()`; `id.listPublished` → resolve with no call; `id.phase !== 2` or `id.userId === null` → reject `CoreError('E_CORE_NO_IDENTITY', '')`; `await routes.putDeviceList(id.userId, core.deviceListBody())`; a `DillaHttpError` with `status === 409` → `cur = await routes.getDeviceList(id.userId)`; `cur !== null && cur.version >= 1n` → published, else rethrow the 409; any other error propagates; finally `core.deviceListPublished()`. (No published list ⇒ every Add of the user's devices is refused, interfaces.md A3.2.)

KeyPackages (`account/keypackages.ts`; L-TS-06, A4.4):
- R15-80. `refillKeyPackages(core, routes, remaining, limits)`: `remaining >= limits.threshold` → resolve 0 with no call; else `count = Math.min(limits.perDevice - remaining, 32)` (L-TS-06: the count is clamped to 32, `key_packages` accepts 1..32), `lastResort = remaining === 0`; `await routes.postKeyPackages(core.keyPackages(count, lastResort))`; resolve `count`.

Common:
- R15-90. No string literal or comment in the new files contains a word of `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs:5-11`; no `console`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` (L-CI-04); no file but `core-wasm-conformance.ts` imports `@dilla/core-wasm`, and no test loads wasm (Global Constraints "Testing").

```ts
const MSG = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x11);

type Impl = Partial<Record<keyof CoreHandle, (...args: never[]) => unknown>>;

function stub(impl: Impl) {
  const calls: { method: string; args: unknown[] }[] = [];
  const handle = new Proxy({}, {
    get(_target, prop) {
      return (...args: unknown[]) => {
        calls.push({ method: String(prop), args });
        const f = impl[prop as keyof CoreHandle] as ((...a: unknown[]) => unknown) | undefined;
        if (f === undefined) throw new Error(`stub: ${String(prop)} is not stubbed`);
        return f(...args);
      };
    },
  }) as unknown as CoreHandle;
  return { port: wrapCore(handle), calls };
}

function caught(fn: () => unknown): CoreError {
  try {

  throw new Error('nothing was thrown');
}
```
