Create `packages/client-core/src/account/kek.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { fromHex } from '../hex';
import { indexedDbKekStore, KEK_DB, KEK_DB_VERSION, KEK_STORE } from './kek';

const HEX = 'ab'.repeat(16);
const OTHER = 'cd'.repeat(16);
const subtle = globalThis.crypto.subtle;
const random = (a: Uint8Array): Uint8Array => globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues(a);

type Handler = ((event: unknown) => void) | null;

class FakeRequest {
  result: unknown = undefined;
  error: DOMException | null = null;
  onsuccess: Handler = null;
  onerror: Handler = null;
  onupgradeneeded: Handler = null;
  onblocked: Handler = null;
}

class FakeTransaction {
  oncomplete: Handler = null;
  onerror: Handler = null;
  onabort: Handler = null;
  error: DOMException | null = null;
  private open = 0;
  private failed = false;
  constructor(private readonly idb: FakeIdb, readonly mode: string) {}
  objectStore(name: string): FakeObjectStore {
    const records = this.idb.stores.get(name);
    if (records === undefined) throw new DOMException(`no object store ${name}`, 'NotFoundError');
    return new FakeObjectStore(this, records);
  }
  /** Runs one request on a later microtask; the transaction completes after its last request. */
  run(op: () => unknown): FakeRequest {
    const request = new FakeRequest();
    this.open += 1;
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      try {
        request.result = op();
        request.onsuccess?.({ target: request });
      } catch (err) {
        request.error = err instanceof DOMException ? err : new DOMException(String(err), 'UnknownError');
        this.failed = true;
        this.error = request.error;
        request.onerror?.({ target: request });
        this.onerror?.({ target: this });
        this.onabort?.({ target: this });
      }
      this.open -= 1;
      if (this.open === 0 && !this.failed) queueMicrotask(() => this.oncomplete?.({ target: this }));
    });
    return request;
  }
}

class FakeObjectStore {
  constructor(private readonly tx: FakeTransaction, private readonly records: Map<string, unknown>) {}
  get(key: string): FakeRequest {
    return this.tx.run(() => this.records.get(key));
  }
  add(value: unknown, key: string): FakeRequest {
    this.writable();
    return this.tx.run(() => {
      if (this.records.has(key)) throw new DOMException('Key already exists in the object store.', 'ConstraintError');
      this.records.set(key, value);
      return key;
    });
  }
  delete(key: string): FakeRequest {
    this.writable();
    return this.tx.run(() => {
      this.records.delete(key);
      return undefined;
    });
  }
  private writable(): void {
    if (this.tx.mode !== 'readwrite') throw new DOMException('the transaction is read-only', 'ReadOnlyError');
  }
}

class FakeDatabase {
  closed = false;
  readonly objectStoreNames = { contains: (name: string): boolean => this.idb.stores.has(name) };
  constructor(private readonly idb: FakeIdb, private readonly upgrading: () => boolean) {}
  createObjectStore(name: string): object {
    if (!this.upgrading()) throw new DOMException('not in a version change', 'InvalidStateError');
    this.idb.stores.set(name, new Map());
    return {};
  }
  transaction(_name: string, mode = 'readonly'): FakeTransaction {
    if (this.closed) throw new DOMException('the database is closed', 'InvalidStateError');
    return new FakeTransaction(this.idb, mode);
  }
  close(): void {
    this.closed = true;
  }
}

/** The IndexedDB subset kek.ts uses (one database), with the real API's asynchrony. */
class FakeIdb {
  readonly stores = new Map<string, Map<string, unknown>>();
  readonly opens: { name: string; version: number }[] = [];
  readonly databases: FakeDatabase[] = [];
  private version = 0;
  open(name: string, version: number): FakeRequest {
    const request = new FakeRequest();
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      this.opens.push({ name, version });
      let upgrading = false;
      const db = new FakeDatabase(this, () => upgrading);
      this.databases.push(db);
      request.result = db;
      if (version > this.version) {
        const oldVersion = this.version;
        this.version = version;
        upgrading = true;
        request.onupgradeneeded?.({ target: request, oldVersion, newVersion: version });
        upgrading = false;
      }
      request.onsuccess?.({ target: request });
    });
    return request;
  }
}

interface StoredRecord { v: number; wrapKey: CryptoKey; iv: Uint8Array; ct: Uint8Array }

function setup() {
  const idb = new FakeIdb();
  const store = indexedDbKekStore(idb as unknown as IDBFactory, subtle, random);
  const records = () => {
    const r = idb.stores.get(KEK_STORE);
    if (r === undefined) throw new Error('no kek store');
    return r;
  };
  const stored = (key: string): StoredRecord => {
    const rec = records().get(key) as StoredRecord | undefined;
    if (rec === undefined) throw new Error(`no record under ${key}`);
    return rec;
  };
  return { idb, store, records, stored };
}

function aad(hex: string): Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> {
  const label = new TextEncoder().encode('dilla kek v1');
  const out = new Uint8Array(label.length + 16);
  out.set(label);
  out.set(fromHex(hex), label.length);
  return out;
}

describe('indexedDbKekStore', () => {
  it('names the database, its version and its store', () => {
    expect([KEK_DB, KEK_DB_VERSION, KEK_STORE]).toEqual(['dilla-device', 1, 'kek']);
  });

  it('creates a 32-byte KEK, stores it wrapped, and loads it back', async () => {
    const { idb, store, stored } = setup();
    const kek = await store.create(HEX);
    expect(kek).toHaveLength(32);
    expect(kek.some((b) => b !== 0)).toBe(true);
    expect(idb.opens[0]).toEqual({ name: 'dilla-device', version: 1 });
    const rec = stored(HEX);
    expect(rec.v).toBe(1);
    expect(rec.iv).toHaveLength(12);
    expect(rec.ct).toHaveLength(48);
    expect(await store.load(HEX)).toEqual(kek);
    expect(idb.databases.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(idb.databases.every((db) => db.closed)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('wraps with a non-extractable AES-GCM-256 key', async () => {
    const { store, stored } = setup();
    await store.create(HEX);
    const key = stored(HEX).wrapKey;
    expect(key.extractable).toBe(false);
    expect(key.algorithm).toEqual({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 });
    expect([...key.usages].sort()).toEqual(['decrypt', 'encrypt']);
    await expect(subtle.exportKey('raw', key)).rejects.toThrow();
  });

  it('binds the wrapped KEK to its instance id', async () => {
    const { store, stored, records } = setup();
    const kek = await store.create(HEX);
    const rec = stored(HEX);
    const plain = new Uint8Array(await subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: new Uint8Array(rec.iv), additionalData: aad(HEX) },
      rec.wrapKey, new Uint8Array(rec.ct)));
    expect(plain).toEqual(kek);
    await expect(subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: new Uint8Array(rec.iv), additionalData: aad(OTHER) },
      rec.wrapKey, new Uint8Array(rec.ct))).rejects.toThrow();
    records().set(OTHER, rec);
    await expect(store.load(OTHER)).rejects.toThrow('E_KEK_UNWRAP');
  });

  it('returns null for a missing record and refuses to create over an existing one', async () => {
    const { store, stored } = setup();
    expect(await store.load(HEX)).toBeNull();
    await store.create(HEX);
    const before = stored(HEX).ct.slice();
    await expect(store.create(HEX)).rejects.toThrow('E_KEK_EXISTS');
    expect(stored(HEX).ct).toEqual(before);
  });

  it('refuses a tampered or malformed record', async () => {
    const { store, stored, records } = setup();
    await store.create(HEX);
    const rec = stored(HEX);
    rec.ct[0] = (rec.ct[0] ?? 0) ^ 1;
    await expect(store.load(HEX)).rejects.toThrow('E_KEK_UNWRAP');
    rec.ct[0] = (rec.ct[0] ?? 0) ^ 1;
    records().set(HEX, { ...rec, v: 2 });
    await expect(store.load(HEX)).rejects.toThrow('E_KEK_UNWRAP');
    records().set(HEX, { ...rec, iv: new Uint8Array(11) });
    await expect(store.load(HEX)).rejects.toThrow('E_KEK_UNWRAP');
  });

  it('removes a record', async () => {
    const { store } = setup();
    await store.create(HEX);
    await store.remove(HEX);
    expect(await store.load(HEX)).toBeNull();
    expect(await store.create(HEX)).toHaveLength(32);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { encode } from '../cbor';
import type { CoreHandle, CoreWasmModule, StoreOpenConfigLike } from '../core-port';
import type { Instance } from '../http/routes';
import { FakeCore } from '../testing/fake-core';
import { boot, opfsDirectoryExists, OPEN_BACKOFF_MS, RESERVE_CAPACITY, STORE_DB_NAME, storeDirectory, wasmCoreOpener,
  WRONG_KEY_TEXT, type BootDeps } from './boot';
import type { KekStore } from './kek';

const INSTANCE: Instance = { instanceId: new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xab), generation: 1n, name: 'dilla.test', registrationMode: 0,
  authMethods: [0], policyVersion: 1n, externalSenderPub: new Uint8Array(32).fill(0xcd) };
const HEX = 'ab'.repeat(16);

class MemoryKek implements KekStore {
  readonly records = new Map<string, Uint8Array>();
  readonly handedOut: Uint8Array[] = [];
  failLoad: Error | null = null;
  load(hex: string): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {
    if (this.failLoad !== null) return Promise.reject(this.failLoad);
    const r = this.records.get(hex);
    if (r === undefined) return Promise.resolve(null);
    const copy = r.slice();
    this.handedOut.push(copy);
    return Promise.resolve(copy);
  }
  create(hex: string): Promise<Uint8Array> {
    if (this.records.has(hex)) return Promise.reject(new Error('E_KEK_EXISTS'));
    this.records.set(hex, new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x5a));
    const copy = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x5a);
    this.handedOut.push(copy);
    return Promise.resolve(copy);
  }
  remove(hex: string): Promise<void> {
    this.records.delete(hex);
    return Promise.resolve();
  }
}

function setup(over: Partial<BootDeps> = {}) {
  const opened: { directory: string; dbName: string; kekHex: string }[] = [];
  const reserved: number[] = [];
  const probedDirs: string[] = [];
  const core = new FakeCore();
  const kek = new MemoryKek();
  const deps: BootDeps = {
    instance: INSTANCE,
    probePersistence: () => Promise.resolve('{"mode":"opfs"}'),
    storeExists: (dir) => {
      probedDirs.push(dir);
      return Promise.resolve(false);
    },
    kek,
    openCore: (directory, dbName, kekHex) => {
      opened.push({ directory, dbName, kekHex });
      return Promise.resolve({ core, reserveCapacity: (n) => {
        reserved.push(n);
        return Promise.resolve();
      } });
    },
    ...over,
  };
  return { deps, opened, reserved, probedDirs, core, kek };
}

class FakeConfig implements StoreOpenConfigLike {
  static made: FakeConfig[] = [];
  constructor(readonly directory: string, readonly db_name: string, readonly kek_hex: string) {
    FakeConfig.made.push(this);
  }
}

describe('wasmCoreOpener', () => {
  const contention = new DOMException('Access Handles cannot be created', 'NoModificationAllowedError');
  const reservations: number[] = [];
  const handle = new Proxy({}, {
    get: (_t, prop) => (...args: unknown[]) => {
      if (prop === 'reserve_capacity') {
        reservations.push(args[0] as number);
        return Promise.resolve();
      }
      if (prop === 'identity') return encode([0, null, null, null, '', 0]);
      throw new Error(`stub: ${String(prop)} is not stubbed`);
    },
  }) as unknown as CoreHandle;

  function module(failures: Error[]): CoreWasmModule {
    let call = 0;
    return {
      core_open: () => {
        const failure = failures[call];
        call += 1;
        return failure === undefined ? Promise.resolve(handle) : Promise.reject(failure);
      },
      StoreOpenConfig: FakeConfig,
      is_sah_contention: (err) => err === contention,
      probe_persistence: () => Promise.resolve('{"mode":"opfs"}'),
    };
  }

  it('retries contention on the spike schedule with a fresh config per attempt', async () => {
    FakeConfig.made = [];
    const sleeps: number[] = [];
    const open = wasmCoreOpener(module([contention, contention]), (ms) => {
      sleeps.push(ms);
      return Promise.resolve();
    });
    const store = await open(`dilla/${HEX}`, 'dilla.db', 'aa'.repeat(32));
    expect(FakeConfig.made).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(new Set(FakeConfig.made).size).toBe(3);
    expect(FakeConfig.made[2]).toMatchObject({ directory: `dilla/${HEX}`, db_name: 'dilla.db', kek_hex: 'aa'.repeat(32) });
    expect(sleeps).toEqual([300, 600]);
    await store.reserveCapacity(16);
    expect(reservations).toEqual([16]);
    expect(store.core.identity().phase).toBe(0);
  });

  it('rethrows anything else at once, and contention after six attempts', async () => {
    const sleeps: number[] = [];
    const sleep = (ms: number) => {
      sleeps.push(ms);
      return Promise.resolve();
    };
    const refused = new Error('E_STORE_KEY: wrong key');
    await expect(wasmCoreOpener(module([refused]), sleep)('d', 'dilla.db', 'aa'.repeat(32))).rejects.toBe(refused);
    expect(sleeps).toEqual([]);
    await expect(wasmCoreOpener(module(Array.from({ length: 6 }, () => contention)), sleep)('d', 'dilla.db', 'aa'.repeat(32)))
      .rejects.toBe(contention);
    expect(sleeps).toEqual([300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500]);
  });
});

class FakeDir {
  constructor(private readonly children: Map<string, FakeDir | Error>) {}
  getDirectoryHandle(name: string): Promise<FakeDir> {
    const child = this.children.get(name);
    if (child === undefined) return Promise.reject(new DOMException(name, 'NotFoundError'));
    if (child instanceof Error) return Promise.reject(child);
    return Promise.resolve(child);
  }
}

describe('opfsDirectoryExists', () => {
  const asRoot = (d: FakeDir) => d as unknown as FileSystemDirectoryHandle;
  it('walks the path and answers whether it exists', async () => {
    const root = new FakeDir(new Map([['dilla', new FakeDir(new Map([[HEX, new FakeDir(new Map())]]))]]));
    expect(await opfsDirectoryExists(asRoot(root), `dilla/${HEX}`)).toBe(true);
    expect(await opfsDirectoryExists(asRoot(root), `dilla/${'cd'.repeat(16)}`)).toBe(false);
    expect(await opfsDirectoryExists(asRoot(new FakeDir(new Map())), 'dilla/x')).toBe(false);
    const file = new FakeDir(new Map([['dilla', new DOMException('a file', 'TypeMismatchError')]]));
    expect(await opfsDirectoryExists(asRoot(file), 'dilla/x')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('propagates any other failure', async () => {
    const denied = new FakeDir(new Map([['dilla', new DOMException('denied', 'SecurityError')]]));
    await expect(opfsDirectoryExists(denied as unknown as FileSystemDirectoryHandle, 'dilla/x')).rejects.toThrow('denied');
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write the fake server and the failing session, signup and KeyPackage tests**

Create `packages/client-core/src/testing/fake-server.ts` (test support; written out because the account tests' assertions depend on its exact answers):

```ts
import { arr, bin, decode, encode, str, u64, type CborInput } from '../cbor';
import { Session } from '../account/session';
import type { CorePort } from '../core-port';
import { fromHex, toHex } from '../hex';
import { HttpClient } from '../http/client';
import { Routes } from '../http/routes';

/** The fixed clock of every account test, in unix seconds. */
export const NOW_S = 1_800_000_000;
export const SESSION_S = 604_800;
export const IDLE_S = 43_200;
/** The nonce of the first challenge; challenge k (1-based) answers nonceAt(k), so every challenge is fresh. */
export const NONCE = new Uint8Array(32).fill(0x6e);
export function nonceAt(k: number): Uint8Array {
  const nonce = NONCE.slice();
  nonce[0] = 0x6e + k - 1;
  return nonce;
}

export interface LoggedRequest { method: string; path: string; auth: string | null; body: Uint8Array }
export type Reply = { status: number; body?: CborInput } | 'network';
interface Account { userId: Uint8Array; username: string; display: string }

function reply(status: number, body?: CborInput): Response {
  if (body === undefined) return new Response(null, { status, headers: { 'X-Dilla-Generation': '1' } });
  return new Response(new Uint8Array(encode(body)), {
    status,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/cbor', 'X-Dilla-Generation': '1' },
  });
}

function refuse(status: number, code: string, detail = ''): Response {
  return reply(status, [code, detail, null]);
}

/** An in-memory model of the account routes of dillad, answering through fetch. */
export class FakeServer {
  readonly log: LoggedRequest[] = [];
  readonly invites = new Set<string>(['INVITE']);
  readonly accounts = new Map<string, Account>();
  readonly devices = new Map<string, string>();
  readonly tokens = new Map<string, string>();
  readonly deviceLists = new Map<string, { version: bigint; blob: Uint8Array }>();
  readonly keyPackages: { device: string; count: number; lastResort: boolean }[] = [];
  scope = 0;
  private users = 0;
  private sessions = 0;
  private challenges = 0;
  private readonly overrides: { method: string; path: string; reply: Reply }[] = [];

  /** The next request with this method and path gets `answer` instead of the model's. */
  once(method: string, path: string, answer: Reply): void {
    this.overrides.push({ method, path, reply: answer });
  }

  count(method: string, path: string): number {
    return this.log.filter((r) => r.method === method && r.path === path).length;
  }

  paths(): string[] {
    return this.log.map((r) => `${r.method} ${r.path}`);
  }

  /** An account and device as if an earlier tab's registration had succeeded. */
  register(username: string, deviceId: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
    this.users += 1;
    const userId = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x30 + this.users);
    this.accounts.set(toHex(userId), { userId, username, display: username });
    this.devices.set(toHex(deviceId), toHex(userId));
    return userId;
  }

  readonly fetch = async (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> => {
    const request = new Request(input, init);
    const header = request.headers.get('Authorization');
    const entry: LoggedRequest = {
      method: request.method,
      path: new URL(request.url).pathname,
      auth: header !== null && header.startsWith('Bearer ') ? header.slice(7) : null,
      body: new Uint8Array(await request.arrayBuffer()),
    };
    this.log.push(entry);
    const i = this.overrides.findIndex((o) => o.method === entry.method && o.path === entry.path);
    const override = i >= 0 ? this.overrides.splice(i, 1)[0] : undefined;
    if (override !== undefined) {
      if (override.reply === 'network') throw new TypeError('fetch failed');
      return reply(override.reply.status, override.reply.body);
    }
    return this.route(entry);
  };

  private route(r: LoggedRequest): Response {
    const line = `${r.method} ${r.path}`;
    if (line === 'POST /v1/accounts') return this.createAccount(r.body);
    if (line === 'GET /v1/instance/limits') {
      return reply(200, [131072, 104857600, 4, 2, 32, 8, 1073741824, 30000, 131584, 30, 30]);
    }
    if (/^POST \/v1\/devices\/[0-9a-f]{32}\/sessions\/challenge$/.test(line)) {
      this.challenges += 1;
      return reply(201, [nonceAt(this.challenges), NOW_S + 60]);
    }
    const establish = /^POST \/v1\/devices\/([0-9a-f]{32})\/sessions$/.exec(line);
    if (establish?.[1] !== undefined) return this.establish(establish[1]);
    const device = r.auth === null ? undefined : this.tokens.get(r.auth);
    const user = device === undefined ? undefined : this.devices.get(device);
    if (device === undefined || user === undefined) return refuse(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED');
    const list = /^(PUT|GET) \/v1\/users\/([0-9a-f]{32})\/device-list$/.exec(line);
    if (list?.[2] !== undefined) return list[1] === 'PUT' ? this.putList(user, list[2], r.body) : this.getList(list[2]);
    if (line === 'POST /v1/keypackages') {
      const b = arr(decode(r.body), 2);
      const count = arr(b[0] ?? null).length;
      this.keyPackages.push({ device, count, lastResort: b[1] !== null });
      return reply(201, [count]);
    }
    if (line === 'GET /v1/accounts/me') {
      const a = this.accounts.get(user);
      if (a === undefined) return refuse(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND');
      return reply(200, [a.userId, a.username, a.display, 0, 0, NOW_S]);
    }
    return new Response('404 page not found\n', { status: 404, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' } });
  }

  private createAccount(body: Uint8Array): Response {
    const b = arr(decode(body), 8);
    const invite = str(b[0] ?? null);
    const username = str(b[1] ?? null);
    const display = str(b[2] ?? null);
    const deviceId = bin(arr(b[7] ?? null, 5)[0] ?? null, 16);
    if (!this.invites.has(invite)) return refuse(410, 'E_INVITE_INVALID');
    if ([...this.accounts.values()].some((a) => a.username === username)) return refuse(409, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST', 'username taken');
    const userId = this.register(username, deviceId);
    const account = this.accounts.get(toHex(userId));
    if (account !== undefined) account.display = display;
    return reply(200, [userId, deviceId, this.mint(toHex(deviceId)), NOW_S + SESSION_S]);
  }

  private mint(deviceHex: string): string {
    this.sessions += 1;
    const token = `tok-${this.sessions}`;
    this.tokens.set(token, deviceHex);
    return token;
  }

  private establish(deviceHex: string): Response {
    const user = this.devices.get(deviceHex);
    if (user === undefined) return refuse(401, 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED');
    return reply(201, [this.mint(deviceHex), this.scope, fromHex(user), fromHex(deviceHex), NOW_S + SESSION_S, NOW_S + IDLE_S, 1]);
  }

  private putList(user: string, target: string, body: Uint8Array): Response {
    if (user !== target) return refuse(403, 'E_FORBIDDEN');
    const b = arr(decode(body), 4);
    if (this.deviceLists.has(target)) return refuse(409, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST', 'device list version exists');
    this.deviceLists.set(target, { version: u64(b[0] ?? null), blob: bin(b[1] ?? null) });
    return reply(204);
  }

  private getList(target: string): Response {
    const l = this.deviceLists.get(target);
    if (l === undefined) return refuse(404, 'E_NOT_FOUND');
    return reply(200, [l.version, l.blob, new Uint8Array(64), new Uint8Array(32)]);
  }
}

export function routesFor(server: FakeServer, auth: { token(): string | null; reauthenticate(): Promise<boolean> }): Routes {
  return new Routes(new HttpClient({
    baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8453',
    fetch: server.fetch as typeof fetch,
    now: () => NOW_S * 1000,
    sleep: () => Promise.resolve(),
    random: () => 0,
    token: () => auth.token(),
    reauthenticate: () => auth.reauthenticate(),
    onGeneration: () => undefined,
  }));
}

/** Routes whose token and 401 recovery come from a Session over `core`, as the worker wires them. */
export function sessionFor(server: FakeServer, core: CorePort): { routes: Routes; session: Session } {
  const holder: { session: Session | null } = { session: null };
  const routes = routesFor(server, {
    token: () => holder.session?.token() ?? null,
    reauthenticate: () => holder.session?.establish() ?? Promise.resolve(false),
  });
  const session = new Session({ core, routes, now: () => NOW_S * 1000 });
  holder.session = session;
  return { routes, session };
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { arr, decode } from '../cbor';
import { toHex } from '../hex';
import { FakeCore } from '../testing/fake-core';
import { FakeServer, IDLE_S, NONCE, nonceAt, NOW_S, SESSION_S, sessionFor } from '../testing/fake-server';
import { RENEW_MARGIN_S } from './session';

const INSTANCE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xab);
const DEVICE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xa1);
const DEV_HEX = toHex(DEVICE);

function setup(registered = true) {
  const server = new FakeServer();
  const userId = registered ? server.register('ada', DEVICE) : new Uint8Array(16).fill(0x99);
  const core = FakeCore.identified({ instanceId: INSTANCE, userId, deviceId: DEVICE, username: 'ada' });
  const { routes, session } = sessionFor(server, core);
  return { server, core, routes, session, userId };
}

describe('Session', () => {
  it('pins the renew margin', () => {
    expect(RENEW_MARGIN_S).toBe(3600);
  });

  it('establishes with a challenge and a purpose-0 signature, and stores the session', async () => {
    const { server, core, session } = setup();
    expect(session.token()).toBeNull();
    expect(await session.establish()).toBe(true);
    expect(server.paths()).toEqual([`POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`, `POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`]);
    expect(server.log.map((r) => r.auth)).toEqual([null, null]);
    expect(decode(server.log[1]?.body ?? new Uint8Array())).toEqual([NONCE, 0n, new Uint8Array(64).fill(6), null, null]);
    expect(core.session()).toEqual({ token: 'tok-1', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + IDLE_S) });
    expect(session.token()).toBe('tok-1');
  });

  it('a stale nonce does not sign the browser out', async () => {
    const { server, core, session } = setup();
    server.once('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`, { status: 401, body: ['E_UNAUTHENTICATED', '', null] });
    expect(await session.establish()).toBe(true);
    expect(server.paths()).toEqual([
      `POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`, `POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`,
      `POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`, `POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`,
    ]);
    const signed = [server.log[1], server.log[3]].map((r) => arr(decode(r?.body ?? new Uint8Array()), 5)[0]);
    expect(signed).toEqual([nonceAt(1), nonceAt(2)]);
    expect(nonceAt(1)).not.toEqual(nonceAt(2));
    expect(core.calls.filter((c) => c === 'sessionSign')).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(core.session()).toEqual({ token: 'tok-1', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + IDLE_S) });
    expect(core.calls).not.toContain('sessionClear');
  });

  it('two refusals in a row are a confirmed refusal', async () => {
    const { server, core, session } = setup(false);
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'stale', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + 10), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + 10) });
    expect(await session.establish()).toBe(false);
    expect(server.count('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`)).toBe(2);
    expect(server.count('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`)).toBe(2);
    expect(core.calls.filter((c) => c === 'sessionClear')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(core.session()).toBeNull();
  });

  it('a confirmed refusal in phase 1 keeps the session record', async () => {
    const server = new FakeServer();
    const core = new FakeCore({ deviceId: DEVICE });
    core.signupBegin(INSTANCE);
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'registered', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S) });
    const { session } = sessionFor(server, core);
    expect(await session.establish()).toBe(false);
    expect(server.count('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`)).toBe(2);
    expect(core.session()).toEqual({ token: 'registered', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S) });
    expect(core.calls).not.toContain('sessionClear');
    expect(core.identity().phase).toBe(1);
  });

  it('propagates a refusal of the challenge without a second attempt', async () => {
    const { server, session } = setup();
    server.once('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`, { status: 401, body: ['E_UNAUTHENTICATED', '', null] });
    await expect(session.establish()).rejects.toMatchObject({ status: 401, code: 'E_UNAUTHENTICATED' });
    expect(server.paths()).toEqual([`POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`]);
  });

  it('establishes once for concurrent callers', async () => {
    const { server, session } = setup();
    expect(await Promise.all([session.establish(), session.establish()])).toEqual([true, true]);
    expect(server.count('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`)).toBe(1);
  });

  it('refuses a session of another scope', async () => {
    const { server, core, session } = setup();
    server.scope = 1;
    await expect(session.establish()).rejects.toThrow('E_SESSION_SCOPE');
    expect(core.session()).toBeNull();
  });

  it('ensure renews only within the margin', async () => {
    const { server, core, session } = setup();
    expect(await session.ensure()).toBe(true);
    expect(server.log).toHaveLength(2);
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'fresh', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + 86_400), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + RENEW_MARGIN_S + 1) });
    expect(await session.ensure()).toBe(true);
    expect(server.log).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(session.token()).toBe('fresh');
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'idle', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + 86_400), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + RENEW_MARGIN_S) });
    expect(await session.ensure()).toBe(true);
    expect(server.log).toHaveLength(4);
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'old', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + RENEW_MARGIN_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + 86_400) });
    expect(await session.ensure()).toBe(true);
    expect(server.log).toHaveLength(6);
  });

  it('ensure answers false for a device the server does not know', async () => {
    const { session } = setup(false);
    expect(await session.ensure()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('re-establishes once when an authenticated request meets 401, then retries it with the new token', async () => {
    const { server, core, routes, userId } = setup();
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'dead', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + 86_400), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + 86_400) });
    await routes.putDeviceList(userId, core.deviceListBody());
    const listPath = `/v1/users/${toHex(userId)}/device-list`;
    expect(server.log.map((r) => [r.method, r.path, r.auth])).toEqual([
      ['PUT', listPath, 'dead'],
      ['POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`, null],
      ['POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`, null],
      ['PUT', listPath, 'tok-1'],
    ]);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { arr, bin, decode } from '../cbor';
import { CoreError } from '../core-port';
import { toHex } from '../hex';
import { DillaHttpError } from '../http/errors';
import { FAKE_RECOVERY_KEY, FakeCore } from '../testing/fake-core';
import { FakeServer, NOW_S, SESSION_S, sessionFor } from '../testing/fake-server';
import { publishDeviceList, Signup } from './signup';

const INSTANCE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xab);
const DEVICE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xa1);
const OTHER = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xb1);
const DEV_HEX = toHex(DEVICE);
const INPUT = { invite: 'INVITE', username: 'ada', display: 'Ada', password: null };

function setup(core = new FakeCore({ deviceId: DEVICE })) {
  const server = new FakeServer();
  const { routes, session } = sessionFor(server, core);
  const signup = new Signup({ core, routes, session, now: () => NOW_S * 1000 });
  return { server, core, routes, session, signup };
}

async function httpError(p: Promise<unknown>): Promise<DillaHttpError> {
  try {
    await p;
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof DillaHttpError) return err;
    throw err;
  }
  throw new Error('nothing was thrown');
}

describe('Signup', () => {
  it('begins with the recovery key in 13 groups of 4', () => {
    const { signup, core } = setup();
    const groups = signup.begin(INSTANCE);
    expect(groups).toHaveLength(13);
    expect(groups.every((g) => g.length === 4)).toBe(true);
    expect(groups.join('')).toBe(FAKE_RECOVERY_KEY);
    expect(core.identity().phase).toBe(1);
    expect(() => signup.begin(INSTANCE)).toThrow(CoreError);
  });

  it('registers, stores the session, signs the device list, publishes it and the KeyPackages, in that order', async () => {
    const { signup, core, server } = setup();
    signup.begin(INSTANCE);
    await signup.submit(INPUT);
    const userId = core.identity().userId;
    if (userId === null) throw new Error('no user id');
    const listPath = `/v1/users/${toHex(userId)}/device-list`;
    expect(server.paths()).toEqual(['POST /v1/accounts', `PUT ${listPath}`, 'GET /v1/instance/limits', 'POST /v1/keypackages']);
    expect(server.log.map((r) => r.auth)).toEqual([null, 'tok-1', null, 'tok-1']);
    const steps = ['signupRequest', 'sessionStore', 'signupComplete', 'deviceListPublished', 'keyPackages'];
    expect(core.calls.filter((c) => steps.includes(c))).toEqual(steps);
    const account = arr(decode(server.log[0]?.body ?? new Uint8Array()), 8);
    expect(account.slice(0, 3)).toEqual(['INVITE', 'ada', 'Ada']);
    expect(account[6]).toBeNull();
    expect(core.identity()).toEqual({ phase: 2, instanceId: INSTANCE, userId, deviceId: DEVICE, username: 'ada', listPublished: true });
    expect(core.session()).toEqual({ token: 'tok-1', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S) });
    const list = arr(decode(server.log[1]?.body ?? new Uint8Array()), 4);
    expect(decode(bin(list[1] ?? null))).toEqual(['fake.list', userId, DEVICE, BigInt(NOW_S)]);
    expect(server.keyPackages).toEqual([{ device: DEV_HEX, count: 32, lastResort: true }]);
  });

  it('keeps phase 1 when the server refuses, and a second submit with other fields succeeds', async () => {
    const { signup, core, server } = setup();
    server.register('ada', OTHER);
    signup.begin(INSTANCE);
    const taken = await httpError(signup.submit(INPUT));
    expect([taken.status, taken.code, taken.detail]).toEqual([409, 'E_INVALID_REQUEST', 'username taken']);
    expect(core.identity().phase).toBe(1);
    expect(core.session()).toBeNull();
    const invalid = await httpError(signup.submit({ ...INPUT, username: 'grace', invite: 'NOPE' }));
    expect([invalid.status, invalid.code]).toEqual([410, 'E_INVITE_INVALID']);
    expect(server.paths().filter((p) => p.startsWith('PUT'))).toEqual([]);
    await signup.submit({ ...INPUT, username: 'grace' });
    expect(core.identity()).toMatchObject({ phase: 2, username: 'grace', listPublished: true });
  });

  it('never repeats a registration blindly after a network failure', async () => {
    const { signup, core, server } = setup();
    server.once('POST', '/v1/accounts', 'network');
    signup.begin(INSTANCE);
    const lost = await httpError(signup.submit(INPUT));
    expect([lost.status, lost.code]).toEqual([0, 'E_NETWORK']);
    expect(server.count('POST', '/v1/accounts')).toBe(1);
    expect(core.identity().phase).toBe(1);
    expect(core.session()).toBeNull();
  });

  it('resumes after a reload when the earlier registration went through', async () => {
    const { core, server } = setup();
    core.signupBegin(INSTANCE);
    const userId = server.register('ada', DEVICE);
    const { signup } = (() => {
      const { routes, session } = sessionFor(server, core);
      return { signup: new Signup({ core, routes, session, now: () => NOW_S * 1000 }) };
    })();
    expect(await signup.resume()).toBe(2);
    expect(core.identity()).toEqual({ phase: 2, instanceId: INSTANCE, userId, deviceId: DEVICE, username: 'ada', listPublished: true });
    expect(server.paths().slice(0, 3)).toEqual([`POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions/challenge`, `POST /v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`,
      'GET /v1/accounts/me']);
    expect(server.deviceLists.get(toHex(userId))?.version).toBe(1n);
    expect(server.keyPackages).toEqual([{ device: DEV_HEX, count: 32, lastResort: true }]);
  });

  it('a resumed signup that was never registered starts over', async () => {
    const { signup, core, server } = setup();
    signup.begin(INSTANCE);
    expect(await signup.resume()).toBe(0);
    expect(server.count('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`)).toBe(2);
    expect(core.calls).toContain('signupReset');
    expect(core.identity().phase).toBe(0);
    expect(server.paths().filter((p) => p.startsWith('PUT'))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a resumed signup with a stored session is never reset', async () => {
    const { signup, core, server } = setup();
    signup.begin(INSTANCE);
    core.sessionStore({ token: 'registered', expires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S), idleExpires: BigInt(NOW_S + SESSION_S) });
    expect(await signup.resume()).toBe('revoked');
    expect(server.count('POST', `/v1/devices/${DEV_HEX}/sessions`)).toBe(2);
    expect(core.calls).not.toContain('signupReset');
    expect(core.calls).not.toContain('sessionClear');
    expect(core.identity().phase).toBe(1);
    expect(core.session()).not.toBeNull();
    expect(server.paths().filter((p) => p.startsWith('PUT'))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('resume does nothing outside phase 1', async () => {
    const { signup, server } = setup();
    expect(await signup.resume()).toBe(0);
    expect(server.log).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('publishDeviceList', () => {
  function identified(server: FakeServer, listPublished: boolean) {
    const userId = server.register('ada', DEVICE);
    const core = FakeCore.identified({ instanceId: INSTANCE, userId, deviceId: DEVICE, username: 'ada', listPublished });
    const { routes, session } = sessionFor(server, core);
    return { core, routes, session, userId };
  }

  it('does nothing when the list is already published', async () => {
    const server = new FakeServer();
    const { core, routes } = identified(server, true);
    await publishDeviceList(core, routes);
    expect(server.log).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('treats a 409 as published when the server already holds version 1', async () => {
    const server = new FakeServer();
    const { core, routes, session, userId } = identified(server, false);
    await session.establish();
    server.deviceLists.set(toHex(userId), { version: 1n, blob: new Uint8Array([1]) });
    await publishDeviceList(core, routes);
    expect(core.identity().listPublished).toBe(true);
    expect(server.paths().slice(-2)).toEqual([`PUT /v1/users/${toHex(userId)}/device-list`, `GET /v1/users/${toHex(userId)}/device-list`]);
  });

  it('rethrows a 409 when the server holds no list', async () => {
    const server = new FakeServer();
    const { core, routes, session, userId } = identified(server, false);
    await session.establish();
    server.once('PUT', `/v1/users/${toHex(userId)}/device-list`, { status: 409, body: ['E_INVALID_REQUEST', 'x', null] });
    const err = await httpError(publishDeviceList(core, routes));
    expect(err.status).toBe(409);
    expect(core.identity().listPublished).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

Create `packages/client-core/src/account/keypackages.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { toHex } from '../hex';
import { FakeCore } from '../testing/fake-core';
import { FakeServer, sessionFor } from '../testing/fake-server';
import { refillKeyPackages } from './keypackages';

const DEVICE = new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xa1);
const LIMITS = { perDevice: 32, threshold: 8 };

async function setup() {
  const server = new FakeServer();
  const userId = server.register('ada', DEVICE);
  const core = FakeCore.identified({ instanceId: new Uint8Array(16).fill(0xab), userId, deviceId: DEVICE, username: 'ada' });
  const { routes, session } = sessionFor(server, core);
  await session.establish();
  return { server, core, routes };
}

describe('refillKeyPackages', () => {
  it('does nothing at or above the threshold', async () => {
    const { server, core, routes } = await setup();
    expect(await refillKeyPackages(core, routes, 8, LIMITS)).toBe(0);
    expect(server.count('POST', '/v1/keypackages')).toBe(0);
  });

  it('tops up to the per-device count without a last-resort package', async () => {
    const { server, core, routes } = await setup();
    expect(await refillKeyPackages(core, routes, 7, LIMITS)).toBe(25);
    expect(server.keyPackages).toEqual([{ device: toHex(DEVICE), count: 25, lastResort: false }]);
  });

  it('publishes the full set and a last-resort package from zero', async () => {
    const { server, core, routes } = await setup();
    expect(await refillKeyPackages(core, routes, 0, LIMITS)).toBe(32);
    expect(server.keyPackages).toEqual([{ device: toHex(DEVICE), count: 32, lastResort: true }]);
  });

  it('never asks the core for more than 32', async () => {
    const { server, core, routes } = await setup();
    expect(await refillKeyPackages(core, routes, 0, { perDevice: 40, threshold: 8 })).toBe(32);
    expect(server.keyPackages[0]?.count).toBe(32);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement `core-port.ts` and `core-wasm-conformance.ts`**

- Copy the ledger's L-TS-03 types verbatim, then the `CoreHandle`, `StoreOpenConfigLike` and `CoreWasmModule` interfaces of the Produces block.
- `CoreError`: `super(detail === '' ? code : `${code}: ${detail}`)`; `this.name = 'CoreError'`; `static from` per R15-3.
- `wrapCore(handle)` returns an object literal implementing `CorePort`. A private `call<T>(method: string, fn: () => T): T` runs `fn` and rethrows `CoreError.from(err)`; a private `decoded<T>(method: string, bytes: Uint8Array, read: (v: CborValue) => T): T` runs `read(decode(bytes))` and converts a `CborError` or a range check failure into `CoreError('E_CORE_DECODE', `${method}: ${reason}`)`. One private reader per result shape (`readIdentity`, `readSession`, `readGroup`, `readApply`, `readWelcome`, `readOutbox`, `readTimeline`), each using only `arr(v, n)`, `u64`, `u53`, `bin(v, 16)`, `str` and `opt`. `resume()` is `async` and awaits `handle.resume()` inside the same conversion.
- `core-wasm-conformance.ts`: exactly the import and the two constants of R15-4, with a module doc comment saying it is type-only and needs the WASM gate. If `npm run lint` reports a rule on this file, add a `// eslint-disable-next-line <that rule> -- type-only conformance check` on the reported line only.

- [ ] **Step 8: Implement `testing/fake-core.ts`**

File header comment (exact): `/** The account half of CorePort for unit tests: identity phases, signup, the session record, the device list flags, KeyPackages, pause/resume/close. Every group, commit, send, outbox and timeline method throws CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'not modelled'); the group half is ModelCore (src/sync/testing/model.ts), held to the Rust core by L-CORE-10. Not exported from src/index.ts. */`

Private model: `identity` fields (phase, instance, user, device, username, listPublished, list body); `session: SessionRecord | null`; `tier`; `paused`, `closed`, `failures: Map<string, CoreError>`, `counter`. Every public `CorePort` method starts with `this.enter('<name>')`, which appends to `calls`, throws a queued `failOnce` error (removing it), and throws `E_STORE_PAUSED` when paused or closed (R15-29, R15-30); `resume` does the same check against `closed` only and clears `paused`. Implement R15-21 and R15-22 in the methods they name; `signupReset` checks the phase first (phase 0 and 2 details of R15-22), then `session !== null` (detail `the account is registered`), and only then clears anything. Each of the 23 methods of R15-23 keeps the full `CorePort` parameter list (the tests call them with arguments) and its body is the single statement `return this.notModelled('<name>', <every parameter>)`, where the private `notModelled(name: string, ...args: unknown[]): never` calls `this.enter(name)` and then throws `new CoreError('E_CORE_STATE', 'not modelled')`; passing the parameters on keeps every one of them used, so no lint suppression is needed. The opaque encodings of R15-21 are built with `encode`; no other blob format exists in the file.

- [ ] **Step 9: Implement `account/kek.ts`**

- A private `openDb(idb)` returns `Promise<IDBDatabase>` from `idb.open(KEK_DB, KEK_DB_VERSION)`: `onupgradeneeded` creates the store when absent (R15-40); `onsuccess` resolves `request.result`; `onerror` rejects with `request.error`.
- A private `inTx<T>(idb, mode, act: (store: IDBObjectStore, done: (value: T) => void, fail: (err: unknown) => void) => void): Promise<T>` opens, starts `db.transaction(KEK_STORE, mode)`, runs `act`, settles once (the first of `done`/`fail` wins), and closes the database in a `finally` (R15-44). Reads call `done` from the request's `onsuccess`; writes call `done` from `tx.oncomplete`; `request.onerror` calls `fail(request.error)`; `tx.onabort` calls `fail(tx.error)`.
- `create`: R15-41, with `Error('E_KEK_EXISTS')` when the failure's `name` is `ConstraintError`. `load`: R15-42; the shape check uses `typeof rec === 'object'`, `rec.v === 1`, `rec.iv instanceof Uint8Array && rec.iv.length === 12`, `rec.ct instanceof Uint8Array && rec.ct.length === 48`, `typeof rec.wrapKey === 'object' && rec.wrapKey !== null`; any shape failure or decrypt rejection → `Error('E_KEK_UNWRAP')`. `remove`: R15-43. The additional data is built once per call as a fresh `Uint8Array` of `12 + 16` bytes.

`storeDirectory(hex)` returns `` `dilla/${hex}` ``. `boot` follows R15-50 step by step (each `store-lost` decision is a `return`, not a throw); the zero-fill sits in a `finally` attached to the `openCore` await only. `wasmCoreOpener` follows R15-51 with a `for` loop over attempts 1..6. `opfsDirectoryExists` follows R15-52; it awaits each `getDirectoryHandle` in sequence and checks `err instanceof DOMException && (err.name === 'NotFoundError' || err.name === 'TypeMismatchError')`.

- [ ] **Step 11: Implement `account/session.ts`, `account/signup.ts`, `account/keypackages.ts`**

## Unit `client-sync` — task 16

### Task 16: The TypeScript half of sync (C1, C12)

> **Ledger notes (read first).** Every matter the first draft raised is settled by the plan head as
> adjudicated on 2026-10-05, and this task follows it literally: the engine tests run against
> `ModelCore`, the group-half model of `CorePort` that this task owns, and against nothing else —
> L-TS-03 now fixes the split of the two doubles (the account-half double of task 15 is not used
> here), and `ModelCore` is held to the Rust core by the parity replay of L-CORE-10 (this task's
> `parity.test.ts`); `SyncRoutes`, `SyncGateway`, `onMembership` and `SyncError` are ledger items
> (L-TS-07); the result shapes of the routes (`raw`, `count`, `lastSeq`, `lastId`) and the two error
> constructors are fixed by L-HTTP-20…45 and L-TS-03; the `through` computation is L-TS-07 rule 2
> as amended (ruling 28), op 21 is honoured (ruling 17 as amended), a Welcome is deleted only after
> a working membership, and the cursor is also posted, debounced, after live frames
> (`SYNC.cursorDebounceMs`). Nothing here changes a Rust, Go or wire interface.
>
> **Amended after the core hardening (2026-10-05).** The Rust core changed after this task was first
> drafted (plan head, "Amended after the core hardening"), and this task now follows it: `ModelCore`
> skips a message row at a stored seq, adopts an own echo only through the commitment it carries and
> for any unresolved outbox row (queued, in flight or failed), confirms at an occupied seq the way
> `send_confirm` does, never lowers `nextSeq`, keeps a floor (`maxEpoch`) and refuses rejoins at or
> below it, returns a discarded rejoin of a gone row to state 4 with its history, refuses joins that
> name another group or rebind a row, and refuses a Welcome whose epoch or tree hash is not its
> served label (`3f26670`); its floor is written when an epoch is reached, never at a deletion;
> `ModelDs` serves every message row with the commitment of its upload (kept when the row is
> deleted) and labels every Welcome with the true epoch and tree hash. The engine re-reads the
> outbox after an adoption (requirement 16), handles a `sendConfirm` refusal without `sendFail`
> (requirement 25), bounds the re-read of a join refused with `E_CORE_INPUT` (requirements 30 and
> 33), and treats the delivery service's leaf-binding refusals as permanent: a `422` on a commit
> makes the group commit-quiet (requirement 18), and a `400 E_INVALID_REQUEST` on a registration or
> a `422` on a join propagates once (requirements 30 and 31; hardening G). The parity fixture is
> unchanged.
>
> **Code-vs-facts note.** `facts/interfaces.md` A4.5 item 9 says the 409 loser must "clear pending
> on refusal". In OpenMLS 0.9.0 `MlsGroup::merge_staged_commit` "also clears any pending commits"
> (`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/openmls-0.9.0/src/group/mls_group/processing.rs:462-463`),
> so after a 409 the abort is functionally load-bearing only when the winner is not applied in the
> same breath (425, 422, a failed catch-up). The code wins: `ModelCore` clears a pending commit on
> every staged merge, and the conflict test pins the **order** of core calls (abort before the
> catch-up) rather than a symptom, which is what makes mutation (c) observable.

- Produces: **L-TS-07** (`src/sync/engine.ts`), exactly as the ledger states it (including `SyncRoutes`, `SyncGateway`, `onMembership`, `SyncError` and `SYNC.cursorDebounceMs`), plus `PageInfo` and `throughOf`, which `engine.ts` exports for its unit test only:

  ```ts
  export type SyncRoutes = Pick<Routes, 'listChannels' | 'postGroup' | 'getGroupInfo' | 'getGroupTree' | 'getHandshakes' | 'getMessages'
    | 'getProposals' | 'postCommit' | 'postMessage' | 'postCursor' | 'postResync' | 'getWelcomes' | 'deleteWelcome'>;
  export type SyncGateway = Pick<Gateway, 'subscribe' | 'commitAck'>;
  export interface SyncDeps { core: CorePort; routes: SyncRoutes; gateway: SyncGateway; instance: Instance; deviceId: Id;
    now(): number; random(): number; setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): number; clearTimeout(id: number): void;
    onGroupChanged(groupId: Id, result: ApplyResult): void; onOutboxChanged(groupId: Id): void;
    onMembership(groupId: Id, status: 'resyncing' | 'not-member'): void; }
  export class SyncEngine {

    start(): void; stop(): void;

    setChannels(channels: ExpectedGroup[]): void;

  export const SYNC = { handshakePage: 512, messagePage: 256, commitRetryMax: 5, commitJitterMs: 400,
    membershipWaitMs: 2000, echoWaitMs: 5000, registerRetryMax: 3, cursorDebounceMs: 30000 } as const;
  export interface PageInfo { count: number; lastSeq: bigint | null; }

   *  message page (read first), `hs` the handshake page (read second), `carry` the handshake page's
   *  lastSeq of the previous round of the same catch-up (null in the first round). */
  export function throughOf(ms: PageInfo, hs: PageInfo, carry: bigint | null): bigint;
  ```

  ```ts
  // src/sync/errors.ts
  export type SyncErrorCode = 'E_SYNC_STOPPED' | 'E_REGISTER_RACE' | 'E_CHANNEL_GONE' | 'E_NO_COMMUNITY';
  export class SyncError extends Error {
    readonly code: SyncErrorCode;
    readonly detail: string;
    constructor(code: SyncErrorCode, detail?: string);   // name 'SyncError'; message `${code}` or `${code}: ${detail}`
  }
  // src/sync/group-queue.ts
  export class SerialQueues {
    /** Queues job behind every job of key; never starts it synchronously; resolves or rejects with the job. */
    run<T>(key: string, job: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
    /** Queues job unless a job with the same tag is already waiting (not started) on key. Its error is swallowed. */
    coalesce(key: string, tag: string, job: () => Promise<void>): boolean;
    /** True when key has no running and no waiting job. */
    idle(key: string): boolean;
    /** Drops every waiting job (its run() promise rejects with SyncError('E_SYNC_STOPPED')); running jobs finish. */
    clear(): void;
  }
  ```
  Test support (not ledger interfaces; consumed only by this task's tests): the exports of `src/sync/testing/model.ts` and `src/sync/testing/harness.ts` written out in Step 1.

**Requirements:**

Queues and lifecycle
1. Every core call and every HTTP call about a group runs inside a job of that group's queue `g:<group hex>`; jobs of one key run strictly one after another; jobs of different keys run concurrently. Channel opening runs on `c:<channel hex>` and calls into the group's queue for every group-scoped step; the multi-group welcome poll and every op-20 frame run on the key `w` (requirement 15c says why). (L-TS-07 rule 1, `plan-head.md:1132`; C1)
2. Exception to requirement 1, stated because the ledger forces it: `send()` returns the message id synchronously, so it calls `core.sendPrepare` outside the queue. That call only appends a state-0 outbox row, which no queue step can observe half-done (a core call is synchronous and JavaScript runs it between two queue steps). (L-TS-07 `send(…): Id`)
3. `SerialQueues.run` never starts a job synchronously; a rejected job does not stop the queue; `coalesce` returns false while a job with the same tag waits (a running one does not count) and swallows the job's rejection; `clear()` rejects every waiting job's `run()` promise with `SyncError('E_SYNC_STOPPED')` and does not interrupt running jobs.
4. `start()` subscribes to the gateway and does nothing else (a `ready` emitted before `start()` is not replayed; task 18 calls `start()` before `Gateway.start()`). `start()` twice subscribes once. `stop()` unsubscribes, clears every timer the engine armed (volunteer, conflict retry, membership wait, echo wait, join wait, cursor), calls `SerialQueues.clear()` and sets the engine stopped: afterwards no job starts, a running job returns before its next HTTP call, `send` throws `SyncError('E_SYNC_STOPPED')` synchronously and `openChannel` rejects with it. (L-TS-07)
5. No background job ever leaves a rejected promise behind: every job the engine queues on its own catches its errors after acting on them (an unhandled rejection fails the vitest run).
6. The engine never parses an MLS object: it reads only CBOR positions of frames (`seq`, `round`, op 21's `[seq, deleted_at]`), of the cursor body (`[last_seq, last_epoch]`), of the proposals body (the `void` flag of each row) and of a welcomes row; everything else is passed to the core as received. It never reads a `CoreError.detail` or a `DillaHttpError.detail`. (Architect ruling 2, `plan-head.md:1583`; Global Constraints "Copy rules")
7. No string literal, JSX-like text or comment in `src/sync/**` contains a word of `scripts/check-ui-copy.mjs:5-11` (`MLS`, `encrypted`, `encryption`, `E2E`, `E2EE`, `end-to-end`, `team`, …): the lint's text heuristic (`check-ui-copy.mjs:17-34`) also reads comments between a `>` and a `<`. Codes such as `E_CORE_MLS` do not match (`\bMLS\b` does not fire after `_`). (F10, L-CI-03)

Catch-up (rule 2)
8. On every gateway `ready`: store the `ReadyInfo`; clear the per-ready sets (`resyncTried`, `quiet`); for every row of `info.groups` with `proposalsOutstanding > 0` whose local group is in state 2, arm the volunteer timer (requirement 21); then queue on `w` the welcome step (requirement 10) and, after it finished (whatever its outcome), for every local group from `core.groups()`: state 2 → request a catch-up and then a drain (both coalesced on the group's queue, so the drain runs after the catch-up; a row left queued by a `401`, requirement 26, or by a commit-quiet group, requirement 25, goes out after the next `ready`); state 3 → request a resync (requirement 33). (L-TS-07 rule 2; C12, C19; `facts/interfaces.md:312` A4.5 item 5)
9. A catch-up of group `g` (a coalesced job, tag `catch-up`, or run inline by a job already on `g`'s queue) cancels the group's cursor timer (requirement 9b), sets `carry: bigint | null = null` and loops: read the group row; return unless its state is 2; `from = nextSeq`; **first** `ms = await getMessages(g, from, SYNC.messagePage)`, **then** `hs = await getHandshakes(g, from, SYNC.handshakePage)` (sequentially, in that order); `through = throughOf(ms, hs, carry)`; when `through >= from`: `groupApply(g, hs.raw, ms.raw, through)` and handle its result (requirement 16); then `carry = hs.lastSeq`; leave the loop when the group's state is no longer 2, or when neither page was full and not (`hs.lastSeq !== null && hs.lastSeq > through`); otherwise loop. After the loop, when the group is still in state 2: `cursorBody(g)`; when not null, `postCursor(g, body)` and on success `cursorAcked(g, last_seq, last_epoch)` with the two values decoded from that body. A refused or failed `postCursor` is left for the next catch-up. (L-TS-07 rule 2 as amended, `plan-head.md:1133-1137`; ruling 28, `plan-head.md:1612`; A4.5 item 12, `facts/interfaces.md:319`)
9b. After a live `groupApply` (requirement 15, `seq == nextSeq`) that left the group in state 2, when no cursor timer is armed for the group, arm one with `deps.setTimeout(…, SYNC.cursorDebounceMs)` through the engine's tracked timers (an armed timer is not re-armed or extended). When it fires it removes its entry and queues a job on `g`'s queue: read the row; return unless state 2; `cursorBody(g)`; when not null `postCursor(g, body)` and on success `cursorAcked(g, last_seq, last_epoch)`, exactly as at the end of a catch-up; a failure is left for the next timer or catch-up (the job catches it). A catch-up of the group (requirement 9) and `stop()` cancel the timer. Without it a session that stays connected for days never moves the server's retention floor. (L-TS-07 rule 3 "Cursor after live frames"; FACTS-SECURITY-11)
10. `throughOf(ms, hs, carry): bigint` (exported from `engine.ts` for its unit test): a page is full when its `count` equals its route's page size (`SYNC.messagePage` for `ms`, `SYNC.handshakePage` for `hs`). `m = ms.lastSeq`, `h = hs.lastSeq`. `boundM = m` when the message page is full (then `m` is not null), else `max(m ?? 0n, carry ?? 0n)`. `boundH = h` when the handshake page is full, else `max(h ?? 0n, m ?? 0n)`. The result is `min(boundM, boundH)`. Reason: the two reads are not a snapshot. A short message page holds every message that existed when it was read, which was after the previous round's handshake read (`carry`); a short handshake page holds every handshake that existed when it was read, which was after this round's message read; `through` may only name a seq both streams are complete up to. Taking the highest `lastSeq` instead skips a row stored between the two reads for good: the message below a later commit is passed by `next_seq`, and its live frame is then dropped as old. Cost: two reads when only messages are new, four when a handshake is new. (L-TS-07 rule 2 as amended; architect rulings 4 and 28, `plan-head.md:1585, 1612`)
11. Catch-up errors: `410 E_PRUNED` on either read → the inline resync of requirement 33 (once per ready); any other `DillaHttpError` or a `CoreError` from `groupApply` ends this catch-up with the group unchanged (the next ready or gap retries it). (rule 2; A3.12 `E_PRUNED`, `facts/interfaces.md:239`)
12. The welcome step (used by requirement 8 and rule 6): `after = 0n`; loop `getWelcomes(after)`; stop when `count` is 0; `welcomesApply(raw, expected)` with `expected` = the `setChannels` list plus every channel `openChannel` was called for (deduplicated by group id); then the outcome handling, which op 20 (requirement 15c) shares: `deleteWelcome(welcomeId)` (its failure is ignored) for outcome 0, and for outcome 1 only when the row of that group in `core.groups()` is in state 2; a Welcome judged outcome 1 while the row is in state 0 or 1 stays on the server (the join in flight may still be refused, and the Welcome is then the way in) and is judged again by the next welcome step; for outcome 0 the group is activated (requirement 34); `after = lastId`; stop when `count < 64`. Outcomes 2 and 3 leave the Welcome on the server, whatever the reason: since the core hardening a Welcome at or below the epoch floor (`E_CORE_INPUT`), one whose epoch or tree hash is not its served label (`E_CORE_INPUT`, `3f26670`) and one for a row bound to another channel (`E_CORE_STATE`) are outcome 2 as well; the engine does not switch on the reason, and such a Welcome is judged again by each later welcome step until the server expires it (bounded: one judgement per step). A failed `getWelcomes` ends the step. (L-TS-07 rule 2 as amended; FACTS-SECURITY-09; A4.5 item 14; protocol/02 "`DELETE /v1/welcomes/{id}` only after a successful join")

Live frames (rule 3)
13. Frame events are handled synchronously in the listener: a frame whose `groupId` is null is ignored; op 18 is ignored (it carries nothing the rows do not; L-TS-07 rule 3); op 17 is requirement 19; ops 16 and 19 each queue one job on `g:<groupId hex>` (requirements 14 and 15); op 21 queues one job on `g:<groupId hex>` (requirement 15b); op 20 queues one job on `w` (requirement 15c). No frame job is coalesced: each frame is its own job, in arrival order. Every other opcode is ignored.
14. An op-16 or op-19 frame job reads the group row: no row, state 3 or state 4 → drop the frame (state 3: the resync fetches it); state 0 or 1 → append it to the group's held list (at most `HELD_MAX = 512` frames per group, a private constant; on overflow drop the oldest) to be replayed by requirement 34; state 2 → normalise and apply. A payload that does not have the documented shape (a `CborError` from `arr`/`u64`/`bin`, a wrong length: op 16 five elements, op 19 six) drops the frame and requests a catch-up of the group.
15. Normalising: op 16 → `handshakes = encode([[seq, epoch, kind, sender, blob]])`, `messages = encode([])`; op 19 → `handshakes = encode([])`, `messages = encode([[seq, epoch, uploader_device, blob, null, franking_tag, recv_ts, 0]])` (commitment null, deleted 0). Then: `seq < nextSeq` → drop; `seq > nextSeq` → run the catch-up of requirement 9 inline (no `groupApply` for the frame itself); `seq == nextSeq` → `groupApply(g, handshakes, messages, seq)`, requirement 16 with source `frame`, and requirement 9b. (rule 3; architect ruling 4)
15b. An op-21 job (`message.deleted`): the payload must be `[seq uint, deleted_at uint]` (exactly two elements read with `u64`; a malformed payload drops the frame, with no catch-up); read the group row; no row or state 4 → drop; else `result = core.messageDeleted(g, seq)` and, when `result.newSeqs.length > 0`, `onGroupChanged(g, result)`. A `CoreError` drops the frame. Op 21 is applied in states 0, 1, 2 and 3 alike (L-CORE-08 `message_deleted`: any state but 4) and is never held. The delivery service fans op 21 only for the uploader's own deletes, so no author rule is needed; a message deleted before this device fetched it arrives as a row with `deleted = 1` instead. (L-TS-07 rule 3 as amended; ruling 17 as amended, `plan-head.md:1598`; FACTS-SECURITY-08)
15c. An op-20 job runs on `w`, not on the group's queue: a Welcome is judged against the state of its group's row, which an external join on the group's queue changes, and it must see a join in flight (state 1) to keep the Welcome on the server (requirement 12); the welcome step runs on `w` for the same reason. The payload must be `[welcome_id uint, epoch uint, commit_seq uint, blob bstr, ratchet_tree bstr, tree_hash b32]` (six elements; a malformed payload drops the frame); then `welcomesApply(encode([[welcome_id, groupId, epoch, commit_seq, blob, ratchet_tree, tree_hash]]), expected)` with requirement 12's `expected` and outcome handling (activation of an outcome-0 group is queued on that group's queue and not awaited). A `CoreError` from `welcomesApply` drops the frame. (rule 3; FACTS-SECURITY-09)
16. After every `groupApply` and `commitConfirm` (the "apply hook"): `onGroupChanged(g, result)`; when `ownAdopted` → re-read `outbox(g)` (an adoption may have resolved a queued, an in-flight or a failed row: the core adopts any unresolved row whose upload the server stored, L-CORE-08 as amended; the engine assumes nothing about a row it saw before), forget the 425 count of every message id no longer listed, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, and when an echo wait is armed for `g` and its row is no longer in the outbox in state 1 → cancel it and request a drain; when `epochChanged` → when a membership wait is armed for `g` cancel it and request a drain, otherwise request a drain when `outbox(g)` has a state-0 row and no echo wait is armed (this is also the drain that a send held back by a commit-quiet group waits for, requirement 25); when the result's state is 3 → the job continues with the resync of requirement 33 (inline, once per ready); when the result's state is 2 and the source is not the commit path (requirement 22) → arm the volunteer timer when `proposalsPending > 0`, disarm it when it is 0.

Commit duty (rule 4)
17. A commit (a coalesced job on `g`, tag `commit`, carrying an attempt number starting at 0): read the row; return unless state 2; when the row has `pendingCommit` the core refuses the build, which requirement 18 handles (the engine does not abort pre-emptively — that would mask mutation (c)); `getProposals(g)`; when the body has no row whose `void` element is 0 and the row's `proposalsPending` is 0 → return (nothing to commit); `body = commitBuild(g, proposals)`; `postCommit(g, body)`; on success `commitConfirm(g)`, the apply hook (source commit; its `epochChanged` branch requests the drain of any message that waited for this commit), disarm the volunteer timer, clear `quiet` for `g`. The commit function answers `true` when it ended with `commitConfirm`, `false` otherwise (requirement 25 reads it). (rule 4; A4.5 item 9; protocol/02 `:83`)
18. Commit failures, each after `commitAbort(g)` first: `409 E_COMMIT_CONFLICT` → inline catch-up (commit path), then when the group's `proposalsPending > 0` and `attempt < SYNC.commitRetryMax` arm a timer of `random() × SYNC.commitJitterMs` that requests a commit with `attempt + 1`; when the attempts are exhausted add `g` to `quiet`; `425 E_COMMIT_REQUIRED` → inline catch-up (commit path); `422` (any code and rule: `E_COMMIT_INVALID` with `structural`, `add_key_package`, `group_info` (hardening G), …) → inline catch-up (commit path), then add `g` to `quiet` (a 422 refuses that commit for good: it is never retried in a loop, and the group is volunteered for again only after the next `ready` or op 17 for it); `403 E_LEAF_NOT_CURRENT` → inline resync (requirement 33); every other `DillaHttpError` (including status 0 and 500) → nothing more. A `CoreError` from `commitBuild` → `commitAbort(g)` and stop. Every one of these exits ends by requesting a drain of `g` (a send that found the commit in flight returned and waits for exactly this request, requirement 25; the drain is coalesced and returns at once when the outbox has no state-0 row). (rule 4; L-TS-07 rule 5 "the commit path in flight requests a drain when it confirms or aborts"; A3.12 `facts/interfaces.md:236, 242-243`; S:605)
19. Op 17 for `g`: when the local group is in state 2, call `gateway.commitAck(g, round)` synchronously inside the listener, disarm the volunteer timer, remove `g` from `quiet`, and request a commit (attempt 0). Op 17 for a group that is not in state 2 is neither acknowledged nor held: it is never replayed, an unacknowledged round only advances the election, and the volunteer path covers the proposals once the group is active (L-TS-07 rule 4). (protocol/02 invariant 7, `protocol/02-delivery-service.md:392-399`)
20. Volunteer delay: `backoffMs + random() × backoffJitterMs` from the last `ReadyInfo`, or `300 + random() × 300` before the first `ready` (`facts/interfaces.md:302`; protocol/02 `:156`).
21. Arming the volunteer timer is a no-op when one is already armed for `g` or when `g` is in `quiet`; when it fires it requests a commit (attempt 0). (rule 4; A4.5 item 8)
22. The catch-ups that the commit path runs (requirement 18) do not arm or disarm the volunteer timer; a group in `quiet` is not volunteered for until the next `ready` or op 17 for it; otherwise the volunteer rule would re-arm a commit after every capped attempt and the cap would end nothing. (L-TS-07 rule 4)

Sending (rule 5)
23. `send(g, text)`: when stopped throw `SyncError('E_SYNC_STOPPED')`; `msgId = core.sendPrepare(g, text, BigInt(Math.floor(now() / 1000)))` (its `CoreError` — `E_CORE_INPUT` for an empty body, `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT` above 4000 UTF-8 bytes, `E_CORE_STATE` when the group is not active — is thrown synchronously to the caller); `onOutboxChanged(g)`; request a drain; return `msgId`. (rule 5; L-CORE-09)
24. A drain (a coalesced job on `g`, tag `drain`) sends at most one row and then requests the next drain: return when an echo wait is armed for `g`; `rows = outbox(g)`; a row in state 1 (left by a lost response or a page that died) → the lost-response procedure (requirement 27) for it and return; else the first row in state 0 (the core orders by `created`, `msg_id`) → requirement 25; none → return. Return when the group is not in state 2 (rows stay queued; activation requests a drain). (rule 5; architect ruling 5, `plan-head.md:1586`)
25. Sending one row: `sendEncrypt(msgId)`. A `CoreError` with code `E_CORE_STATE` is not a failure of the row (the core changed nothing; the row stays in state 0). Read the group's row from `core.groups()`: `pendingCommit` → return (the commit path in flight requests a drain when it confirms or aborts, requirements 17 and 18); `proposalsPending > 0` → when `g` is in `quiet` (commit-quiet), return — the `epochChanged` branch of requirement 16 requests the drain on the group's next epoch change, and requirement 8 on the next `ready`; otherwise run the commit duty for the group now (the commit function of requirement 17 with attempt 0, called inline: the drain is already a job on `g`'s queue), and request a drain afterwards whatever its outcome; when that commit did not end with `commitConfirm`, add `g` to `quiet` first, so that the drain it requests returns instead of committing again (this bounds the drain-and-commit loop to one commit per drain while the server keeps refusing); this is the normal state right after someone joined, and the `425` path below is never reached for it because the core refuses first; neither → return (another row is in flight, or the group is not active). The engine never reads the error's `detail`. Any other `CoreError` → `sendFail(msgId, code)`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, request a drain, return. Then `postMessage(g, messageBody)`; on success `sendConfirm(msgId, raw)`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, forget the row's 425 count, request a drain; a `CoreError` from `sendConfirm` → never `sendFail` or `sendRequeue` (when the answer names a seq that holds another stored row the core has already moved the row to failed with error `E_CORE_STATE` and committed that before throwing, L-CORE-09; a second transition would itself be refused), `onOutboxChanged(g)`, forget the row's 425 count, request a catch-up and then a drain (the group's other rows send on), and return.
26. `postMessage` failures, by `DillaHttpError.status` and `code`: `425` → `sendRequeue`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, increment the row's 425 count; when it reached `SYNC.commitRetryMax` → `sendFail(msgId, 'E_COMMIT_REQUIRED')`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, request a drain; else arm the membership wait: a timer of `SYNC.membershipWaitMs` that, when it fires, requests a commit (attempt 0) and then a drain (an epoch change before it fires cancels it and requests a drain, requirement 16). `403 E_LEAF_NOT_CURRENT` → `sendRequeue`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, inline resync (requirement 33; a successful resync requests the drain). `401` → `sendRequeue`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, return without requesting a drain (the account layer re-establishes or reports `revoked`). Status `0` (network) or `500` → the lost-response procedure; it never resends from here. Every other status (413, 422, 404, 403 with another code, 429 and 503 after the HTTP layer gave up, 400) → `sendFail(msgId, code)`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`, request a drain. (rule 5; `facts/interfaces.md:164, 232-246`; A1.14 `POST …/message` is not idempotent)
27. Lost-response procedure for a state-1 row: inline catch-up; then look the row up in a fresh `outbox(g)`: when it is no longer there (adopted by rule 4 of L-CORE-08 through its commitment, or by rule 2 when the upload was deleted before this device read it) or no longer in state 1 → `onOutboxChanged(g)`, request a drain, return; else arm the echo wait for `g` (`SYNC.echoWaitMs`): when it fires, a job on `g` runs a catch-up, then when the row is still in state 1 → `sendRequeue`, `onOutboxChanged(g)`; in both cases it removes the echo wait and requests a drain. A row is never posted twice without a catch-up and an expired echo wait in between. (rule 5; architect ruling 5)
28. `retry(msgId)`: `core.sendRetry(msgId)` first (its `CoreError` propagates synchronously: `E_CORE_NOT_FOUND`, `E_CORE_STATE`); find the group whose `outbox` holds the id; forget its 425 count; `onOutboxChanged(g)`; request a drain. `discard(msgId)`: find the group first, then `core.sendDiscard(msgId)` (its error propagates), then `onOutboxChanged(g)` when a group was found.

Opening a channel (rule 6) and resync (rule 7)
29. `openChannel(ch)` runs on `c:<channel hex>` (so two opens of one channel are serial) after adding `{ groupId: textGroupId, communityId, channelId, policyVersion: instance.policyVersion }` to the welcome `expected` set when `textGroupId` is not null. Loop: find the local row with `targetId == channelId`, `kind == 0`, state ≠ 4. State 2 → return `{ groupId, state: 2 }`. State 3 → resync (requirement 33, not limited by `resyncTried`) and return `{ groupId, state }` of the row afterwards (3 after a refusal; no rejection). State 0 or 1 (a page died mid-open; this open is the only one for the channel) → `groupDiscard` on the group's queue; when the row is now in state 3 continue as for state 3, else (the row was deleted, or it was a rejoin of a gone row and is back in state 4 with its history) continue as if there were no row. (rule 6; architect ruling 16, `plan-head.md:1597`)
30. No local row and `textGroupId` set: run the welcome step (requirement 12, on `w`); when it produced a state-2 row for `textGroupId` return it. Else the external join on `g:<textGroupId>`: `getGroupInfo`, `getGroupTree`, `groupJoinExternal({ groupId, communityId, channelId, policyVersion: instance.policyVersion }, info, tree)`, `postResync`; on success `groupJoined(g, seq)`, activation (requirement 34), return `{ groupId, state: 2 }`. A `DillaHttpError` from `postResync` → `groupDiscard(g)`, then: `425 E_COMMIT_REQUIRED` (the delivery service holds an external join while one of its proposals is outstanding, which is the state right after a community join) → wait `SYNC.membershipWaitMs` (an engine timer) and run the loop again from the top (so the welcome step runs first: a member's commit of the Add produces the Welcome); `409 E_COMMIT_CONFLICT` (the external commit raced another member's commit) → run the loop again from the top at once, with a fresh `getGroupInfo` and `getGroupTree`; both count against one budget of `SYNC.commitRetryMax` joins (`postResync` attempts) per `openChannel` call, and when the budget is spent the last refusal propagates (L-TS-07 rule 6 as amended; SLICE-UX-11); every other refusal propagates unchanged (403 means the account may not join; 404 means the channel's ACL does not admit it; `422 E_COMMIT_INVALID` with rule `external_joiner` or `group_info` means the delivery service refused the join's leaf or GroupInfo — hardening G for `group_info` and the credential cases — and is never retried). A failure of `getGroupInfo`/`getGroupTree` propagates (no row was left in state 1). A `CoreError` from `groupJoinExternal` writes nothing, so nothing is discarded: code `E_CORE_INPUT` (the two reads straddled a commit, which a fresh pair of reads cures; or the GroupInfo names another group, or it would rejoin at or below an epoch this device has held, which no re-read cures while the server serves the same state) → count one join against the same budget of `SYNC.commitRetryMax` and, while the budget lasts, run `getGroupInfo`, `getGroupTree` and `groupJoinExternal` again at once (no welcome step, no wait); when the budget is spent that `CoreError` propagates, so `openChannel` rejects with it and the channel keeps no row (pre-flight ruling (a); bounded so a refusal that survives every re-read ends the call); any other code (`E_CORE_STATE`: a join in progress, the row bound to another channel, another group holding the channel) propagates at once, because no re-read changes it. A row of the group in state 4 (this device was removed earlier) does not count as a local row in requirement 29's search; the external join runs over it, keeps its timeline and outbox, and a refused `postResync` returns it to state 4 through `groupDiscard`. (rule 6; protocol/02 invariant 5, `protocol/02-delivery-service.md:317-329`; A4.5 item 15)
31. No local row and `textGroupId` null: when `SYNC.registerRetryMax` registrations were already attempted in this call → reject with `SyncError('E_REGISTER_RACE')`. Else a fresh id from `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))`; on `g:<id>`: `groupCreate(id, communityId, channelId, instance.policyVersion, instance.externalSenderPub)`, `postGroup(body)`; success → `groupRegistered(id, nextSeq)`, activation, return `{ groupId: id, state: 2 }`. `409 E_GROUP_EXISTS` → `groupDiscard(id)`, `listChannels(communityId)`, take the row whose `id` equals `channelId` (none → `SyncError('E_CHANNEL_GONE')`), set `textGroupId` to its `textGroupId` and run the loop again. Any other failure → `groupDiscard(id)` and propagate, never retried — in particular `400 E_INVALID_REQUEST`, the delivery service's answer to a registration that is not exactly one leaf of this device under its registered key or whose device is not in its user's newest signed device list (hardening G). `groupCreate` always builds that one-leaf group, and the engine runs only after the account's device list v1 is published (task 18 enters ready with `publishDeviceList` before `SyncEngine.start`, and `openChannel` is accepted only in the `ready` phase), so the engine performs no list check of its own. (rule 6; A3.12 `E_GROUP_EXISTS` "do not scrape the id from detail text", `facts/interfaces.md:235`)
32. `setChannels(list)` replaces the stored list; it triggers no work.
33. Resync of `g` (rule 7), run inline on `g`'s queue: read the row (none → return false); add `g` to `resyncTried`; `onMembership(g, 'resyncing')`; when the row's `communityId` is null → refusal; else the external join of requirement 30 over `g` with the row's `communityId` and `targetId` (no 425 wait and no 409 restart for a resync: protocol/02 exempts a resync from the freeze, and a refused resync is retried by the next trigger; the `E_CORE_INPUT` re-read of requirement 30 applies, at most `SYNC.commitRetryMax` `groupJoinExternal` calls in all, after which the last `CoreError` is the refusal — a GroupInfo below the epoch floor ends here, with the row in state 3 and `not-member`, until a later trigger finds the server past the floor). Success → activation, return true. Any refusal or error → `groupDiscard(g)` when the row is in state 1 (it returns to state 3), `onGroupChanged(g, snapshot)`, `onMembership(g, 'not-member')`, return false. Background triggers (a state-3 apply result, 410, a 403 on commit or send, a `ready`) resync a group at most once per `ready` (`resyncTried`); `openChannel` always tries. (rule 7; A4.5 item 11)
34. Activation of `g` (after `groupRegistered`, `groupJoined`, or welcome outcome 0): `onGroupChanged(g, snapshot)` where `snapshot` is the `ApplyResult` built from the `groups()` row (`newSeqs: []`, `epochChanged: false`, `ownAdopted: false`); replay the held frames of `g` in ascending `seq` through requirement 15 (inline when already on `g`'s queue, else as one job on it); then request a catch-up and a drain of `g` (coalesced jobs, so they run after any frame jobs already queued). (rule 3 "held and replayed after it becomes active"; A4.5 item 18)
