- Produces:
  - **L-E2E-01** — `dilla-testkit web-driver --ds <url> --seed <n>`. One JSON object per line on stdin; one answer per line on stdout, flushed per answer, carrying the request's `id`, `"ok": true` plus the op's fields, or `"ok": false` plus `"error": <string>`. A blank line is skipped; a line that is not JSON answers `{"id": null, "ok": false, "error": "not JSON: <serde error>"}`. Every id in a request or an answer is 32 lower-case hex characters; every number is a JSON integer.

    | op | request fields | answer fields | through the public routes |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `setup` | `community` (string, 1..=255 bytes), `channel` (string, 1..=100 bytes) | `username`, `display`, `user_id`, `device_id`, `community_id`, `channel_id`, `invite_code` | `POST /v1/accounts` with the first unspent code of `DILLA_TESTKIT_INVITE` as a **native-tier user** device; `PUT /v1/users/{id}/device-list` (version 1); `POST /v1/keypackages` (32 + a last-resort one); `POST /v1/communities`; `POST /v1/communities/{id}/channels` (`kind 0, mode 0, visibility 0`); `POST /v1/communities/{id}/invites` (`max_uses 100, ttl_seconds 3600, grants_admin 0`) |
    | `register` | — | `group_id`, `epoch` (0) | `POST /v1/groups` for the channel's text group, with the instance's external sender |
    | `join` | `community_id`, `channel_id`, `group_id`, `invite_code` | `group_id`, `epoch` | `POST /v1/communities/{id}/join`, then the external join of the text group (`GET …/info`, `GET …/tree`, `POST …/resync`) (L-E2E-01 `join`) |
    | `send` | `body` (string, 1..=4000 UTF-8 bytes, the core's limit, L-CORE-09) | `seq` | `POST /v1/groups/{id}/message` with one type-0 envelope |
    | `sync` | — | `epoch`, `members` (leaf count), `received`: `[{ seq, body, sender_user, sender_device, tier }]` | drains the gateway (a reconnect catches up over `GET …/handshakes` and `GET …/messages`), applies everything in seq order, commits when the group has outstanding non-void proposals; `received` lists every message of the group decrypted since the previous `sync` answer, in order |
    | `members` | — | `devices`: `[device_id]` in leaf order | drains and applies as `sync` does (keeping what it decrypted for the next `sync`), then reads the roster of the text group |
    | `update` | — | `epoch` | drains and applies, then commits a self Update (it also carries any outstanding proposal) (L-E2E-01 `update`) |

    `username` is `peer` followed by the six lower-case hex digits of `seed & 0xffffff` (`peer005eed` for seed `0x5eed`); `display` equals `username` (the runner registers `new_account(name, name)`, `run.rs:732`; L-E2E-01 `setup` answer). `tier` is 0 (native) or 1 (browser), read from the sender's MLS credential (L-CORE-01). `invite_code` is the community invite's plain code. The driver needs `DILLA_TESTKIT_INVITE`; `DILLA_TESTKIT_CONTROL` is passed through and used by no op.

**Requirements:**

1. `dilla-testkit web-driver --ds <url> [--seed <n>]` (default seed `0x5eed`) serves the protocol above on stdin/stdout until stdin ends, then exits 0; an I/O error writes `web-driver: <error>` to stderr and exits 1 — the same shape as `media-driver` (`testkit/src/bin/dilla-testkit.rs:55-66`, `media_driver.rs:41-58`). (L-E2E-01)
2. Request validation runs before any network call and before the setup check, in this order, with these exact error strings (each prefixed `scenario: ` by `TestkitError::Scenario`, `testkit/src/lib.rs:43-44`): a missing string field `k` → `the request carries no k`; `community` outside 1..=255 bytes → `community must be 1..=255 bytes`; `channel` outside 1..=100 bytes → `channel must be 1..=100 bytes` (`internal/api/communities.go:81-84`, interfaces A3 row "POST /v1/communities/{id}/channels"); an id field `k` that is not 32 lower-case hex → `k is not 32 lowercase hex`; `body` whose UTF-8 length (`body.len()`, bytes, not characters) is 0 or more than 4000 → `body must be 1..=4000 bytes` (the core's `MAX_BODY_LONG`, `core/dilla-core/src/envelope/mod.rs:15-16, 362`; L-CORE-09: the limit is bytes); an unknown op → `unknown op <op>`. Then every op but `setup` before a successful `setup` → `setup first`; a second `setup` → `setup runs once per driver`; `send`, `sync`, `members`, `update` before `register` or `join` → `no group yet: register or join first`; `register` or `join` when a group is already held → `the driver already holds a group`. (L-E2E-01)
3. `setup` enrols through `Runner` exactly as a remote scenario client does (`run.rs:697-783`: bootstrap invite, user id minted by the instance, client rebuilt around it, device list v1 signed and put), as client `WebDriver::username(seed)` with `tier=native`, then publishes 32 KeyPackages plus a last-resort one (`publish_key_packages <name> 32`; the instance refuses more than `max_keypackages_per_device = 32` non-last-resort packages, `internal/ds/keypackage.go:103`), then calls `create_community(community)`, `create_text_channel(community_id, channel)` (an answer whose mode or visibility is not 0 is the error `the instance answered mode <m> visibility <v> for a text channel`), and `create_invite(community_id, 100, 3600)`. (L-E2E-01; C18)
4. `register` runs the statement `group text kind=text target=<channel hex> community=<community hex> creator=<username>` through `Runner::exec_line` (the media driver's pattern, `media_driver.rs:120-129`), which builds the binding `{v 1, instance_id of the instance, community, target = channel, kind text, policy_version 1, e2ee 1, media Text}` with `external_senders(<instance key>, <instance id>)` (`run.rs:257-294`) and registers it; the answer's `group_id` is `Runner::group_id("text")` and `epoch` the creator's epoch (0). Under `ProductionACL` the instance admits it because the peer owns the community (`internal/api/dschannels.go:74-118`). (L-E2E-01)
5. `join` calls `join_community(community_id, invite_code)`, then, inside `Runner::with_member`, `TestClient::join_external(ds, group_id, &binding)` with the binding of requirement 4 built from `instance_document(ds_url)` (`instance_id`) and the request's ids (policy_version 1; `DillaBinding::matches` does not compare it, plan head L-CORE-07); the answer's `epoch` is the joiner's epoch after the join. (L-E2E-01 extension; protocol/01 "Joining": a community member enters a channel group by external commit, `internal/api/private.go:213-219`)
6. `send` calls `TestClient::send_seq` inside `with_member` and answers its `seq`. The envelope is type 0 (`client.rs:579-589`). (L-E2E-01)
7. `sync`: inside `with_member`, `TestClient::sync(ds)`; then, when `ds.proposals(group)` lists at least one item with `void == false`, `TestClient::commit(ds, group)`; a commit refused with `E_COMMIT_CONFLICT` runs `sync` again and retries, at most 3 commit attempts in total, after which the refusal is the answer's error; any other error is the answer's error. The answer's `received` is the driver's pending list (messages `members` or `update` decrypted earlier) followed by what this call's syncs returned, filtered to the held group, each as `{"seq", "body": envelope.body, "sender_user": sender_user hex, "sender_device": sender hex, "tier": tier as u8}`; the pending list is then emptied. `epoch` is `epoch_of(group)`, `members` is `member_count(group)`. A `TestClient::sync` error (task 1's sender check among them) is the answer's error string unchanged (`TestkitError`'s `Display`: `assertion: message seq …`). (L-E2E-01; L-CORE-01)
8. `members`: `TestClient::sync(ds)` inside `with_member`, its result appended to the pending list, then `roster(group)` → `devices` (device ids, leaf order). (L-E2E-01)
9. `update`: `TestClient::sync(ds)` (result appended to the pending list), then `TestClient::commit(ds, group)` once; answers `epoch_of(group)`. (task 25 proposal)
10. `HttpDs::{create_community, create_text_channel, create_invite, join_community}` speak exactly the bodies of their doc comments, deterministic CBOR via `encode` (`remote.rs:111-115`), through `post_decoded` (`remote.rs:1174-1182`) with the session's bearer; a non-2xx answer is the `DsError` `check_status` makes (`remote.rs:290-341`). The community `policy` element is the 2-byte byte string `{}` (`communities.go:110-116, 149-151`). (A3 rows, `interfaces.md:104, 111, 117, 131`)
11. `TestClient::send_seq` frames exactly as `send` does (`seal`, `client.rs:570-594`) and posts through `post_message_from`, returning `UploadResult.seq` (`testkit/src/ds/mod.rs:180-184`). `TestClient::roster` returns `self.groups.get(group_id).map(DillaGroup::roster)`.

The Go harness test runs two drivers against `testkit.Start(…, ProductionACL: true)`; one of them reaches the instance through an in-test reverse proxy that, once armed, replaces the bearer of exactly one `POST /v1/groups/{id}/message` with a session token of the **other** device, so the delivery service records that device as the uploader of a ciphertext it did not make; the other driver's `sync` must answer `ok: false` with task 1's error naming both devices. (lesson a; C22; task index mutation)

'go'} -C <REPO_ROOT> build -o <REPO_ROOT>/target/dilla-testhost ./cmd/dilla-testhost`; refuses to start when `WASI_CORE` is missing (`<path> is missing: cargo build -p dilla-core-wasi --target wasm32-wasip1 --release --locked, then copy it there`) or when `webRoot` is set and `<REPO_ROOT>/<webRoot>/index.html` is missing (`<abs webRoot> has no index.html: build it first (npm run build:harness -w @dilla/client-core, or npm run build -w @dilla/web)`); removes `/tmp/dw/host-<port>` and creates `/tmp/dw`; spawns the host with `hostArgs`; writes stdout (invite codes replaced by `[redacted]`) and stderr to `<REPO_ROOT>/e2e/test-results/testhost-<port>.log`; waits for the banner line `DILLA_TESTKIT_INVITE=` and then for `GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` to answer 200, each within 90 000 ms when `process.env.CI === 'true'` else 60 000 ms; sets the three environment variables; returns a teardown that sends SIGTERM, SIGKILLs after 10 000 ms, and removes `/tmp/dw/host-<port>`. Whether `-web-root` is passed is a setting of the config, not a run-time existence check, so a missing harness build fails loudly (requirement 13) instead of silently serving the placeholder (L-E2E-03).
16. `persistent.ts`: for every test, `profileDir` = `profileDirFor(testInfo.project.name, testInfo.workerIndex)`, removed and recreated empty before the test and removed after it; `context` = `playwright[browserName].launchPersistentContext(profileDir, { ...launchOptions, headless, channel, viewport, baseURL })` (the project's own options; no `firefoxUserPrefs` beyond what the project sets, so Firefox runs a normal, persistent profile — G4); `page` = `context.pages()[0] ?? await context.newPage()`; `relaunch()` closes the current context, launches a persistent context on the same `profileDir` with the same options, and returns `{ context, page }` (its first page); the fixture's teardown closes whichever context is current at the end and does nothing else. The fixture never calls `context.tracing`: with `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` the runner itself starts tracing on a context made by `launchPersistentContext` (`node_modules/playwright/lib/index.js:134-145, 648-651` in 1.63.0) and keeps the trace on failure; a second `tracing.start` throws `Tracing has been already started`. (L-E2E-03, L-E2E-04)
17. `axe.ts`: `injectAxe` reads `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('axe-core/axe.min.js')` once per process and evaluates it with `page.evaluate(source)` unless `window.axe` is already defined; it answers nothing (L-E2E-04: `Promise<void>`); `runAxe` runs `axe.run(document, { resultTypes: ['violations'], rules: { 'target-size': { enabled: true } } })` and maps every violation whose impact is `serious` or `critical` to `{ id, impact, help, targets: nodes.map(n => n.target.join(' ')) }`. `e2e/package.json` declares `"axe-core": "4.13.0"` (the installed version, pin table) so the resolution does not lean on hoisting. (Global Constraints "Accessibility rules"; pin table, row `axe-core`)

The typed methods strip `id` and `ok` from the answer.

```rust
        ];

            (json!({"id": 3, "op": "setup", "community": "", "channel": "general"}),

            (json!({"id": 4, "op": "setup", "community": "c".repeat(256), "channel": "general"}),
             "scenario: community must be 1..=255 bytes"),
            (json!({"id": 5, "op": "setup", "community": "c", "channel": ""}),
             "scenario: channel must be 1..=100 bytes"),
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the failing Go harness test**

Create `internal/testkit/webdriver_test.go`:

```go
package testkit_test

// dilla-web-1 task 17: `dilla-testkit web-driver`, the native peer of the browser tests, against an
// in-process instance wired as production wires it. Two driver processes enrol through the
// bootstrap invite, build a community through the public routes, meet in its channel's text group
// and exchange messages. Then one upload is relabelled in flight, so the delivery service records
// the other device as the uploader of a ciphertext it did not make, and the receiving driver must
// refuse it: the sender a browser test reads from `sync` is the MLS-authenticated one, never the
// delivery service's label (C22).

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/http/httputil"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/jonasthim/dilla/internal/api"
	"github.com/jonasthim/dilla/internal/id"
	"github.com/jonasthim/dilla/internal/testkit"
)

var hex32 = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{32}$`)

// driverWait bounds one answer and one polling loop. Generous on purpose: CI runs this package
// under the race detector on a 4-vCPU runner (lesson c); nothing here asserts a duration.
const driverWait = 90 * time.Second

// lockedBuffer collects a driver's stderr; exec's copier writes it while a failing test reads it.
type lockedBuffer struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	b  bytes.Buffer
}

func (l *lockedBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return l.b.Write(p)
}

func (l *lockedBuffer) String() string {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return l.b.String()
}

// webDriver is one `dilla-testkit web-driver` process: one JSON request per stdin line, one answer
// per stdout line, in order.
type webDriver struct {
	t      *testing.T
	name   string
	stdin  io.WriteCloser
	lines  chan string
	stderr *lockedBuffer
	next   int
}

func startWebDriver(t *testing.T, h *testkit.Harness, base, name string, seed uint64) *webDriver {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := exec.Command(os.Getenv("DILLA_TESTKIT"), "web-driver", "--ds", base, "--seed", fmt.Sprint(seed)) //nolint:gosec // G204: DILLA_TESTKIT is the test-harness input testkit.Start already checked
	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
		"DILLA_TESTKIT_INVITE="+h.Invite(),
		"DILLA_TESTKIT_CONTROL="+h.ControlURL(),
	)
	stderr := &lockedBuffer{}
	cmd.Stderr = stderr
	stdin, err := cmd.StdinPipe()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	stdout, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("start %s: %v", name, err)
	}
	lines := make(chan string, 16)
	go func() {
		sc := bufio.NewScanner(stdout)
		sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), 8<<20)
		for sc.Scan() {
			lines <- sc.Text()
		}
		close(lines)
	}()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = stdin.Close()
		done := make(chan error, 1)
		go func() { done <- cmd.Wait() }()
		select {
		case <-done:
		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
			_ = cmd.Process.Kill()
			<-done
		}
		if t.Failed() {
			t.Logf("%s stderr:\n%s", name, stderr.String())
		}
	})
	return &webDriver{t: t, name: name, stdin: stdin, lines: lines, stderr: stderr}
}

// call sends one request and returns its answer, whatever "ok" says.
func (d *webDriver) call(op string, fields map[string]any) map[string]any {
	d.t.Helper()
	d.next++
	req := map[string]any{"id": d.next, "op": op}
	for k, v := range fields {
		req[k] = v
	}
	line, err := json.Marshal(req)
	if err != nil {
		d.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := d.stdin.Write(append(line, '\n')); err != nil {
		d.t.Fatalf("%s %s: write: %v", d.name, op, err)
	}
	select {
	case got, open := <-d.lines:
		if !open {
			d.t.Fatalf("%s exited before answering %s:\n%s", d.name, op, d.stderr.String())
		}
		var answer map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(got), &answer); err != nil {
			d.t.Fatalf("%s %s: not JSON: %q", d.name, op, got)
		}
		if answer["id"] != float64(d.next) {
			d.t.Fatalf("%s %s: the answer %v carries another id", d.name, op, answer)
		}
		return answer
	case <-time.After(driverWait):
		d.t.Fatalf("%s did not answer %s within %v:\n%s", d.name, op, driverWait, d.stderr.String())
	}
	return nil
}

// ok is call for an op that must succeed.
func (d *webDriver) ok(op string, fields map[string]any) map[string]any {
	d.t.Helper()
	a := d.call(op, fields)
	if a["ok"] != true {
		d.t.Fatalf("%s %s refused: %v", d.name, op, a["error"])
	}
	return a
}

// waitFor syncs until a message with body arrives and returns it.
func (d *webDriver) waitFor(body string) map[string]any {
	d.t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(driverWait)
	for {
		for _, item := range d.ok("sync", nil)["received"].([]any) {
			if m := item.(map[string]any); m["body"] == body {
				return m
			}
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			d.t.Fatalf("%s never received %q within %v", d.name, body, driverWait)
		}
		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// relabelProxy relays every request to the instance unchanged, except that once armed it sends
// the next POST /v1/groups/{id}/message with another device's bearer. httputil.ReverseProxy also
// relays the gateway's WebSocket upgrade, so a driver can live entirely behind it.
type relabelProxy struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	token string
	srv   *httptest.Server
}

func newRelabelProxy(t *testing.T, target string) *relabelProxy {
	t.Helper()
	u, err := url.Parse(target)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	relay := httputil.NewSingleHostReverseProxy(u)
	p := &relabelProxy{}
	p.srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.Method == http.MethodPost && strings.HasPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/v1/groups/") &&
			strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "/message") {
			p.mu.Lock()
			token := p.token
			p.token = ""
			p.mu.Unlock()
			if token != "" {
				r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
			}
		}
		relay.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	}))
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		p.srv.CloseClientConnections()
		p.srv.Close()
	})
	return p
}

func (p *relabelProxy) arm(token string) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	p.token = token
}

func (p *relabelProxy) armed() bool {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	return p.token != ""
}

func mustID(t *testing.T, v any) id.ID {
	t.Helper()
	s, _ := v.(string)
	if !hex32.MatchString(s) {
		t.Fatalf("%v is not 32 lowercase hex", v)
	}
	parsed, err := id.Parse(s)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return parsed
}

func TestTheWebDriverPeersExchangeMessagesUnderTheProductionACL(t *testing.T) {
	h := testkit.Start(t, testkit.Options{DataDir: t.TempDir(), ProductionACL: true})
	t.Cleanup(h.Stop)
	ctx := context.Background()
	repo := h.Repo()

	proxy := newRelabelProxy(t, h.BaseURL())
	alice := startWebDriver(t, h, proxy.srv.URL, "alice", 0xa11ce)
	bob := startWebDriver(t, h, h.BaseURL(), "bob", 0xb0b)

	// setup: an account, a device list, KeyPackages, a community, a channel and an invite, all
	// through the public routes, read back from the instance's own store.
	sa := alice.ok("setup", map[string]any{"community": "web driver", "channel": "general"})
	if sa["username"] != "peer0a11ce" || sa["display"] != "peer0a11ce" {
		t.Fatalf("setup answered username %v display %v, want peer0a11ce twice", sa["username"], sa["display"])
	}
	aliceUser, aliceDev := mustID(t, sa["user_id"]), mustID(t, sa["device_id"])
	community, channel := mustID(t, sa["community_id"]), mustID(t, sa["channel_id"])
	if code, _ := sa["invite_code"].(string); code == "" {
		t.Fatalf("setup answered no invite_code: %v", sa)
	}
	c, err := repo.GetCommunity(ctx, community)
	if err != nil || c.Owner != aliceUser || c.Name != "web driver" {
		t.Fatalf("community row = %+v, %v; want owner %s named \"web driver\"", c, err, aliceUser)
	}
	ch, err := repo.GetChannel(ctx, channel)
	if err != nil || ch.CommunityID == nil || *ch.CommunityID != community || ch.Kind != api.ChannelText ||
		ch.Mode != 0 || ch.Visibility != 0 || ch.Name != "general" {
		t.Fatalf("channel row = %+v, %v; want an e2ee private text channel \"general\" of %s", ch, err, community)
	}
	dev, err := repo.GetDevice(ctx, aliceDev)
	if err != nil || dev.UserID != aliceUser || dev.Tier != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("device row = %+v, %v; want a native-tier device of %s", dev, err, aliceUser)
	}
	if n, err := repo.CountKeyPackages(ctx, aliceDev, time.Now().Unix()); err != nil || n != 32 {
		t.Fatalf("KeyPackages of alice's device = %d, %v; want 32", n, err)
	}

	// register: the channel's text group, under the production registration ACL.
	ra := alice.ok("register", nil)
	group := mustID(t, ra["group_id"])
	if ra["epoch"] != float64(0) {
		t.Fatalf("register answered epoch %v, want 0", ra["epoch"])
	}
	groups, err := repo.GroupsForTarget(ctx, channel, api.GroupText)
	if err != nil || len(groups) != 1 || groups[0].GroupID != group {
		t.Fatalf("open text groups of the channel = %v, %v; want exactly %s", groups, err, group)
	}

	// join: a second peer enters the community with its invite and the group by external commit.
	sb := bob.ok("setup", map[string]any{"community": "bob's own", "channel": "elsewhere"})
	bobUser, bobDev := mustID(t, sb["user_id"]), mustID(t, sb["device_id"])
	jb := bob.ok("join", map[string]any{
		"community_id": sa["community_id"], "channel_id": sa["channel_id"],
		"group_id": ra["group_id"], "invite_code": sa["invite_code"],
	})
	if jb["group_id"] != ra["group_id"] || jb["epoch"] != float64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("join answered %v, want group %v at epoch 1", jb, ra["group_id"])
	}
	if _, err := repo.GetMember(ctx, community, bobUser); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("bob is not a member of alice's community after join: %v", err)
	}

	// members: alice applies bob's external commit and sees both devices.
	deadline := time.Now().Add(driverWait)
	for {
		devices := alice.ok("members", nil)["devices"].([]any)
		if len(devices) == 2 && slices.Contains(devices, any(sa["device_id"])) && slices.Contains(devices, any(sb["device_id"])) {
			break
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("alice's roster never held both devices: %v", devices)
		}
		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	if s := alice.ok("sync", nil); s["epoch"] != float64(1) || s["members"] != float64(2) {
		t.Fatalf("alice's sync after the join = %v, want epoch 1 with 2 members", s)
	}

	// send and sync, both ways: the sender is the MLS credential's, with its user and tier.
	sent := alice.ok("send", map[string]any{"body": "hello from alice"})
	if seq, _ := sent["seq"].(float64); seq < 1 {
		t.Fatalf("send answered seq %v", sent["seq"])
	}
	got := bob.waitFor("hello from alice")
	if got["seq"] != sent["seq"] || got["sender_user"] != sa["user_id"] || got["sender_device"] != sa["device_id"] || got["tier"] != float64(0) {
		t.Fatalf("bob received %v; want seq %v from alice's user and device at tier 0", got, sent["seq"])
	}
	bob.ok("send", map[string]any{"body": "hello from bob"})
	back := alice.waitFor("hello from bob")
	if back["sender_user"] != sb["user_id"] || back["sender_device"] != sb["device_id"] || back["tier"] != float64(0) {
		t.Fatalf("alice received %v; want bob's user and device at tier 0", back)
	}

	// The relabelled upload: alice's ciphertext reaches the delivery service under bob's session.
	bobRow, err := repo.GetDevice(ctx, bobDev)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	token, err := h.Server().Sessions().NewDeviceSession(ctx, repo, bobRow.UserID, bobRow.ID, bobRow.Tier)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a session for bob's device: %v", err)
	}
	proxy.arm(token.Token)
	relabelled := alice.ok("send", map[string]any{"body": "relabelled in flight"})
	if proxy.armed() {
		t.Fatal("the proxy never saw alice's upload, so nothing was relabelled")
	}
	want := fmt.Sprintf("the MLS sender %s is not the uploader %s", aliceDev, bobDev)
	deadline = time.Now().Add(driverWait)
	for {
		a := bob.call("sync", nil)
		if a["ok"] == false {
			if msg := fmt.Sprint(a["error"]); !strings.Contains(msg, want) {
				t.Fatalf("bob's sync failed for another reason: %s (want it to contain %q)", msg, want)
			}
			break
		}
		if items := a["received"].([]any); len(items) > 0 {
			t.Fatalf("bob accepted a message whose MLS sender (alice) is not its uploader of record (bob): %v", items)
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("bob never saw the relabelled upload (seq %v) within %v", relabelled["seq"], driverWait)
		}
		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}
```

- `new(ds, seed)`: `Runner::new(seed).with_ds(Some(ds.clone()))`, the rest empty.

- `serve` and `handle`: identical in behaviour to `MediaDriver::serve`/`handle` (`media_driver.rs:41-72`): the answer object gets `id` and `"ok": true`; a non-object `Ok` value is wrapped as `{"value": …}` (no op here returns one); an `Err(e)` is `{"id", "ok": false, "error": e.to_string()}`.
- `dispatch(op, req)`: first `validate(op, req)` (requirement 2's checks, in its order; `unknown op` is raised here, so an unknown op never reaches the setup check), then for every op but `setup` require `self.peer` (`setup first`), then for `send`/`sync`/`members`/`update` require `self.group` (`no group yet: register or join first`) and for `register`/`join` require it to be `None` (`the driver already holds a group`); then the op.
- Helpers: `text(req, key) -> Result<&str, TestkitError>` (`the request carries no <key>`); `hex16(req, key) -> Result<[u8; 16], TestkitError>` accepting exactly 32 characters of `[0-9a-f]` (`<key> is not 32 lowercase hex`; `hex::decode` alone accepts upper case, so check the characters first); `body` length counted with `body.len()` (UTF-8 bytes; refused when `0` or `> BODY_MAX_BYTES`).

Stores `Peer` and answers the seven fields.
- `register`: `exec_line(&format!("group {GROUP} kind=text target={} community={} creator={}", hex(channel), hex(community), name))` where community and channel are kept from setup (add `community: [u8; 16]` and `channel: [u8; 16]` to `Peer`); `group = runner.group_id(GROUP)?`; answers `group_id` hex and `epoch` from `runner.epoch_of(&name, GROUP)?`.

- `send`: `with_member(&name, |c, ds| c.send_seq(ds, &group, body))` → `{"seq": seq}`.
- `sync`: requirement 7. Inside one `with_member` closure: `let mut got = c.sync(ds)?;` then `for attempt in 1..=3` — `let outstanding = ds.proposals(&group)?.iter().filter(|p| !p.void).count(); if outstanding == 0 { break; }` `match c.commit(ds, &group) { Ok(()) => break, Err(TestkitError::Ds(DsError::CommitConflict { .. })) if attempt < 3 => { got.extend(c.sync(ds)?); } Err(e) => return Err(e) }` (`DsError::CommitConflict`, `testkit/src/ds/state.rs:71-75`; import `crate::DsError`); after the loop `got.extend(c.sync(ds)?)` once more (the commit's own echo and anything that arrived meanwhile); return `(got, c.epoch_of(&group), c.member_count(&group))`. - `received_json(r: &Received) -> Value`: `json!({"seq": r.seq, "body": r.envelope.body, "sender_user": r.sender_user.to_hex(), "sender_device": r.sender.to_hex(), "tier": r.tier as u8})`.
- `members`: `with_member` closure `let got = c.sync(ds)?; Ok((got, c.roster(&group)))`; extend `pending` with `got`; roster `None` → `scenario("the peer holds no state for its group")`; answer `devices` = `entry.device_id.to_hex()` in order.
- `update`: `with_member` closure `let got = c.sync(ds)?; c.commit(ds, &group)?; Ok((got, c.epoch_of(&group)))`; extend `pending`; answer `epoch`.

```ts
import { test as base, expect, type BrowserContext, type BrowserType, type Page, type TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';import { mkdirSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';

export const PROFILE_ROOT = '/tmp/dw';
export function profileDirFor(project: string, workerIndex: number): string {
  return `${PROFILE_ROOT}/${project}-${workerIndex}`;
}

type Holder = { context: BrowserContext | null; open: () => Promise<BrowserContext> };
type Fixtures = {
  profileDir: string;
  relaunch: () => Promise<{ context: BrowserContext; page: Page }>;
  holder: Holder;
};

export const test = base.extend<Fixtures>({
  profileDir: async ({}, use, testInfo: TestInfo) => {
    const dir = profileDirFor(testInfo.project.name, testInfo.workerIndex);
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    await use(dir);
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  },
  // No context.tracing call anywhere in this file: with trace: 'retain-on-failure' the runner starts
  // tracing on every context launchPersistentContext makes and keeps the trace when the test fails
  // (playwright 1.63.0, lib/index.js:134-145, 648-651); a second tracing.start throws
  // "Tracing has been already started".
  holder: async ({ playwright, browserName, launchOptions, headless, channel, viewport, baseURL, profileDir }, use) => {
    const holder: Holder = {
      context: null,
      open: async () => {
        const type: BrowserType = playwright[browserName];
        const context = await type.launchPersistentContext(profileDir, { ...launchOptions, headless, channel, viewport, baseURL });
        holder.context = context;
        return context;
      },
    };
    await holder.open();
    await use(holder);
    await holder.context?.close();
  },
  context: async ({ holder }, use) => {
    await use(holder.context as BrowserContext);
  },
  page: async ({ context }, use) => {
    await use(context.pages()[0] ?? (await context.newPage()));
  },
  relaunch: async ({ holder }, use) => {
    await use(async () => {
      const previous = holder.context;
      holder.context = null;
      await previous?.close();
      const context = await holder.open();
      return { context, page: context.pages()[0] ?? (await context.newPage()) };
    });
  },
});
export { expect };
```

The `holder` fixture is internal (not in the produced surface); `context` and `page` are the first launch's, `relaunch` hands back the new ones. A failing test's trace is the runner's (`e2e/test-results/<test>/trace.zip`), recorded for every context the holder launched.

`e2e/web/support/axe.ts` (requirement 17):

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';

export interface AxeFinding { id: string; impact: 'serious' | 'critical'; help: string; targets: string[] }

let source: string | null = null;
function axeSource(): string {
  source ??= readFileSync(createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('axe-core/axe.min.js'), 'utf8');
  return source;
}

type AxeWindow = Window & { axe?: { version: string; run(context: unknown, options: unknown): Promise<{ violations: { id: string; impact: string | null; help: string; nodes: { target: string[] }[] }[] }> } };

/** Not page.addScriptTag: an inline <script> is refused by the served CSP (L-HTTP-10) and reported as a
 *  securitypolicyviolation. A protocol-level evaluate is not subject to the page's CSP. */
export async function injectAxe(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  if (!(await page.evaluate(() => typeof (window as AxeWindow).axe !== 'undefined'))) {
    await page.evaluate(axeSource());
  }
}

export async function runAxe(page: Page): Promise<AxeFinding[]> {
  await injectAxe(page);
  return page.evaluate(async () => {
    const result = await (window as AxeWindow).axe!.run(document, {
      resultTypes: ['violations'],
      rules: { 'target-size': { enabled: true } },
    });
    return result.violations
      .filter((v) => v.impact === 'serious' || v.impact === 'critical')
      .map((v) => ({ id: v.id, impact: v.impact as 'serious' | 'critical', help: v.help, targets: v.nodes.map((n) => n.target.join(' ')) }));
  });
}
```

```ts
import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { expect, test } from './support/persistent';
import { WebDriver, testHostUrl, testkitEnv } from './support/driver';
import { injectAxe, runAxe } from './support/axe';

const HEX32 = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/;
const WAIT = process.env.CI === 'true' ? 90_000 : 30_000;
// L-HTTP-10, exactly, with HOST = 127.0.0.1:8453.
const CSP =
  "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; " +
  "connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:8453 wss://127.0.0.1:8453; worker-src 'self'; media-src 'none'; " +
  "object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'";
// The invite landing's own policy (internal/api/invites.go:107), set on every answer of GET /i/{code}.
const LANDING_CSP = "default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'";

test('the test host serves the client root same-origin, with its headers, to a persistent profile', async ({ page, profileDir }) => {
  expect(profileDir).toMatch(/^\/tmp\/dw\/(chromium|firefox)-core-\d+$/);
  const response = await page.goto('/');
  // A persistent context: the browser wrote its profile into the directory the fixture created empty.
  expect(readdirSync(profileDir).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(response?.status()).toBe(200);
  const headers = response!.headers();
  expect(headers['content-security-policy']).toBe(CSP);
  expect(headers['content-type']).toBe('text/html; charset=utf-8');
  expect(headers['cache-control']).toBe('no-cache');
  expect(headers['x-content-type-options']).toBe('nosniff');
  expect(headers['referrer-policy']).toBe('no-referrer');
  expect(headers['x-frame-options']).toBe('DENY');
  expect(headers['permissions-policy']).toBe('camera=(), microphone=(), display-capture=(), geolocation=()');
  expect(headers['cross-origin-opener-policy']).toBeUndefined();
  expect(headers['cross-origin-embedder-policy']).toBeUndefined();
  expect(headers['access-control-allow-origin']).toBeUndefined();
  await expect(page.locator('meta[name="dilla-web"]')).toHaveAttribute('content', 'placeholder', { timeout: WAIT });
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveText('dilla: this build does not include the web client.');
});

test('axe evaluates under the served CSP without a policy violation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const w = window as Window & { cspViolations?: string[] };
    w.cspViolations = [];
    document.addEventListener('securitypolicyviolation', (e) => w.cspViolations!.push(e.violatedDirective));
  });
  await injectAxe(page);
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as Window & { axe?: { version: string } }).axe?.version)).toBe('4.13.0');
  const findings = await runAxe(page);
  for (const f of findings) expect(['serious', 'critical']).toContain(f.impact);
  await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0)));
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as Window & { cspViolations?: string[] }).cspViolations)).toEqual([]);
});

test('the native peer enrols and builds its community through the public routes', async ({ request }) => {
  const peer = await WebDriver.start(testHostUrl(), testkitEnv());
  try {
    const s = await peer.setup({ community: 'support community', channel: 'general' });
    expect(s.username).toBe(`peer${(peer.seed & 0xff_ffff).toString(16).padStart(6, '0')}`);
    expect(s.display).toBe(s.username);
```

*State (L-TS-08)*
1. `SliceStore.set` deep-clones the value with `structuredClone`, deep-freezes the clone (every nested object and array), and publishes `(name, rev, clone)` with `rev` one higher than the last for that name; when `JSON.stringify` of the new value equals that of the held value it does nothing (no publish, no `rev` change). `get` returns the held clone, the same object until the next accepted `set`. Every slice value is replaced whole. (L-TS-08 "every slice value is immutable and replaced whole")
2. `buildTimeline`: stored rows first, in the order the core returned them (ascending `seq`), then the outbox rows in the order the core returned them (`created`, `msgId`). A stored row is left out when its `type` is neither `0` nor `null` (envelope types 1–6 are kept in the database and not shown, L-TS-08; ruling 17). A stored row maps to `key 'o' + hex(msgId)` when its `senderDevice` equals `ownDevice` and its `msgId` is not null (so a sent message keeps the key its outbox row had when it is confirmed, and the page does not announce it twice), else to `key 's' + seq`; `state` `ok`/`cannot-read`/`deleted` for status 0/1/2, `reason` = the row's reason when status is 1 else `''`, `senderUser` hex or `null`, `senderDevice` hex, `own` = `senderDevice` equals `ownDevice`, `web` = `senderTier === 1`, `bot` = `senderKind === 1`, `ts` = `Number(recvTs)`, `body` = the row's body **only when status is 0, else `''`**, `msgId` hex or `null`. A status-2 row can carry this device's `senderDevice` and a `msgId` (the core stores the deleted upload of an own outbox row as such a marker and drops the outbox row, L-CORE-08 rule 2 as amended after the core hardening): it maps by the same rules, to key `'o' + hex(msgId)`, state `deleted`, body `''`, so the message keeps its key from pending to deleted. An outbox row whose `msgId` equals the `msgId` of a stored row is left out; the others map to `key 'o' + hex(msgId)`, `state` `pending` for outbox states 0 and 1 and `failed` for 2, `reason` = `error` when failed else `''`, `senderUser` = hex(ownUser), `senderDevice` = hex(ownDevice), `own: true`, `web: true` (this device is browser tier), `bot: false`, `ts` = `Number(created)`, `body`, `msgId` hex. `hasEarlier` = `rows.length >= limit` (the unfiltered count the core returned). (L-TS-08; L-CORE-09 `timeline`/`outbox`; the deferred-list row "a `cannot-read` row with one fixed string and the raw reason code")
3. `channelGroupState(channel, groups, { refusedChannel, notMember, resyncing })`: `unsupported` when `kind !== 0` or `mode !== 0`; else the group is the first of `groups` with `kind === 0`, `targetId` equal to the channel id and `state !== 4`, else the first with `kind === 0`, that target and `state === 4`; with `g` = the hex of that group's `groupId`: none → `refusedChannel ? 'not-member' : 'none'`; state 0 or 1 → `joining`; 2 → `resyncing.has(g) ? 'resync' : 'active'` (a resync can start from a group still in state 2, after `E_LEAF_NOT_CURRENT` or `E_PRUNED`); 3 → `notMember.has(g) || refusedChannel ? 'not-member' : 'resync'`; 4 → `not-member`. (L-TS-08 "A channel of mode 1 or kind other than 0 has group 'unsupported'" and "`resync` while a resync runs, `not-member` after a refused one or a 403 on open"; L-TS-07 rule 7)

*Bridge (L-TS-10)*
4. `connectCore` listens with `worker.addEventListener('message', …)`; `call` posts `{ t: 'call', id, command }` with ids 1, 2, 3, … and resolves or rejects when the `ret` with that id arrives (`ok: false` rejects with `new CoreCallError(error)`, carrying the `WorkerError`'s `code`, `detail`, `status` and `retryAfterMs`); a `ret` for an unknown id is ignored; a `slice` is accepted only when its `rev` is greater than the held one for that name (none held counts as 0), then every listener of that name is called once; `subscribe` returns a function that removes exactly that listener; `dispose` calls `worker.terminate()` and rejects every pending call with `new CoreCallError({ code: 'E_DISPOSED', detail: '', status: 0, retryAfterMs: null })`, after which `call` rejects the same way without posting. A message that is neither a `ret` nor a `slice` is ignored. (L-TS-10)

*Worker protocol and leadership (L-TS-09, C5)*
5. `Controller.handle(data)`: a `TestHook` is run only when `deps.testHooks` is true (`gateway-stop` → `gateway.stop()`; `gateway-start` → `gateway.start()`; both ignored before the gateway exists), else ignored; anything that is not `isToWorker` is ignored without an answer; a call is answered with exactly one `ret`. Validation runs first and synchronously, in this order: an unknown `command.m` → `E_BAD_INPUT` (detail `unknown command <m>`); every id field (`communityId`, `channelId`, `msgId`) must match `^[0-9a-f]{32}$` → else `E_BAD_INPUT` (detail `<field> is not 32 lowercase hex`); `invite` must be non-empty after `trim()` → else `E_BAD_INPUT` (`invite is empty`); `send`'s `text` must be non-empty after `trim()` → else `E_BAD_INPUT` (`the message is empty`) (the core enforces the 4000-byte limit, `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`, L-CORE-09). Then the phase check of requirement 9; then the command. (L-TS-09 error codes)
6. Errors are answered as a `WorkerError` (L-TS-08, ruling 33), by the one private function `errorOf(e: unknown): WorkerError`, checked in this order: a `DillaHttpError` → its `code`, `detail`, `status` and `retryAfterMs`; a `CoreError`, a `CborError` or a `SyncError` → its own `code` and `detail` (a `CborError`'s detail is its `message`), `status: 0`, `retryAfterMs: null`; an `Error` whose `message` is exactly `E_KEK_EXISTS`, `E_KEK_UNWRAP` or `E_SESSION_SCOPE` → that code, detail `''`, `status: 0`, `retryAfterMs: null`; the controller's own refusals (`E_BAD_INPUT`, `E_NOT_READY`, `E_INVITE_NOT_COMMUNITY`, `E_UNSUPPORTED`) with the codes and details of this task, `status: 0`, `retryAfterMs: null`; anything else → `E_INTERNAL` with the error's `message` (`String(e)` for a non-`Error`), `status: 0`, `retryAfterMs: null` (never a value that could hold a key, a token or a message body: the controller never interpolates one into an error). (L-TS-09 error codes)
7. `start` is idempotent: the first call publishes `account` `{ phase: 'loading', instance: null, user: null, deviceId: null, recoveryKey: null, error: null }` and `connection` `{ status: 'offline', generation: null }`, reads `routes.getInstance()` and `routes.getLimits()`, publishes `account.instance` = `{ id: toHex(instanceId), name, registrationMode, passwordSignup: authMethods.includes(0) }`, and resolves the call with `null`; every later `start` resolves with the same in-flight result and does nothing else. A failure of either read rejects the call with `errorOf` of it and publishes `phase: 'error'` with that same `WorkerError`. After the reads (not awaited by the call) it runs `acquireLeadership(deps.locks, lockName(hex), onWaiting)` with `onWaiting` publishing `phase: 'other-tab'`, then `boot`. (L-TS-09 worker rules)
8. `acquireLeadership` first requests the lock with `{ ifAvailable: true }`; a granted lock resolves the returned promise and the callback never settles (the lock is held until the worker dies, released by the browser on `pagehide`/termination); a `null` grant calls `onWaiting()` and then requests the same lock with `{}`, whose grant resolves the promise and is likewise held for ever. (L-TS-09; ruling 13; Web Locks facts, `facts-platform.md:181-186`)
9. Phases and the commands each accepts (any other command in that phase → `E_NOT_READY`, detail `the phase is <phase>`; `start` is accepted in every phase): `loading`, `other-tab`, `unsupported`, `revoked`, `error` → none; `store-lost` → `resetDevice`; `needs-signup` → `signupBegin`; `signup-keys` → `signupSubmit`, `signupReset`; `registering` → none; `ready` → `joinCommunity`, `selectCommunity`, `openChannel`, `closeChannel`, `loadEarlier`, `send`, `retrySend`, `discardSend`. (L-TS-09: `E_NOT_READY` is "a command the current phase does not accept")
10. Boot (`deps.boot(instance)` once the lock is held): `unsupported` → `phase: 'unsupported'`, `error: { code: 'E_UNSUPPORTED', detail: reason, status: 0, retryAfterMs: null }`; `store-lost` → `phase: 'store-lost'`; `opened` → keep `core`, build `session = parts.session({ core, routes, now: deps.now })` and `signup = parts.signup({ core, routes, session, now: deps.now })` (`parts` = `{ ...REAL_PARTS, ...deps.parts }`), then by `core.identity().phase`: 0 → `needs-signup`; 1 → `r = await signup.resume()`: `0` → `needs-signup`, `2` → enter ready, `'revoked'` → `enterRevoked()` (nothing is deleted: the controller never calls `signupReset` on this path); 2 → enter ready. A thrown error → `phase: 'error'` with `errorOf` of it, **unless the phase is already `revoked`** (the error is then the consequence of the revocation, for example the 401 that `reauthenticate` turned into `enterRevoked()`, and is dropped). (L-TS-06, L-TS-09)
11. `signupBegin` → `account.recoveryKey = signup.begin(instanceId)` (13 groups of 4), `phase: 'signup-keys'`, `error: null`; resolves `null` after the slice is published. `signupReset` → `core.signupReset()`, `phase: 'needs-signup'`, `recoveryKey: null`. `signupSubmit` (its `recoveryKeyAcknowledged: true` is required by the type), in this order (ruling 34; L-TS-09 "`signupSubmit` and the invite"):
    1. publish `phase: 'registering'`, `error: null`;
    2. when `invite.trim()` is not empty: `inv = await routes.getInvite(invite.trim())`; a `DillaHttpError` with code `E_INVITE_INVALID` → publish `phase: 'signup-keys'` with `error` = its `WorkerError` and reject the call with it (`signup.submit`, the only caller of `postAccount`, is not called); any other failure of this read → `inv = null` (the server stays the authority at registration);
    3. `await signup.submit({ invite, username, display, password })`. A throw while `core.identity().phase` is still 1 → `phase: 'signup-keys'` with `error` = its `WorkerError` (the recovery key stays shown) and the call rejects with the same. A throw after the core reached phase 2 (the account exists; publishing the device list or the KeyPackages failed) → enter ready, which retries `publishDeviceList`; if entering ready throws, `phase: 'error'` with its `WorkerError` and the call rejects with it;
    4. on success → `recoveryKey: null`, enter ready;
    5. once `phase` is `ready`: when `inv?.communityId` is set, run the join path of requirement 14 for it with the same trimmed invite — success → resolve `{ communityId: toHex(inv.communityId), joinError: null }`; a failure → resolve `{ communityId: null, joinError: errorOf(it) }` (never a rejected signup); otherwise resolve `{ communityId: null, joinError: null }`.

    The recovery key crosses to the page only in these slices and only while the phase is `signup-keys` or `registering` (Global Constraints "Never written"; L-TS-08). (L-TS-06 `Signup`; ruling 6)
12. `resetDevice` (phase `store-lost` only): `await deps.resetDevice(instance)`, then boot again exactly as requirement 10; the call resolves `null` after that boot published its phase. (ruling 19; L-TS-09)
13. Enter ready, in this order: `ok = await session.ensure()` — `false` → `enterRevoked()` and stop; `await publishDeviceList(core, routes)`; build `gateway = parts.gateway({ url: origin with http→ws + '/gateway', mintTicket: async () => (await routes.postTicket()).ticket, WebSocket, now, random, setTimeout, clearTimeout })` and subscribe to it; build `sync = parts.sync({ core, routes, gateway, instance, deviceId, now, random, setTimeout, clearTimeout, onGroupChanged, onOutboxChanged, onMembership })`; `sync.start()`; `wasDown = false`; `gateway.start()`; `await refreshCommunities()`; publish `account` `{ phase: 'ready', user: { id: hex(userId), username }, deviceId: hex(deviceId), recoveryKey: null, error: null }` (from `core.identity()`). After every `await` of this sequence, when the phase has become `revoked` meanwhile, enter ready returns without publishing anything further.

    `enterRevoked()` (private; the one `revoked` path, ruling 29, L-TS-09): when the phase is already `revoked` it does nothing; else `sync?.stop()`, `gateway?.stop()`, publish `phase: 'revoked'`. It has three callers: enter ready's `ensure()` answering `false`; the gateway `revoked` event when `establish()` answers `false`; and the HTTP client's `reauthenticate`.

    Gateway events:
    - `status` → the controller keeps `wasDown: boolean` (set `false` before `gateway.start()`). Status `ready` → `connection.status = 'online'` and `wasDown = false`; `waiting` → `'offline'` and `wasDown = true`; `connecting` → `'offline'` when `wasDown`, else `'connecting'`; `idle` → `'offline'`. (The slice store publishes nothing when the value is unchanged, so `waiting` then `connecting` publishes one `offline`.) (L-TS-08 `ConnectionState`; ruling 35)
    - `ready` → `connection.generation = info.generation.toString()`; `void refillKeyPackages(core, routes, info.keypackagesRemaining, { perDevice: limits.keypackagesPerDevice, threshold: limits.keypackageRefillThreshold })` with a rejection ignored; `void refreshCommunities()` with a rejection ignored; and when a community is selected (`selected !== null`), the two reads of requirement 15 for it again (`listChannels`, `listMembers`, republishing both slices and calling `sync.setChannels`), each rejection ignored (the next `ready` retries). (L-TS-09 "On every gateway `ready` the worker refreshes …")
    - `revoked` → `await session.establish()`; `true` → `gateway.start()`; `false` → `enterRevoked()` (it may already have run through `reauthenticate`; it is idempotent).

    The HTTP client is `new HttpClient({ baseUrl: origin, fetch, now, sleep, random, token: () => session?.token() ?? null, reauthenticate: async () => { if (!session) return false; const ok = await session.establish(); if (!ok) enterRevoked(); return ok; }, onGeneration: (g) => publish connection.generation = g.toString() })`, and `routes = parts.routes(http)`. (L-TS-09; L-TS-04; L-GW-02; C5, C19)

    `onMembership(groupId, status)` (`SyncDeps.onMembership`, L-TS-07 rule 7): the controller keeps two sets of group id hex, `resyncing` and `notMember`. `'resyncing'` adds the group to `resyncing` and removes it from `notMember`; `'not-member'` adds it to `notMember` and removes it from `resyncing`; `onGroupChanged(groupId, result)` with `result.state === 2` removes it from both. Each of the three then refreshes, synchronously, the `channels:` row of every known channel bound to that group (its `textGroupId` or its open `groupId` has that hex) and the timeline of every such channel that is open. (L-TS-08 `ChannelGroupState`)
14. `refreshCommunities` → `communities` = `routes.listCommunities()` mapped to `{ id: hex, name }` in the server's order. `joinCommunity(invite)` → `routes.getInvite(trimmed)`; `communityId === null` → `E_INVITE_NOT_COMMUNITY` (detail `''`); else the join path: `routes.joinCommunity(communityId, trimmed)`, `await refreshCommunities()`, resolve `{ communityId: hex }` (the `communities` slice is posted before the `ret`). `signupSubmit` (requirement 11, step 5) runs the same join path with the `communityId` its own `getInvite` read returned. (L-TS-09; L-HTTP-21, -30, -29)
15. `selectCommunity(id)` → `selected = id`; `routes.listChannels(id)` and `routes.listMembers(id)`; keep the channel rows (the controller's map `channel id → { communityId, row }` is replaced for that community); publish `channels:<id>` (each row → `{ id, communityId, kind, mode, name, topic, parentId: hex|null, position, group: channelGroupState(row, core.groups(), membership(channelId)) }`, server order, where `membership(c)` = `{ refusedChannel: refusedChannels.has(c), notMember, resyncing }`) and `members:<id>` (`{ userId, username, display, kind }`); then `sync.setChannels(all known channels with kind 0, mode 0 and textGroupId !== null, as { groupId: textGroupId, communityId, channelId, policyVersion: instance.policyVersion })`; resolve `null`. (L-TS-09; L-HTTP-31, -32; L-CORE-07 "policy_version … is the instance's")
16. `openChannel(id)`: the channel must be in a loaded `channels:` slice → else `E_BAD_INPUT` (`unknown channel`). Mark it open with `limit = TIMELINE_PAGE`. An `unsupported` channel publishes `timeline:<id>` `{ channelId, group: 'unsupported', items: [], hasEarlier: false }` and resolves. Otherwise publish its timeline with the current group state, then `await sync.openChannel({ communityId, channelId, textGroupId })`; on success remember `groupId`, refresh the channel's `channels:` row and its timeline, resolve `null`; a `DillaHttpError` with status 403 adds the channel to the channel-keyed set `refusedChannels`, refreshes both slices (`not-member`) and resolves `null`; any other error rejects (a `SyncError` keeps its own code, requirement 6). `closeChannel` forgets the open channel (its slice stays). `loadEarlier` adds `TIMELINE_PAGE` to its `limit` and refreshes. Refreshing a timeline = `buildTimeline({ channelId, group: channelGroupState(…, membership(channelId)), rows: core.timeline(groupId, 0n, limit), outbox: core.outbox(groupId), ownUser, ownDevice, limit })`, then the member lookup: for each built item whose `senderUser` is not null, is not a `userId` of the loaded `members:<community>` slice, and is not yet in the controller's `lookedUp: Set<string>`, add it to `lookedUp` and run `listMembers(community)` once more (one call per refresh however many such users it found), then publish `members:<community>`; a rejection is ignored. `onGroupChanged(groupId)` and `onOutboxChanged(groupId)` refresh the timeline and the channel row of every open channel with that `groupId`. (L-TS-07 rule 6; L-TS-08; L-TS-09 "a timeline row whose `senderUser` is not in the loaded member list re-runs `listMembers` … once per unknown user"; ruling 18)
17. `send(channelId, text)`: the channel must be open with a group whose state is `active` → else `E_NOT_READY` (`the channel's group is <state>`); `msgId = sync.send(groupId, text)`; refresh the timeline; resolve `{ msgId: hex }`. The controller does not measure `text`: the core enforces the 4000-byte limit in `sendPrepare` and its `CoreError('E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT', …)` is the call's error (L-CORE-09; the composer counts the same bytes first, ruling 39). `retrySend`/`discardSend(msgId)` → `sync.retry`/`sync.discard(fromHex(msgId))`, resolve `null`. (L-TS-07 rule 5; L-TS-09 results)
18. Ordering: every slice a command changes is posted before that command's `ret` (so a page that awaited the call reads the new slice). The controller posts only `ret` and `slice` messages, to its own page only (Global Constraints "Never written").

*Runtime and entry*
19. `startCoreWorker(scope, { testHooks })` builds `ControllerDeps` from the worker scope — `origin: scope.location.origin`, `fetch: scope.fetch.bind(scope)`, `WebSocket: scope.WebSocket`, `locks: { request: (n, o, cb) => scope.navigator.locks.request(n, o, cb) }`, `now: () => Date.now()`, `random: () => Math.random()`, `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` of the scope, `sleep` (a `setTimeout` promise that rejects with the signal's reason when aborted), `post: (m) => scope.postMessage(m)`, `boot`, `resetDevice` — constructs the `Controller` and installs `scope.addEventListener('message', (e) => controller.handle(e.data))`. `boot(instance)`: `const mod = await loadCoreWasm()`; `const root = await scope.navigator.storage.getDirectory()`; `return boot({ instance, probePersistence: () => mod.probe_persistence(), storeExists: (dir) => opfsDirectoryExists(root, dir), kek, openCore: wasmCoreOpener(mod, sleep) })` with `kek = indexedDbKekStore(scope.indexedDB, scope.crypto.subtle, (a) => scope.crypto.getRandomValues(a))`. `resetDevice(instance)`: `kek.remove(hex)`, then `(await root.getDirectoryHandle('dilla')).removeEntry(hex, { recursive: true })`, a `NotFoundError` `DOMException` from either OPFS call being success. `loadCoreWasm()` imports `@dilla/core-wasm` dynamically once, casts it through `unknown` to `CoreWasmModule & { default(): Promise<unknown> }` (no static import of the generated types: L-TS-03 keeps them out of lint), and awaits `default()` once; with no argument wasm-bindgen's init loads `new URL('dilla_core_wasm_bg.wasm', import.meta.url)`, which Vite emits as one hashed asset. (C5, C7; L-TS-05; ruling 14)
20. `src/worker/entry.ts` is `startCoreWorker(self as unknown as DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope, { testHooks: false })` and nothing else; `harness/worker.ts` is the same with `{ testHooks: true }`. The production bundle therefore never honours a test hook (requirement 5).

*Harness and serving*
21. The harness page has no inline script or style (CSP `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'`, L-HTTP-10): `index.html` loads `./main.ts` as a module, Vite emits it as a file. `vite.config.ts`: `root` the harness directory, `base: '/'`, `build.outDir` `../harness-dist`, `emptyOutDir: true`, `target: 'es2022'`, `assetsInlineLimit: 0`, `modulePreload: { polyfill: false }`, `worker: { format: 'es' }`. The build output's file extensions are all in L-HTTP-10's content-type table (`web.New` refuses any other). (C9; L-HTTP-10, -11)
22. `scripts/write-manifest.mjs` writes `<dir>/dilla-manifest.json` = `JSON.stringify(buildManifest(dir)) + '\n'`; refuses (exit 1, writing nothing) when `dir` does not exist (`<dir>: no such directory`) or has no `index.html` (`<dir>: index.html is missing`); without an argument prints `usage: write-manifest.mjs <dist-dir>` and exits 2; walks directories recursively and ignores entries that are neither files nor directories; excludes only the top-level `dilla-manifest.json`. Task 22's script imports `buildManifest` and `MANIFEST_NAME` from this file (ruling 37), so there is one implementation of these semantics and the two cannot disagree on a manifest. (L-HTTP-11)
23. The core config serves `packages/client-core/harness-dist` from this task on (`webRoot: 'packages/client-core/harness-dist'`); the root-page test of `support.spec.ts` asserts the harness page instead of the placeholder, and a new test asserts the wasm asset's headers against the manifest. (L-E2E-03)

*The integration proof*
24. `e2e/web/core-worker.spec.ts` runs in `chromium-core` and `firefox-core`, on a persistent profile, against the production-ACL test host and a native `web-driver` peer, and proves in one test: signup through the bridge with an instance invite (`needs-signup` → `signup-keys` with 13 Crockford groups of 4 → `ready`, the key gone, `signupSubmit` resolving `{ communityId: null, joinError: null }` because an instance invite names no community); joining the peer's community with its invite; the community's channel and both members; opening the channel by external join (`active`, and the peer's roster gains this device); receiving the peer's message with the peer's user and device, `web: false`, `own: false`; sending, the pending row turning into a stored own row under the same key `o<msgId>` (one item for that message throughout), and the peer decrypting it with this device's user, device and `tier` 1; a message sent while the gateway was stopped appearing after it restarts (catch-up on `ready`, C12/C19); a reload reaching `ready` without signup, with the same user, device and stored timeline, and messages still flowing both ways (the session re-established from the stored device key); a second page of the same origin showing `other-tab` while the first stays `ready`; and no `pageerror` on either page. Every wait is a state wait of 90 000 ms on CI, 30 000 ms locally; the test's own timeout is 900 000 ms on CI, 300 000 ms locally. (task index; C5, C12, C18, C19, C22; lesson c)
25. Unit tests never load the wasm and never touch IndexedDB, OPFS or Web Locks: they run on the injected `ControllerDeps` (with `parts` doubles for `Routes`, `Session`, `Signup`, `Gateway` and `SyncEngine` where a test reaches the `ready` phase), a fake `Worker` and partial `CorePort` stubs (Global Constraints "Testing"; ruling 15).
26. Mutations (lesson a), each shown red once and reverted (Step 9): (a) the Web Lock requested without `ifAvailable` handling → the second-page assertion and the controller's other-tab test go red; (b) the catch-up on `ready` dropped in `src/sync/engine.ts` → the missed message never appears after the forced gateway reconnect; (c) the gateway status `waiting` mapped to `connecting` → the controller test "`ready → waiting → connecting → ready` publishes `online, offline, offline, online`" goes red; (d) the bridge accepting every `slice` whatever its `rev` → "keeps the newest revision …" goes red. (task index, task 18 mutations (a)-(c); (d) is this task's own)

Create `packages/client-core/src/state/store.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { SliceStore } from './store';
import type { AccountState, CommunitySummary, SliceName } from './types';

function account(phase: AccountState['phase']): AccountState {
  return { phase, instance: null, user: null, deviceId: null, recoveryKey: null, error: null };
}

function recording() {
  const posted: { name: SliceName; rev: number; value: unknown }[] = [];
  const store = new SliceStore((name, rev, value) => posted.push({ name, rev, value }));
  return { store, posted };
}

describe('SliceStore', () => {
  it('publishes every change with a revision per slice name that starts at 1', () => {
    const { store, posted } = recording();
    store.set('account', account('loading'));
    store.set('account', account('needs-signup'));
    store.set('communities', []);
    expect(posted.map((p) => [p.name, p.rev])).toEqual([['account', 1], ['account', 2], ['communities', 1]]);
    expect(posted[1]?.value).toEqual(account('needs-signup'));
    expect(store.rev('account')).toBe(2);
    expect(store.rev(`timeline:${'a'.repeat(32)}`)).toBe(0);
    expect(store.get('account')?.phase).toBe('needs-signup');
  });

  it('does not publish a value equal to the one it holds', () => {
    const { store, posted } = recording();
    store.set('connection', { status: 'offline', generation: null });
    store.set('connection', { status: 'offline', generation: null });
    expect(posted).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(store.rev('connection')).toBe(1);
  });

  it('stores a deep-frozen copy, so neither the caller nor a reader can change what was published', () => {
    const { store } = recording();
    const list: CommunitySummary[] = [{ id: 'a'.repeat(32), name: 'one' }];
    store.set('communities', list);
    list[0]!.name = 'changed';
    list.push({ id: 'b'.repeat(32), name: 'two' });
    const held = store.get('communities')!;
    expect(held).toEqual([{ id: 'a'.repeat(32), name: 'one' }]);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(held)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(held[0])).toBe(true);
    expect(() => (held as CommunitySummary[]).push({ id: 'c'.repeat(32), name: 'three' })).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  it('returns the same object until the slice changes', () => {
    const { store } = recording();
    store.set('communities', []);
    const first = store.get('communities');
    store.set('communities', []);
    expect(store.get('communities')).toBe(first);
    store.set('communities', [{ id: 'a'.repeat(32), name: 'x' }]);
    expect(store.get('communities')).not.toBe(first);
  });
});
```

Create `packages/client-core/src/state/derive.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { GroupInfo, OutboxRow, TimelineRow } from '../core-port';
import { buildTimeline, channelGroupState, type GroupMembership } from './derive';

const id = (b: number): Uint8Array => new Uint8Array(16).fill(b);
const hex = (b: number): string => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0').repeat(16);
const OWN_USER = 0x0a;
const OWN_DEVICE = 0x0b;
const PEER_USER = 0x1a;
const PEER_DEVICE = 0x1b;

function row(seq: number, over: Partial<TimelineRow> = {}): TimelineRow {
  return {
    seq: BigInt(seq), epoch: 1n, recvTs: 1_700_000_000n + BigInt(seq), status: 0, reason: '',
    senderUser: id(PEER_USER), senderDevice: id(PEER_DEVICE), senderKind: 0, senderTier: 0,
    msgId: id(0x30 + seq), type: 0, body: `body ${seq}`, ...over,
  };
}

function outbox(m: number, state: 0 | 1 | 2, over: Partial<OutboxRow> = {}): OutboxRow {
  return { msgId: id(m), state, error: '', created: 1_700_000_100n, body: `draft ${m}`, ...over };
}

function timeline(rows: TimelineRow[], out: OutboxRow[] = [], limit = 100) {
  return buildTimeline({
    channelId: 'c'.repeat(32), group: 'active', rows, outbox: out,
    ownUser: id(OWN_USER), ownDevice: id(OWN_DEVICE), limit,
  });
}

describe('buildTimeline', () => {
  it("maps a peer's readable row with its authenticated sender", () => {
    expect(timeline([row(1)])).toEqual({
      channelId: 'c'.repeat(32), group: 'active', hasEarlier: false,
      items: [{
        key: 's1', state: 'ok', reason: '', senderUser: hex(PEER_USER), senderDevice: hex(PEER_DEVICE),
        own: false, web: false, bot: false, ts: 1_700_000_001, body: 'body 1', msgId: hex(0x31),
      }],
    });
  });

  it("marks this device's rows as own and a browser-tier sender as web", () => {
    const [item] = timeline([row(2, { senderUser: id(OWN_USER), senderDevice: id(OWN_DEVICE), senderTier: 1 })]).items;
    expect(item).toMatchObject({ key: `o${hex(0x32)}`, own: true, web: true, bot: false });
  });

  it('a sent message keeps its key when it is confirmed', () => {
    const m = 0x45;
    const pending = timeline([], [outbox(m, 1)]).items;
    const stored = timeline([row(12, { msgId: id(m), senderUser: id(OWN_USER), senderDevice: id(OWN_DEVICE), senderTier: 1 })]).items;
    expect(pending.map((i) => [i.key, i.state])).toEqual([[`o${hex(m)}`, 'pending']]);
    expect(stored.map((i) => [i.key, i.state])).toEqual([[`o${hex(m)}`, 'ok']]);
    // An own row whose message id is unknown, and a peer's row, keep the seq key.
    expect(timeline([row(13, { msgId: null, senderDevice: id(OWN_DEVICE) })]).items[0]?.key).toBe('s13');
    expect(timeline([row(14, { msgId: id(m) })]).items[0]?.key).toBe('s14');
  });

  it('marks a bot sender', () => {
    const [item] = timeline([row(3, { senderKind: 1 })]).items;
    expect(item).toMatchObject({ key: 's3', bot: true, web: false, own: false });
  });

  it('shows an unreadable row with its raw reason and never a body', () => {
    const [item] = timeline([row(4, {
      status: 1, reason: 'E_SENDER_MISMATCH', senderUser: null, senderKind: null, senderTier: null,
      msgId: null, type: null, body: 'must not show',
    })]).items;
    expect(item).toEqual({
      key: 's4', state: 'cannot-read', reason: 'E_SENDER_MISMATCH', senderUser: null, senderDevice: hex(PEER_DEVICE),
      own: false, web: false, bot: false, ts: 1_700_000_004, body: '', msgId: null,
    });
  });

  it('shows a deleted row without its body', () => {
    const [item] = timeline([row(5, { status: 2, body: 'gone' })]).items;
    expect(item).toMatchObject({ key: 's5', state: 'deleted', reason: '', body: '' });
  });

  it('leaves out stored rows of envelope types other than 0', () => {
    expect(timeline([row(6, { type: 3 }), row(7)]).items.map((i) => i.key)).toEqual(['s7']);
  });

  it('appends the outbox after the stored rows: queued and in flight are pending, failed carries its error', () => {
    const items = timeline([row(8)], [outbox(0x41, 0), outbox(0x42, 1), outbox(0x43, 2, { error: 'E_TOO_LARGE' })]).items;
    expect(items.map((i) => [i.key, i.state, i.reason])).toEqual([
      ['s8', 'ok', ''],
      [`o${hex(0x41)}`, 'pending', ''],
      [`o${hex(0x42)}`, 'pending', ''],
      [`o${hex(0x43)}`, 'failed', 'E_TOO_LARGE'],
    ]);
    expect(items[1]).toEqual({
      key: `o${hex(0x41)}`, state: 'pending', reason: '', senderUser: hex(OWN_USER), senderDevice: hex(OWN_DEVICE),
      own: true, web: true, bot: false, ts: 1_700_000_100, body: 'draft 65', msgId: hex(0x41),
    });
  });

  it('drops an outbox row whose message is already stored', () => {
    const stored = row(9, { msgId: id(0x44), senderUser: id(OWN_USER), senderDevice: id(OWN_DEVICE), senderTier: 1 });
    expect(timeline([stored], [outbox(0x44, 1)]).items.map((i) => [i.key, i.state])).toEqual([[`o${hex(0x44)}`, 'ok']]);
  });

  it('keeps the outbox key of an own upload deleted before it was confirmed', () => {
    const marker = row(10, { status: 2, body: '', msgId: id(0x45), senderUser: id(OWN_USER), senderDevice: id(OWN_DEVICE), senderTier: 1 });
    expect(timeline([marker], []).items.map((i) => [i.key, i.state, i.own, i.body])).toEqual([[`o${hex(0x45)}`, 'deleted', true, '']]);
  });

  it('reports earlier rows when the core filled the page, counting rows it did not show', () => {
    expect(timeline([row(10), row(11)], [], 2).hasEarlier).toBe(true);
    expect(timeline([row(10, { type: 4 }), row(11)], [], 2).hasEarlier).toBe(true);
    expect(timeline([row(10)], [], 2).hasEarlier).toBe(false);
  });
});

function group(target: number, state: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4, kind = 0): GroupInfo {
  return {
    groupId: id(0x60 + state + kind * 8), kind, communityId: id(0x70), targetId: id(target), state,
    epoch: 1n, nextSeq: 1n, proposalsPending: 0, pendingCommit: false,
  };
}
const channel = (over: Partial<{ kind: number; mode: number }> = {}) => ({ id: id(0x50), kind: 0, mode: 0, ...over });
const known = (over: { refusedChannel?: boolean; notMember?: string[]; resyncing?: string[] } = {}): GroupMembership => ({
  refusedChannel: over.refusedChannel ?? false, notMember: new Set(over.notMember ?? []), resyncing: new Set(over.resyncing ?? []),
});
const NONE = known();
const REFUSED = known({ refusedChannel: true });

describe('channelGroupState', () => {
  it('calls a voice channel, a category and a readable channel unsupported', () => {
    expect(channelGroupState(channel({ kind: 1 }), [group(0x50, 2)], NONE)).toBe('unsupported');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel({ kind: 2 }), [], NONE)).toBe('unsupported');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel({ mode: 1 }), [group(0x50, 2)], NONE)).toBe('unsupported');
  });

  it('maps the local text group state', () => {
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [], NONE)).toBe('none');
    const cases = [[0, 'joining'], [1, 'joining'], [2, 'active'], [3, 'resync'], [4, 'not-member']] as const;
    for (const [state, want] of cases) expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, state)], NONE)).toBe(want);
  });

  it("ignores another channel's group and a call group of this channel", () => {
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x51, 2), group(0x50, 2, 1)], NONE)).toBe('none');
  });

  it('prefers a live group over a gone one', () => {
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 4), group(0x50, 2)], NONE)).toBe('active');
  });

  it('reports not-member after a refused open unless a group is joining or active', () => {
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [], REFUSED)).toBe('not-member');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 3)], REFUSED)).toBe('not-member');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 1)], REFUSED)).toBe('joining');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 2)], REFUSED)).toBe('active');
  });

  it("follows what onMembership reported for the channel's own group", () => {
    // group(0x50, s) has the id id(0x60 + s), so its hex is hex(0x60 + s).
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 2)], known({ resyncing: [hex(0x62)] }))).toBe('resync');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 3)], known({ resyncing: [hex(0x63)] }))).toBe('resync');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 3)], known({ notMember: [hex(0x63)] }))).toBe('not-member');
    // Another group's report changes nothing.
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 3)], known({ notMember: [hex(0x62)] }))).toBe('resync');
    expect(channelGroupState(channel(), [group(0x50, 2)], known({ resyncing: [hex(0x63)] }))).toBe('active');
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { CoreCallError, connectCore } from './bridge';
import type { AccountState } from './state/types';

class FakeWorker {
  readonly posted: unknown[] = [];
  terminated = false;
  private readonly listeners: ((e: MessageEvent) => void)[] = [];
  postMessage(message: unknown): void { this.posted.push(message); }
  terminate(): void { this.terminated = true; }
  addEventListener(type: string, listener: (e: MessageEvent) => void): void {
    if (type === 'message') this.listeners.push(listener);
  }
  removeEventListener(): void {}
  emit(data: unknown): void { for (const l of this.listeners) l({ data } as MessageEvent); }
}

function account(phase: AccountState['phase']): AccountState {
  return { phase, instance: null, user: null, deviceId: null, recoveryKey: null, error: null };
}

function connected() {
  const worker = new FakeWorker();
  return { worker, client: connectCore(worker as unknown as Worker) };
}

describe('connectCore', () => {
  it("posts each call with a fresh id and resolves it with the worker's value", async () => {
    const { worker, client } = connected();
    const first = client.call({ m: 'joinCommunity', invite: 'code' });
    const second = client.call({ m: 'selectCommunity', communityId: 'a'.repeat(32) });
    expect(worker.posted).toEqual([
      { t: 'call', id: 1, command: { m: 'joinCommunity', invite: 'code' } },
      { t: 'call', id: 2, command: { m: 'selectCommunity', communityId: 'a'.repeat(32) } },
    ]);
    worker.emit({ t: 'ret', id: 2, ok: true, value: null });
    worker.emit({ t: 'ret', id: 1, ok: true, value: { communityId: 'b'.repeat(32) } });
    await expect(first).resolves.toEqual({ communityId: 'b'.repeat(32) });
    await expect(second).resolves.toBeNull();
  });

  it("rejects with the worker's error: code, detail, status and wait", async () => {
    const { worker, client } = connected();
    const pending = client.call({ m: 'send', channelId: 'a'.repeat(32), text: 'x' });
    const later = client.call({ m: 'joinCommunity', invite: 'code' });
    worker.emit({ t: 'ret', id: 1, ok: false, error: { code: 'E_NOT_READY', detail: 'the phase is needs-signup', status: 0, retryAfterMs: null } });
    worker.emit({ t: 'ret', id: 2, ok: false, error: { code: 'E_RATE_LIMITED', detail: '', status: 429, retryAfterMs: 4200 } });
    const error: unknown = await pending.catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(CoreCallError);
    expect(error).toMatchObject({
      name: 'CoreCallError', code: 'E_NOT_READY', detail: 'the phase is needs-signup', status: 0, retryAfterMs: null,
      message: 'E_NOT_READY: the phase is needs-signup',
    });
    const limited: unknown = await later.catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect(limited).toMatchObject({ code: 'E_RATE_LIMITED', detail: '', status: 429, retryAfterMs: 4200, message: 'E_RATE_LIMITED' });
    expect(new CoreCallError({ code: 'E_X', detail: 'd', status: 409, retryAfterMs: null })).toMatchObject({ code: 'E_X', detail: 'd', status: 409, message: 'E_X: d' });
  });

  it('ignores an answer to an id it never sent and a message of no known kind', () => {
    const { worker, client } = connected();
    expect(() => worker.emit({ t: 'ret', id: 99, ok: true, value: 1 })).not.toThrow();
    expect(() => worker.emit({ t: 'nonsense' })).not.toThrow();
    expect(client.get('account')).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('keeps the newest revision of each slice and notifies its listeners once per accepted revision', () => {
    const { worker, client } = connected();
    let calls = 0;
    const off = client.subscribe('account', () => { calls += 1; });
    worker.emit({ t: 'slice', name: 'account', rev: 1, value: account('loading') });
    const held = client.get('account');
    expect(held?.phase).toBe('loading');
    expect(client.get('account')).toBe(held);
    worker.emit({ t: 'slice', name: 'account', rev: 3, value: account('ready') });
    worker.emit({ t: 'slice', name: 'account', rev: 2, value: account('other-tab') });
    worker.emit({ t: 'slice', name: 'account', rev: 3, value: account('error') });
    expect(client.get('account')?.phase).toBe('ready');
    expect(calls).toBe(2);
    off();
    worker.emit({ t: 'slice', name: 'account', rev: 4, value: account('revoked') });
    expect(calls).toBe(2);
    expect(client.get('account')?.phase).toBe('revoked');
    expect(client.get('communities')).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('dispose terminates the worker and rejects pending and later calls with E_DISPOSED', async () => {
    const { worker, client } = connected();
    const pending = client.call({ m: 'start' });
    client.dispose();
    expect(worker.terminated).toBe(true);
    await expect(pending).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'E_DISPOSED', detail: '', status: 0, retryAfterMs: null });
    await expect(client.call({ m: 'start' })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'E_DISPOSED', detail: '', status: 0, retryAfterMs: null });
    expect(worker.posted).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```
